Therefore, my spirit has awakened me to explain some hints in the arrangement of prayer and the order of their matters, as our sages, the holy ones on high, the sages of truth, peace be upon them, established them. However, the prayers that the sages of truth established did not depart from the ways of Scripture, for from Scripture they took all the hint and arranged all that their mind required of praise, thanksgiving, confession, request, and supplication. And it is necessary, when the one who prays comes to pray, to bow down to God, face to the ground, as it says, "Let us come to His dwelling place; let us worship at His footstool" (Ps 132:7), and it says, "Come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the Lord our Maker" (Ps 95:6), and when he kneels and bows down, he begins to pray. And they established that the cantor should begin to praise God with a language of blessing, saying, "I will bless the Lord" (Ps 34:2), and they established to begin this psalm for reasons, because this psalm was established by David, peace be upon him, outside the Land [of Israel], and therefore, because we are in exile outside the Land, they established this, and also because it begins with a language of blessing, and the language of blessing means praise, to praise and glorify Him with the utmost perfection, and it includes all types of perfections by which He is distinguished from all created beings, that He is an eternal existence without beginning or end, far from physicality and from what applies to physicality, and that He is uniquely unified, a true unity without combination or composition, without partner with Him, may He be exalted, from all deficiency - all these are included in the language of blessing. Therefore, he begins with the language of blessing and completes, "at all times His praise shall be in my mouth" (Ps 34:2). And this psalm is honored and excellent in its awakening of reasons by which a person is obligated to praise and glorify God, to serve Him with a complete heart because his life and preservation depend on the hands of God at all times, in every hour, and in every moment, to provide for him and to keep him alive. And because there is in it the hope of reward and the fear of punishment, such as it says, "The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears to their cry" (Ps 34:16), and it says, "The face of the Lord is against evildoers, to cut off their memory from the earth" (Ps 34:17), and it completes to the hope of a final reward, "The Lord redeems the soul of His servants" (Ps 34:23), and it concludes with "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen" (Ps 89:53). And already we have included His praises, may He be exalted, in the word "blessing," which are taken from the consideration of the intellect from the side of His works, which are the world in its entirety. And the world is only called "world" because it is renewed, for the language of "world" is a language of renewal, from the verb "youth," and since it is renewed, it needs a renewer and an actor who brings it into existence and maintains it - He is God, may He be exalted, who is distinguished from it in His perfection, may He be exalted, in all types of perfections. Therefore, he said, "Amen and Amen," meaning, Amen to what is obligated in His perfection, may He be exalted, and Amen to what is obligated to the world, which needs Him because it is renewed from Him. And afterward, they stand and pray, as it says, "And to stand every morning to thank and praise the Lord, and likewise at evening" (1Chr 23:30). And they pray a prayer that those who ascended from Babylon, the good figs, prayed, as it says, "And Jeshua and Bani, Kadmiel arose on the platform of the Levites" (Neh 9:4), and it is written, "And they cried out with a loud voice" "Arise, bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting" (Neh 9:5), with the verse, "You alone are the Lord" (Neh 9:6). And the redactors, may God have mercy on them, chose to place these verses at the beginning of the prayer of unity and its conclusion, for they indicate the truth of the unity of God, may He be exalted, for in the statement, "Arise, bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting," there is a hint to the existence of the Renewer from the side of the world being renewed. Therefore, he said, "And let them bless Your glorious name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise" (Neh 9:5), for He is exalted and superior in all types of perfections, for so is fitting in consideration of Him, may He be exalted. And the arranger connected verses agreeing with the matter of the verse, saying, "Lift up your hands in holiness" (Ps 134:2), "Bless the Lord, O peoples" (Ps 66:8), "In assemblies, bless God" (Ps 68:27), "In the Lord shall they be justified and glory" (Isa 45:25), "You who fear the Lord, praise Him" (Ps 22:24). And these verses indicate that "In the multitude of people is the king's glory" (Prov 14:28), and in the selection of the nation of Israel, and gives the reason that even though He is high above all heights and is lifted up above all who are lifted up, He hears the prayer of the lowliest of the lowly, as it says, "For He has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted" (Ps 22:25), and because He hears the prayer of all who pray, therefore all are obligated to pray to Him, may He be exalted, as it says, "O You who hear prayer, to You all flesh shall come" (Ps 65:3), "For the Lord hears the needy" (Ps 69:34), "Hear, O Lord, my voice when I call" (Ps 27:7), "Hear, O Lord, and be gracious to me" (Ps 30:11). And because the second verse is "You alone are the Lord" (Neh 9:6), which indicates His unity, may He be exalted, and that all that exists, He brought into existence, therefore he connects verses similar to its matter. And the thoughts of the arranger, through goodness, they have been instructed, and the knowledge of his lips, they have clearly spoken, and therefore he presented this prayer at the beginning to establish the unity, because you know the opinion of the Rabbanites in what they established in the secret of their prayers and praises, that they pray, believing in two powers, saying that because the cause is near and far, and this is the secret of Metatron, whom they call "the lesser Lord," who leads the lower world, which is called the active intellect, which gives forms to all the existents below in the lower world, which is the world of generation and corruption, and about him they explain verses that are said, such as "I will exalt You, my God, the King" (Ps 145:1), "Blessed be the Lord, my rock, who trains my hands for war" (Ps 144:1), "He is your praise and He is your God" (Deut 10:21), "And I will magnify myself and sanctify myself" (Ezek 38:23), which the Torah did not intend with all this intention, but stood against it and unified a true unity. But we who believe in a true unity, the unity of God, may He be exalted, that the will of the Torah revolves around this, to establish the unity and to nullify the duality, as we have awakened in the verse, "For the Lord your God, He is the God of gods" (Deut 10:17), that the intention in it is the God of the angels and the Lord of the spheres, not that His intention is on the idols and graven images, for this is not praise that He would be praised that He is the lord of wood and stones. And how many times did He repeat that there is none besides Him (Deut 4:35) to indicate a true unity. And after all these statements, is it possible to believe in a duality to God, may He be exalted, and that prayer should turn to something other than Him, may He be exalted? God forbid to Him, to the point that a commandment has come in the Torah to believe in the unity, saying, "Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is one" (Deut 6:4). For God's accounts are divided - there are some that it is impossible to rely on them in the statement of the prophet, such as the existence of God, may He be blessed, through an account of ability and knowledge, because the knowledge of the existence of God, may He be blessed, necessarily precedes the belief in the prophet, but concerning the belief in His unity, may He be exalted, there is no necessity for any knowledge of His unity, may He be exalted, to precede the belief in the prophet. Therefore, even though the necessity of investigation indicates, just as we know His existence, may He be exalted, by way of the intellect, so by the necessity of the proof we know His unity by way of the intellect. Further, the one who is negligent, who does not know it by way of the intellect, can rely on the statement of the prophet, which is not the case with the knowledge of His existence, for the knowledge of His existence is necessitated before the belief in the prophet, but not so the knowledge of His unity. Therefore, the commandment of unity came in the Torah in the statement, "Hear, O Israel," etc. And from this reason, which I have prefaced, from the knowledge of the Rabbanites from the secret of their prayers and praises, therefore the arranger established first the root of unity by way of the Torah, which includes one who is foolish and one who investigates, and afterward by way of the intellect, as will be explained. Therefore, he opened with the statement, "Hear, O Israel," and therefore he connected to it, "Believe in the Lord your God so shall you be established; believe His prophets, so shall you prosper" (2Chr 20:20), for this statement is by way of a commandment of the Torah, since the matter of prayer is obligated from the knowledge and from the hearing. Therefore, it says, "The Lord our God, the Lord is one," that the first Name indicates that He alone is necessary of existence, and the second, that He brought all existence into being, not like the opinion of those who preceded, who say that the creator of the beginning is the near cause, and therefore next to it, "O Lord, Your name is everlasting; O Lord, Your remembrance is throughout all generations" (Ps 135:13), which is said in the Torah, "This is My name forever, and this is My memorial unto all generations" (Exod 3:15), saying, "This is My name forever," shows that from the side of the renewal of the world, investigation requires that He is necessarily existent of Himself, and saying, "and this is My memorial unto all generations," shows that He is the one who brings all existence into being and sustains the lower world by way of generation and corruption, and therefore next to it, he wanted to arrange the three parts of existence, which are the world of generation and corruption, the world of the spheres, and the world of the angels, as he says, "The Lord by wisdom founded the earth" (Prov 3:19), "O Lord, Your kindness is in the heavens" (Ps 36:6), and he brings verses, all of which begin with the unique Name, to indicate that they all exist from Him, may He be exalted. And afterward, "The Lord has established His throne in the heavens" (Ps 103:19), hinting that the throne is with servants. And he said, "O Lord, our Lord, how glorious is Your name in all the earth, who has set Your glory above the heavens" (Ps 8:2), the hint that above and below there is none like Him. And if there is mourning, he hints at the day of death and the day of resurrection, as it is "the end of all man" (Eccl 7:2), that they depend on His hands, as it says, "The Lord kills and gives life" (1Sam 2:6), "O Lord, You have brought up my soul from the grave" (Ps 30:4), and he said that in all that exists, there is none like Him, as it says, "O Lord, who is like You" (Ps 35:10), "There is none like You, O Lord" (Jer 10:6), "Who would not fear You, O king of nations? For to You it is fitting" (Jer 10:7). And because he wanted to hint at the existence of the angels, who are on high, he said, "And Your righteousness, O God, to the heights, You who have done great things" (Ps 71:19), and he said, "Who is like You among the gods, O Lord, who is like You, glorious in holiness" (Exod 15:11), showing in this that the angels acknowledge to God, "who is like You." And if so, the intention in all this arrangement from the words of the prophets is that God, may He be exalted, is separated from the three parts of existence, and He is the one who brings them into existence and sustains them, and he included in this the highest kind of the angels, and how can the mind bear that a kind below them should be worshipped? God forbid to us from this. Therefore, the arranger came and did wonders in his arrangement to nullify that thought, to believe in a true unity, without partner with Him, may He be exalted. And when he arranged the actions of God, may He be exalted, including that He brings the evening and forms light, and these are the times of prayer, therefore he began to give praise to God, may He be exalted, saying, "O Lord my God, You are; I will exalt You, I will praise Your name, for You have done wonders" (Isa 25:1), for these are from the wonders of God, may He be exalted, and His deeds. And he said, "You make darkness, and it is night" (Ps 104:20), "He counts the number [of the stars]" (Ps 147:4), "The day is Yours, the night also is Yours; You have prepared the light and the sun" (Ps 74:16), for through them He illuminates and darkens. And he concludes, "For You are great, and do wondrous things; You alone are God" (Ps 86:10). And he indicated that He alone, may He be exalted, leads this existence. And he said the true unity by way of the proof of the intellect, "You alone are the Lord; You have made the heavens, the highest heavens, and all their host, the earth and all that is on it, the seas and all that is in them" (Neh 9:6), and he attributed all actions to the power of God, may He be exalted, saying, "And You preserve them all" (Neh 9:6). And because apparently there are actions dependent on the hands of intermediaries, he said that they are like an axe in the hand of the one who hews, and therefore he said, "And the host of heaven bows down to You" (Neh 9:6). Next to this, they say, "We also will serve the Lord" (Josh 24:18), that is to say, just as the host of heaven serves, so we will serve the Lord our God. And the reason for the service is to thank God, may He be exalted, that all that He brought into existence, He brought into existence in His kindness and it depends on His power. Therefore, after that, he arranged "who is abundantly kind," which is the psalm, "O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His kindness is eternal" (Ps 136:1), which is a true thanksgiving that all that He brought into existence, He brought into existence in complete kindness, and He sustains it, and the reason for mentioning this psalm is to give thanks to God, may He be exalted, for all that He brought into existence, and also to mention the exodus from Egypt, which Scripture obligated to remember all the days of our lives, as it says, "That you may remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt all the days of your life" (Deut 16:3), and that the exodus from Egypt is like the creation of the world. Therefore, he connected it with the creation of the world. And because it recounts practical things in the exodus from Egypt, and that it indicates a true providence in a perceptible proof in His choosing the nation of Israel, and it concludes with "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen" (Ps 89:53). And after he concluded from the matter of general praise and general thanks, he began with the creation of the day, which is the deed of every day, to indicate the true providence that confirms prophecy, through which is the obligation of the sacrifice, and he mentions a psalm that indicates God's choice of Israel and the obligation of His service upon them, which is the service of God through the sacrifice, and he says, "A psalm for thanksgiving. Shout joyfully to the Lord, all the earth. (Ps 100:1) Serve the Lord with joy" (Ps 100:2), and he says all the psalm, and begins, "The beginning of Your word is truth" (Ps 119:160), which indicates the truth of the Torah, and he arranges the matter of the sacrifice, "And the Lord spoke to Moses saying, Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, My food" (Num 28:2), which is the sacrifice and the burning of incense and the lighting of the lamps, which are the services of the Temple. And he mentions, "And to stand every morning to thank and praise the Lord, and likewise at evening" (1Chr 23:30). And he says a psalm of the place of the song, which they would sing at the time of offering the sacrifice, and he begins the psalm, "A praise of David: I will exalt You, my God, the King" (Ps 145:1), until the end of the book, six psalms arranged for the six days of the act of creation, on each and every day one psalm, and he concludes, "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen." And afterward, he falls on his face and confesses, like the matter of "And he fell on his face" (2Sam 9:6), and says by way of lamentation, "And now, what shall we say, our God" (Ezra 9:10), because the Temple has been destroyed and the service has ceased. And he says, "The joy of our heart has ceased" (Lam 5:15), "For this our heart is faint" (Lam 5:17), "For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate" (Lam 5:18), and he says, "If I forget you, O Jerusalem" (Ps 137:5), and he asks for forgiveness and pardon and atonement for his sins and the destruction of the Temple, and concludes, "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen." And after that, he says the psalm, "Lord, I have called You; hasten to me" (Ps 141:1), which awakens that our lips' expression concerning the sacrifice will be in place of its offering, such as, "Let my prayer be set forth as incense before You; the lifting of my hands as the evening sacrifice" (Ps 141:2), and he says verses that indicate that a humble spirit is the place of the sacrifice, such as it says, "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise" (Ps 51:19). And he asks, "Do good in Your will to Zion; build the walls of Jerusalem. (Ps 51:20) Then You will delight in sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt-offering and whole burnt-offering; then bulls will be offered" (Ps 51:21), to restore the captivity of Jerusalem and to build the Temple, to return the service to its place, and concludes, "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen." And afterward, he stands and begins a psalm concerning the redemption, which is the psalm, "Ascribe to the Lord, O sons of the mighty; ascribe to the Lord glory and strength" (Ps 29:1), which explains the building of the Temple and the coming of the glory, and concludes, "The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace" (Ps 29:11). And because at the time of the redemption, they will sing to God a new song, as it says, "In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah" (Isa 26:1), they say a psalm of what is fitting according to the will of the one who prays, whether for praise, or for request, or for joy, or for the opposite, and concludes "Blessed be the Lord." And afterward, he says the psalm, "A prayer of Moses" (Ps 90:1), which this psalm includes how God chose Israel and that He is a dwelling place for them, and how He awakens them to the matter of repentance, as it says, "And You said, Return, O children of men" (Ps 90:3), and he mentioned what befell them from the matter of exile, as it says, "For we are consumed by Your anger" (Ps 90:7), "For all our days have passed away in Your wrath" (Ps 90:9), and he asks from God forgiveness to repent from the evil that He brought upon them, to redeem them, and it is the time of the end of the salvation, as it says, "Let Your work appear to Your servants" (Ps 90:16), and he says, "And let the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us" (Ps 90:17), and concludes, "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen." And afterward, he brings verses that indicate the matter of request, such as, "Do not disgrace, for Your name's sake, do not dishonor the throne of Your glory" (Jer 14:21), "Remember, O Lord, what has come upon us" (Lam 5:1), and similar to these, and hints that we are Your handiwork and You are our redeemer, and You should have mercy on us, as it says, "For You are our Father" (Isa 63:16), and behold, "As clay in the hand of the potter" (Jer 18:6), so are we in Your hand. And if there is mourning, he connects, "Remember now that You have made me as clay" (Job 10:9), "Remember that my life is a breath" (Job 7:7), for the reason of generation and corruption, which depend according to His will, may He be exalted. And he mentions from the matter of exile and the destruction of the Temple and the breaking of Zion and Jerusalem, as he says, "The cities of Your holiness have become a wilderness" (Isa 64:9), "Our holy and beautiful house" (Isa 64:10). And he asks that He bring out His people from exile for the sake of the jealousy for His people and the profanation of His name and the profanation of His Torah and the profanation of the Temple, and he says, "Will You restrain Yourself for these things, O Lord?" (Isa 64:11), and concludes with the request for forgiveness and pardon, as he says, "Turn from Your fierce anger" (Exod 32:12), "Return for the sake of Your servants" (Isa 63:17), "Return us to You, O Lord" (Lam 5:21), "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen" (Ps 89:53). And behold, after he finished the offering of the sacrifice and began the matter of confession because the service ceased with the destruction of the Temple because of our sins, and he indicated that the utterance of our lips would be accepted in place of the sacrifice, and that there is a future for the service to return to its place, and he indicated to rise to give thanks in the matter of the redemption, and he awakened in the matter of repentance, because through repentance the redemption will come, and he arranged verses for the sake of the profanation of His name and the profanation of His Torah and the profanation of His Temple, that He should be jealous for their sake and redeem Israel, and concludes. All the arrangement is connected one to the other. And afterward, he arranges five sanctifications corresponding to the five books of the Torah, and the reason for it is that at the beginning of the prayer, when he began to bless and praise God, may He be exalted, the intention was in this praise that He is separate from all existents and far from physicality and from what applies to physicality and all needs of the body, since all these are possibly existent, and He alone is separate in the necessity of existence; it is impossible that they should be included in one definition, and all this we understood from consideration of His actions, and we obligated it that He is perfect in the ultimate perfection, and His unity is a true unity, for this is the true praise that is fitting to praise God, may He be exalted, and after this belief, the belief in the Torah also was confirmed, a complete belief. And the Torah spoke the language of man, and its matters appear to stand against what the intellect demonstrated from the truth of His perfection, may He be exalted, from all deficiency, and all the more so that it arranged matters of the sacrifices, and because of the arrangement of the sacrifice mentioned in the prayer, the arranger wanted to indicate that God, may He be exalted, is separate in the ultimate separation from the benefits of physicality; no physical attainment will reach Him, but all these matters that the Torah arranged from physical attainments is to help the listeners understand. And all the arrangement of the sacrifices is the need of the lowly; therefore, the arranger came to arrange five sanctifications corresponding to the five books of the Torah, each and every sanctification teaches its matter from the essence of that book. Behold, for the book of Genesis, he says, "And You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel" (Ps 22:4), which means that You are separate, eternal, for the word "holy" teaches about separation and distinction, and the word "enthroned" teaches about persistence and eternity; the reason is that if the world is renewed, as was indicated in the verse, "In the beginning, God created" (Gen 1:1), God, may He be exalted, is primordial, eternal, separate from all existents. And the explanation of the verse, "And You are holy," is that You are holy, You dwell forever, You are the praises of Israel. And the second sanctification is for the book of "And these are the names" (Exodus), concerning the matter because the matter of the book is for the sake of the exodus of Israel from Egypt, they say in the sanctification the verse, "Our redeemer, the Lord of hosts is His name, the Holy One of Israel" (Isa 47:4), which means the redeemer of Israel, and it calls Him "the Lord of hosts" for the sake of the hosts of Israel, as it says, "And I will bring out My hosts, My people" (Exod 7:4), and it described Him with the name "Holy" for separation and distinction. And the third sanctification is for the book of Leviticus, because in this book it arranges matters of the sacrifices, it says the threefold "holy," which is the verse, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts" (Isa 6:3), to indicate the ultimate separation and distinction from all needs of the body, for all these that are brought [as sacrifices] are not for the benefit of God, may He be exalted, from all deficiency, but all these are for the need of the lowly. And because He watches over the lower world with individual providence and knows the slowness and the guidance of His creatures at the time of their sin, He made them eat slowly and guided them and purified them from the defilement of the material, and this is the ultimate correction of the sacrifices, not that they are for the benefit of God, may He be exalted, from all deficiency. And the fourth sanctification is for the sake of the book of Numbers, and it is the verse, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place" (Ezek 3:12). And because the intention of the book is in the counting of Israel, who are the twelve tribes, that they should be four standards, for Israel is similar to the upper world, resembling the four faces of the chariot, which are the twelve signs of the zodiac, "He set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel" (Deut 32:8). And behold, "Each had four faces; and each one had four wings" (Ezek 1:6), the hint is that three tribes, which are one standard, behold, there are "four faces to one," for the sons of Levi were divided into four heads, for Moses and Aaron and his sons were in the east, and behold, there are "four faces to one." And behold, he arranged the whole inclusion of this passage and the matters of the standards and the Tabernacle and the Ark and the glory that dwells in it, resembling the matters of the chariot, and the discerning will understand them. And because this verse is said concerning the matter of the chariot, therefore they said it concerning this book, and therefore he said, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place," like the chariot, which indicates the rider. And the fifth sanctification is for the fifth book, which is the book of Deuteronomy, and it is the verse, "Hear, O Israel" (Deut 6:4). And the arranger chose this verse because this book is the repetition of the Torah; he wanted to unify God, that He has no change of any kind of changes, neither change of knowledge nor change of will, but He is uniquely unified, a true unity, in the proof of the intellect, in this arrangement, not in the statement of a prophet, as we have agreed concerning the matter of unity, that it bears bearing God by way of a statement of a prophet, and therefore he connected to it, "Believe in the Lord your God so shall you be established" (2Chr 20:20). But because the desire was to stand here against Scripture in the proofs of the intellect, therefore this verse is justified to be here by way of an intellectual teacher, and therefore the word, that is to say, the word "Hear," is established according to the two intentions in the arrangement of unity, its matter being the matter of reception, and in the arrangement of the sanctification, its matter being the matter of understanding, and what helped in this is the verse itself being from the essence of the book. And in each and every sanctification, they preface verses according to the desire of the one who prays, according to the time and the will, but conclude with those verses from the nature of the sanctification, to connect between the stages, like saying, "And to whom will you liken God" (Isa 40:18), "And to whom will you liken Me, and I shall be equal, says the Holy One" (Isa 40:25), "And You are holy" (Ps 22:4), and similarly, "And your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel" (Isa 41:14), "Our redeemer, the Lord of hosts" (Isa 47:4), similar to this is the arrangement of the sanctifications. And after the sanctifications, he says an acknowledgement, "One is our God, great is our Lord, holy and awesome is His name forever." And he arranges four acknowledgements: the Lord our God, one true God, and His perfect Torah is true, and His Temple, the house of prayer, is true, and His prophets are true, and His commandments and His statutes and His testimonies and His judgments and all His words are true, "And the Lord God is truth, He is the living God" etc. (Jer 10:10), "And do not snatch the word of truth from my mouth utterly" etc. (Ps 119:43), and he says, "All Your works shall praise You, O Lord, and Your pious ones shall bless You" (Ps 145:10). And he says the kingdom of heaven, "Blessed are You, O Lord God of Israel, our Father, from everlasting to everlasting. (1Chr 29:10) Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the might" etc. (1Chr 29:11), which includes the praises of God, may He be exalted, praises with which He is praised in consideration of all parts of existence, the upper world and the middle and the lower. And he says, "And now, our God, we thank You, and praise the name of Your glory" (1Chr 29:13). And he falls on his face on the ground and says a supplication, "In You our fathers trusted; they trusted, and You delivered them" (Ps 22:5), "Let my heart be perfect in Your statutes, that I may not be ashamed" (Ps 119:80). And he says, "For we do not present our supplications before You because of our righteousness, but because of Your great mercies" (Dan 9:18). And he requests forgiveness and mercy for Jerusalem and for His people Israel, and he says, "O Lord, hear; O Lord, forgive; O Lord, listen and act, do not delay; for Your own sake, my God, for Your name is called upon Your city and upon Your people" (Dan 9:19). And he says, "Turn from Your fierce anger" (Exod 32:12), and concludes, "Blessed be the Lord forever." And he makes a prayer in a whisper, as we found a hint from Hannah the righteous one, as it says, "Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard" (1Sam 1:13), and this is the prayer of individuals, each one requesting atonement for his sin, his affliction, and his pain, that He look upon him with mercy to provide for him according to his needs, that he not be ashamed in his life, and requesting forgiveness for himself and his household and his sons, with verses that indicate these matters, and for the peace of all Israel, and afterward, the cantor prays aloud, "Be strong, and let your heart take courage" (Ps 31:25), "And you, be strong, and do not let your hands be weak" (2Chr 15:7), concerning the matter of the building of Jerusalem and the gathering of all Israel, as he says, "The Lord builds Jerusalem" (Ps 147:2), "Creating the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him who is far off and to him who is near" (Isa 57:19), that is to say, peace to whoever repents from a near time and peace to whoever repents from a far time, and concludes, "The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace" (Ps 29:11), and concludes, "Blessed be the Lord forever; Amen and Amen" (Ps 89:53). And they still make a prayer in a whisper, each and every one, to sanctify His great name and to magnify His Torah and to build His Temple and the building of Zion and Jerusalem and the gathering of Isr

content.hebrew: סדר תפלת בקר. ובבקר השכם נכנסים בבית הכנסת כורעים ומשתחוים. וחזן הכנסת מתחיל "יְהִי שֵׁם ה' מְבֹרָךְ--  מֵעַתָּה, וְעַד-עוֹלָם. (תהילים קיג, ב) מִמִּזְרַח-שֶׁמֶשׁ עַד-מְבוֹאוֹ--  מְהֻלָּל, שֵׁם ה'" (תהילים קיג, ג) דומה הענין לפי העת. ומתחיל בענין ברכה כמו שבארנו ומחבר מזמור "בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי,  אֶת-ה'" (תהילים קד, א) כי בהקיצו  משנתו נפשו פנויה מכל עסקים ומברכת ומשבחת לאל ית' וחתימתו "בָּרְכוּ ה',  מַלְאָכָיו: גִּבֹּרֵי כֹחַ, עֹשֵׂי דְבָרוֹ" (תהילים קג, כ) "בָּרְכוּ ה', כָּל-צְבָאָיו" (תהילים קג, כא) "בָּרְכוּ ה', כָּל-מַעֲשָׂיו" (תהילים קג, כב) דמיון " בְּרָן-יַחַד, כּוֹכְבֵי בֹקֶר;  וַיָּרִיעוּ, כָּל-בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים" (איוב לח, ז). ומחבר עמו מזמור "ה' אֱלֹהַי, גָּדַלְתָּ מְּאֹד;  הוֹד וְהָדָר לָבָשְׁתָּ" (תהילים קד, א). כי בידוע לחוקרי האמת ששני המזמורים כאחד ורמזים יש בזה המזמור לפי העת כגון "עֹטֶה-אוֹר, כַּשַּׂלְמָה" (תהילים קד, ב) "תִּזְרַח הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, יֵאָסֵפוּן" (תהילים קד, כב) "יֵצֵא אָדָם לְפָעֳלוֹ" (תהילים קד, כג) וחותם "יְהִי כְבוֹד ה' לְעוֹלָם;  יִשְׂמַח ה' בְּמַעֲשָׂיו" (תהילים קד, לא) וחותם "בָּרוּךְ, ה' אֱלֹהִים--אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" (תהילים עב, יח) ועומד ומסדר היחוד ובהגיע למקום שאומר "תָּשֶׁת-חֹשֶׁךְ, וִיהִי לָיְלָה" (תהילים קד, כ) בערב אומר בבקר ברוך "יוֹצֵר אוֹר וּבוֹרֵא חֹשֶׁךְ" (ישעיהו מה, ז) "וְהוּא מְהַשְׁנֵא עִדָּנַיָּא, וְזִמְנַיָּא" (דניאל ב, כא) כפי הסדר המסודר לענין היוצר. ומשלים היחוד ואומר רב חסד ומסדר ענין הקרבן ובמקום שאומר בערב "וּבְהַעֲלֹת אַהֲרֹן אֶת-הַנֵּרֹת" (שמות ל, ח) אומר בבקר "וְהִקְטִיר עָלָיו אַהֲרֹן, קְטֹרֶת סַמִּים" (שמות ל, ז) מפני כי בבקר צריכים הנרות תקון והטבה ובערב הדלקה לבערם כמשפט. ומסדרים אחרי הקרבן מזמור "בְּכָל-יוֹם אֲבָרְכֶךָּ"{{fn:31}} (תהילים קמה, ב) כנרמז "וְלַעֲמֹד בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר, לְהֹדוֹת וּלְהַלֵּל לַה'; וְכֵן, לָעָרֶב" (דברי הימים א כג, ל) מקום השיר שהיו משוררים בעת עלות הקרבן ומתחילים ביום ראשון "ה' מָלָךְ,  גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ" (תהילים צג, א) סדר אותם המזמורים עד "ה' מָלָךְ, תָּגֵל הָאָרֶץ" (תהילים צז, א). וביום ששי מזמור "ה' אֲדֹנֵינוּ--  מָה-אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ, בְּכָל-הָאָרֶץ" (תהילים ח, ב) כפי מה שנאות לבריאת היום. ויושב ואומר ודוי "וְעַתָּה מַה-נֹּאמַר אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (עזרא ט, י) ומשלים הודוי ומתחיל מזמור "אֲמָרַי הַאֲזִינָה ה'" (תהילים ה, ב) בעבור פסוק "ה' - בֹּקֶר, תִּשְׁמַע קוֹלִי" (תהילים ה, ד). ומחבר פסוקים מרמיזים על עת תפלת הבקר ואומר "וְתִיטַב לַה', מִשּׁוֹר פָּר;  מַקְרִן מַפְרִיס" (תהילים סט, לב) שניב שפתינו יהא מקום הקרבת הקרבן. ובעבור כי אחר קרבן הבקר יכשר להביא קרבנות נדרים ונדבות כי בין קרבן ערב ובקר אין מקריבים קרבן אבל בין קרבן בקר וערב יש להקריב על כן מחבר פסוקים "וְאָבוֹאָה, אֶל-מִזְבַּח אֱלֹהִים--  אֶל-אֵל, שִׂמְחַת גִּילִי" (תהילים מג, ד) ואומר "וְאֶזְבְּחָה בְאָהֳלוֹ, זִבְחֵי תְרוּעָה" (תהילים כז, ו) "נְדָרַי, לַה' אֲשַׁלֵּם;  נֶגְדָה-נָּא, לְכָל-עַמּוֹ" (תהילים קטז, יד) ואומר "וְעָרְבָה, לַה', מִנְחַת יְהוּדָה" (מלאכי ג, ד) וחותם " הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ ה' אֵלֶיךָ וְנָשׁוּבָה" (איכה ה, כא) שמבקש להשיב העבודה על מכונתה בשוב ישראל לארצם "כִּימֵי עוֹלָם, וּכְשָׁנִים קַדְמֹנִיֹּת" (מלאכי ג, ד). ואחרי כן מסדר המזמורים שהם בקשה למחילת עונות ולבקשת הישועה להוציאם מן הגלות והם מזמורים משובחים כגון מזמור "הַטֵּה-ה' אָזְנְךָ עֲנֵנִי--  כִּי-עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן אָנִי" (תהילים פו, א) ומזמור "חָנֵּנִי אֱלֹהִים כְּחַסְדֶּךָ" (תהילים נא, ג). הנה במזמור "הַטֵּה-ה' אָזְנְךָ" אומר "חָנֵּנִי אֲדֹנָי:  כִּי אֵלֶיךָ אֶקְרָא, כָּל-הַיּוֹם" (תהילים פו, ג). ואומר במזמור "חָנֵּנִי אֱלֹהִים כְּחַסְדֶּךָ" מה שמרמיז מקרבנות הנדבה "אָז תַּחְפֹּץ זִבְחֵי-צֶדֶק,  עוֹלָה וְכָלִיל" (תהילים נא, כא) שהם נקרבים ביום. ואחרי כן אומר "מִי-אֵל כָּמוֹךָ, נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן" (מיכה ז, יח) הרמז כלו למחילת העון וגאולת ישראל מן הגלות. ועומד ואומר מזמור "אֵלֶיךָ ה', נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" (תהילים כה, א) המורה לגאולת ישראל. והיה זה המזמור מסגולת תפלת היום כאשר אומר "הַדְרִיכֵנִי בַאֲמִתֶּךָ, וְלַמְּדֵנִי–   כִּי-אַתָּה, אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׁעִי; אוֹתְךָ קִוִּיתִי,  כָּל-הַיּוֹם" (תהילים כה, ה). ואחרי כן אומר מזמור הראוי וחותם כל התפלה כדרך שחותם בערב:
content.english: The order of the morning prayer. And in the early morning, they enter the house of assembly, kneel, and bow down. And the cantor of the assembly begins, "Let the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forevermore. (Ps 113:2) From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the Lord is praised" (Ps 113:3), similar to the matter according to the time. And he begins with the matter of blessing, as we have explained, and connects the psalm, "Bless the Lord, O my soul" (Ps 104:1), for in his awakening from his sleep, his soul is free from all business, and it blesses and praises God, may He be exalted, and its conclusion, "Bless the Lord, O His angels, mighty in strength, who do His word" (Ps 103:20), "Bless the Lord, all His hosts" (Ps 103:21), "Bless the Lord, all His works" (Ps 103:22), like "when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted" (Job 38:7). And he connects with it the psalm, "O Lord my God, You are very great; You are clothed with glory and majesty" (Ps 104:1). For it is known to the investigators of truth that the two psalms are as one, and there are hints in this psalm according to the time, such as "Who covers Yourself with light as with a garment" (Ps 104:2), "The sun rises, they are gathered together" (Ps 104:22), "Man goes forth to his work" (Ps 104:23), and concludes, "Let the glory of the Lord endure forever; let the Lord rejoice in His works" (Ps 104:31), and concludes, "Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel" (Ps 72:18), and he stands and arranges the unity, and when he reaches the place where it says, "You make darkness, and it is night" (Ps 104:20), in the evening; he says in the morning, blessed is "Who forms light and creates darkness" (Isa 45:7), "And He changes the times and the seasons" (Dan 2:21), according to the arrangement arranged for the matter of the Creator. And he completes the unity and says "Who is abundantly kind," and arranges the matter of the sacrifice, and in the place where it says in the evening, "And when Aaron lights the lamps" (Exod 30:8), he says in the morning, "And Aaron shall burn on it incense of spices" (Exod 30:7), because in the morning, the lamps need repair and preparation, and in the evening, lighting to burn them according to the law. And they arrange after the sacrifice the psalm, "Every day I will bless You" (Ps 145:2), as hinted, "And to stand every morning to thank and praise the Lord, and likewise at evening" (1Chr 23:30), the place of the song that they would sing at the time of the rising of the sacrifice, and they begin on the first day, "The Lord reigns, He is clothed with majesty" (Ps 93:1), arranging those psalms until "The Lord reigns, let the earth rejoice" (Ps 97:1). And on the sixth day, the psalm, "O Lord, our Lord, how glorious is Your name in all the earth" (Ps 8:2), according to what is appropriate for the creation of the day. And he sits and says a confession, "And now, what shall we say, our God" (Ezra 9:10), and completes the confession, and begins the psalm, "Give ear to my words, O Lord" (Ps 5:2), for the sake of the verse, "O Lord, in the morning shall You hear my voice" (Ps 5:4). And he connects verses hinting to the time of the morning prayer, and says, "And it shall be better to the Lord than an ox or bull that has horns and hoofs" (Ps 69:32), that the utterance of our lips will be in place of the offering of the sacrifice. And because after the morning sacrifice, it is proper to bring sacrifices of vows and freewill offerings, for between the evening and morning sacrifices, they do not offer a sacrifice, but between the morning and evening sacrifice, there is to offer, therefore he connects verses, "And I will come to Your altar, O God, to God, the joy of my delight" (Ps 43:4), and he says, "And I will sacrifice in His tent sacrifices of shouts of joy" (Ps 27:6), "I will pay my vows to the Lord; may it be in the presence of all His people" (Ps 116:14), and he says, "And the offering of Judah and Jerusalem shall be pleasant to the Lord" (Mal 3:4), and concludes, "Return us to You, O Lord, and we will return" (Lam 5:21), asking to return the service to its place when Israel returns to their land, "as in the days of old and as in former years" (Mal 3:4). And afterward, he arranges the psalms that are a request for the forgiveness of sins and for the request of salvation to bring them out from exile, and they are excellent psalms, such as the psalm, "Incline your ear, O Lord, answer me, for I am poor and needy" (Ps 86:1), and the psalm, "Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your kindness" (Ps 51:3). Behold, in the psalm, "Incline your ear, O Lord," he says, "Be gracious to me, O Lord, for to You I cry all the day" (Ps 86:3). And he says in the psalm, "Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your kindness," what hints from the sacrifices of freewill offering, "Then You will delight in sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt-offering and whole burnt-offering" (Ps 51:21), which are offered during the day. And afterward, he says, "Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity" (Mic 7:18), the entire hint for the forgiveness of sin and the redemption of Israel from exile. And he stands and says the psalm, "To You, O Lord, I lift up my soul" (Ps 25:1), which indicates the redemption of Israel. And this psalm was from the special properties of the prayer of the day, as he says, "Lead me in Your truth, and teach me, for You are the God of my salvation; for You I wait all the day" (Ps 25:5). And afterward, he says the appropriate psalm and concludes all the prayer in the way that he concludes in the evening.
content.comments: 31 אֲבָרְכֶךָּ" — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "every single day," whereas the verse as cited (Ps 145:2) reads: "every day I will bless you."

content.hebrew: פרק שלישי
content.english: Chapter Three

content.hebrew: סדר תפלת ראש חדש. אם יקרה להיות ראש חדש מוסיפים אחר מזמור "הָבוּ לַה', בְּנֵי אֵלִים" (תהילים כט, א) פסוקים מרמיזים לענין חדוש הירח ומתחילים הענין "נֵר-לְרַגְלִי דְבָרֶךָ;  וְאוֹר, לִנְתִיבָתִי" (תהילים קיט, קה) הטעם התורה התמימה היא המאירת עינים ללכת בדרכי יושר. "פֵּתַח דְּבָרֶיךָ יָאִיר;  מֵבִין פְּתָיִים" (תהילים קיט, קל) הרמז כלו על התורה אשר "דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי-נֹעַם;  וְכָל-נְתִיבוֹתֶיהָ שָׁלוֹם" (משלי ג, יז) כמאמר "יְהִי מְאֹרֹת" (בראשית א, יד) ועל כן סמוך לו "מֵפֵר אֹתוֹת בַּדִּים, וְקֹסְמִים יְהוֹלֵל" (ישעיהו מד, כה) רמז על הבודים מלבם לשנות מצות התורה שהתורה הישירתנו לקדש החדש בראייה וכך מודים גם בעלי הקבלה אלא החליפו הכתוב ובדו מלבם לקדש החדש במולד כיוצא בזה החדש אשר בדא מלבו (מלכים א יב, לג). סמוך לו "מֵשִׁיב חֲכָמִים אָחוֹר, וְדַעְתָּם יְסַכֵּל" (ישעיהו מד, כה) כי אפילו על המולד עצמו אינם מתנהגים על המולד האמתי מפני שזה הדבר עמוק להשיגו על בוריו ועד עתה מדקדקים עליו האצטגנינים ולא יוכלו לעמוד על בוריו. והנה הם מתנהגים לקדש המולד במהלך האמצעי והמולד האמתי פעם יתקדם ופעם יתאחר למה שהוא במהלך האמצעי. הנה בזמננו זה שנת חמשת אלפים מאה וארבע עשרה שנה ליצירה בחדש תשרי אשר הקרה לקות השמש בשש שעות של יום אשר שעת הלקות הוא הקבוץ האמתי והמולד שלהם היה בשמנה שעות של לילה על כן נאמר "מֵשִׁיב חֲכָמִים אָחוֹר, וְדַעְתָּם יְסַכֵּל" (ישעיהו מד, כה). וסדר פסוקים לזייף מחשבת האצטגנינים. וחבר מאמר "עַל-הָרֹעִים חָרָה אַפִּי" (זכריה י, ג) שבאמת שזה הטעות לא היה כי אם מן גדולי האומה והרמיז שעונש עתיד לבוא עליהם באמרו "עַל-הָרֹעִים חָרָה אַפִּי, וְעַל-הָעַתּוּדִים אֶפְקוֹד" (זכריה י, ג) בעת שתבוא נחמה לישראל כאמרו "כִּי-פָקַד ה' צְבָאוֹת אֶת-עֶדְרוֹ, אֶת-בֵּית יְהוּדָה" (זכריה י, ג) רמז לדבר "הִנֵּה עֲבָדַי יָרֹנּוּ, מִטּוּב לֵב; וְאַתֶּם תִּצְעֲקוּ מִכְּאֵב לֵב, וּמִשֵּׁבֶר רוּחַ תְּיֵלִילוּ" (ישעיהו סה, יד). ואחרי כן מחבר פרק "יְהִי מְאֹרֹת" (בראשית א, יד) עם פסוקים דומים לענין ואומר מזמור "הַרְנִינוּ, לֵאלֹהִים עוּזֵּנוּ" (תהילים פא, ב) בעבור "תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר;  בַּכֵּסֶה, לְיוֹם חַגֵּנוּ" (תהילים פא, ד). ומסדר מזמורים מרמיזים לענין המאורות וצבא השמים כגון "הַלְלוּ-יָהּ: הַלְלוּ אֶת-ה', מִן-הַשָּׁמַיִם" (תהילים קמח, א) "הַלְלוּ-יָהּ: הַלְלוּ-אֵל בְּקָדְשׁוֹ" (תהילים קנ ,א) וחותם "הוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (תהילים קו, מז) ומשלימים כל התפלה כסדר. ובבקר בהגיע למזמור "חָנֵּנִי אֱלֹהִים כְּחַסְדֶּךָ" (תהילים נא, ג) מוסיף ודוי "ה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, צַדִּיק אַתָּה" (עזרא ט, טו) כפי תוספת המרי. ואומר מזמור "הַלְלוּ-יָהּ: הַלְלוּ, אֶת-שֵׁם ה';  הַלְלוּ, עַבְדֵי ה'.  (תהילים קלה, א) שֶׁעֹמְדִים, בְּבֵית ה'" (תהילים קלה, ב)  הקדמה למזמור "כִּי אֲנִי יָדַעְתִּי, כִּי-גָדוֹל ה'" (תהילים קלה, ה) וזה המזמור משובח ומעולה לענין הגאולה כמו שגאל את ישראל ממצרים שיגאלם גם מזו הגלות כאשר אמר "כִּי-יָדִין ה' עַמּוֹ;  וְעַל-עֲבָדָיו, יִתְנֶחָם. (תהילים קלה, יד)  עֲצַבֵּי הַגּוֹיִם, כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב;  מַעֲשֵׂה, יְדֵי אָדָם" (תהילים קלה, טו) "כְּמוֹהֶם, יִהְיוּ עֹשֵׂיהֶם" וכו' (תהילים קלה, יח) וחותם המזמור ועומד ואומר "שַׂמֵּחַ, נֶפֶשׁ עַבְדֶּךָ:  כִּי אֵלֶיךָ אֲדֹנָי, נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" (תהילים פו, ד) שגם זה המזמור לענין הגאולה. ובעבור שרוצה לסדר ענין החדש בקרבן עוד מסדר שבח והודאה וסדר מעשיי לאמת ההשגחה ומסדר הקרבן. וענין השבח הוא מזמור "ה', אוֹרִי וְיִשְׁעִי" וכו' (תהילים כז, א) שהוא שבח לענין הגאולה. וההודאה מזמור "אוֹדְךָ בְכָל-לִבִּי" (תהילים קלח, א). וסדר מעשיי לאמת ההשגחה ענין השירה כי התורה לא תתאמת רק באמונת ההשגחה וענין הקרבן הוא ענין תוריי. ומסדר אחרי השירה מזמור "אַשְׁרֵי נְשׂוּי-פֶּשַׁע" (תהילים לב, א) בעבור "עַל-זֹאת, יִתְפַּלֵּל כָּל-חָסִיד אֵלֶיךָ--  לְעֵת מְצֹא: רַק, לְשֵׁטֶף מַיִם רַבִּים--  אֵלָיו, לֹא יַגִּיעוּ" (תהילים לב, ו) ומזמור "רַנְּנוּ צַדִּיקִים, בַּה'" (תהילים לג, א) בעבור "כֹּנֵס כַּנֵּד, מֵי הַיָּם;  נֹתֵן בְּאוֹצָרוֹת תְּהוֹמוֹת" (תהילים לג, ז). וחותם "הוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ" וכו' (תהילים קו, מז). ומתחיל "ה', בְּצִיּוֹן גָּדוֹל" (תהילים צט, ב) "בָּרוּךְ, ה' אֱלֹהִים--אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" וכו' (תהילים עב, יח). משבח ומברך את השי"ת אשר נתן את התורה ומאשר את התורה באמרו "כִּי-יָשָׁר דְּבַר-ה'" (תהילים לג, ד) "רֹאשׁ-דְּבָרְךָ אֱמֶת" (תהילים קיט, קס) "אַתָּה, צִוִּיתָה פִקֻּדֶיךָ" (תהילים קיט, ד) "גַּל-עֵינַי וְאַבִּיטָה" (תהילים קיט, יח) "טוֹב-אַתָּה וּמֵטִיב" וכו' (תהילים קיט, סח) ומתחיל הקרבן "וּבְרָאשֵׁי, חָדְשֵׁיכֶם" וכו' ( במדבר כח, יא) וחותם בפסוק "וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶם וּבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם, וּבְרָאשֵׁי חָדְשֵׁיכֶם" (במדבר י, י) כי בכל המוספים היו תוקעים בחצוצרות. ואומר שיר כי בעת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה, הֵחֵל שִׁיר-ה' (דברי הימים ב כט, כז) והוא מזמור "הַרְנִינוּ, לֵאלֹהִים עוּזֵּנוּ" וכו' (תהילים פא, ב) מרמיז לענין החדש "תִּקְעוּ בַחֹדֶשׁ שׁוֹפָר" (תהילים פא, ד) ונופל על פניו ואומר ודוי "וּבְעֵת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה, הֵחֵל שִׁיר-ה' וְהַחֲצֹצְרוֹת" (דברי הימים ב כט, כז) "וְעַתָּה מַה-נֹּאמַר אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (עזרא ט, י) ומחבר פסוקים "חָדְשֵׁיכֶם וּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם שָׂנְאָה נַפְשִׁי" (ישעיהו א, יד) לאמר מתי יעבור החדש (עמוס ח, ה) "וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי, כָּל-מְשׂוֹשָׂהּ, חַגָּהּ, חָדְשָׁהּ וְשַׁבַּתָּהּ--וְכֹל, מוֹעֲדָהּ" (הושע ב, יג) ערבה כל שמחה וכו' (ישעיהו כד, יא) כאלו הפסוקים וכיוצא בהם המורים לענין החדש. וחותם בענין בקשת מחילה "שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ" (שמות לב, יב) ואחרי כן אומר "לֹא הֶאֱמִינוּ מַלְכֵי-אֶרֶץ, כֹּל יֹשְׁבֵי תֵבֵל:  כִּי יָבֹא צַר וְאוֹיֵב" וגו' (איכה ד, יב) וקם ואומר "אֱלֹהִים, בָּאוּ גוֹיִם בְּנַחֲלָתֶךָ" (תהילים עט, א) שצריך בזה הסדר לומר  בעבור ששבתה העבודה בקרבן המוסף והיה זה מפני שנתחייבו גלות ונחרב המקדש. ועוד מבשר לענין הגאולה. ובכל המועדים אומרים מזמור "לָמָה אֱלֹהִים, זָנַחְתָּ לָנֶצַח" (תהילים עד, א) משום "שָׁאֲגוּ צֹרְרֶיךָ, בְּקֶרֶב מוֹעֲדֶךָ" (תהילים עד, ד) "שָׂרְפוּ כָל-מוֹעֲדֵי-אֵל בָּאָרֶץ" (תהילים עד, ח). ויום ראש חדש אינו מועד על כן אומרים מזמור "אֱלֹהִים, בָּאוּ גוֹיִם בְּנַחֲלָתֶךָ" (תהילים עט, א) שהוא דומה לענינו. ואחרי כן מסדר מזמורים מרמיזים לענין המאורות הכתובים בערב ומזמור "הַשָּׁמַיִם, מְסַפְּרִים" וגו' (תהילים יט, ב) עם מזמור "ה' אֲדֹנֵינוּ--  מָה-אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ" ( תהילים ח, ב) בעבור "כִּי-אֶרְאֶה שָׁמֶיךָ" (תהילים ח, ד). ואומר קדושה ובקדושות מחבר פסוקים מרמיזים לענין החדש ומסדר פרק "וְאָהַבְתָּ, אֵת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" (דברים ו, ה) למעלת היום וכנראה שדין לומר בכל הימים זה הפרק ערב ובקר כאשר מתנהגים קהלות אחרות. אבל אני סובר כי מפני עלה קצרוהו לאופן מה שכונו בו בעלי הקבלה רצו להרחיק המחשבה ההיא והמבין יבין. ואומר ארבע הודאות והודאה חמישית וראשי חדשיו בראיית הירח אמת. ומסדר ההלל "הַלְלוּ אֶת-ה', כָּל-גּוֹיִם" וכו' (תהילים קיז, א) כסדרו מפני שכל יום שנתחייבו אנשי הבית קרבן מוסף בזמן המקדש נתחייבו אותו היום אנשי הגלות במוסף הלל ושבח על דרך "וּנְשַׁלְּמָה פָרִים, שְׂפָתֵינוּ" (הושע יד, ג) ואומר ההלל וחותמים  התפלה כמנהג:
content.english: The order of the prayer of the new moon. If it happens that Rosh Chodesh (New Moon)occurs, they add, after the psalm, "Ascribe to the Lord, O sons of the mighty" (Ps 29:1), verses that hint to the matter of the renewal of the moon, and they begin the matter, "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path" (Ps 119:105), the reason being, the perfect Torah is what enlightens the eyes to walk in the ways of righteousness. "The entrance of Your words gives light; it gives understanding to the simple" (Ps 119:130), the entire hint is on the Torah, which "her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace" (Prov 3:17), like the verse, "Let there be lights" (Gen 1:14), and therefore next to it, "Who frustrates the signs of the liars and makes fools of diviners" (Isa 44:25), a hint about those who fabricate from their hearts to change the commandments of the Torah, which the Torah directed us to sanctify the month by sight, and so the Rabbanites also acknowledge, but they changed the verse and fabricated from their hearts to sanctify the month at the conjunction, similar to this is "the month which he had devised of his own heart" (1Kgs 12:33). Next to it, "Who turns the wise backward and makes their knowledge foolish" (Isa 44:25), for even on the conjunction itself, they do not conduct themselves according to the true conjunction, because this matter is deep to grasp it properly, and until now, the astronomers are precise about it, and they cannot stand on its clarity. And behold, they conduct themselves to sanctify the conjunction by the average motion, and the true conjunction sometimes precedes and sometimes delays from what it is in the average motion. Behold, in our time, year 5114 from creation, in the month of Tishri, when there was an eclipse of the sun at six hours of the day, which the time of the eclipse is the true conjunction, and their conjunction was at eight hours of the night, therefore it says, "Who turns the wise backward and makes their knowledge foolish" (Isa 44:25). And he arranged verses to falsify the thought of the astronomers. And he connected the verse, "My anger burns against the shepherds" (Zech 10:3), for in truth, this error was only from the great ones of the nation, and the hint is that punishment is destined to come upon them, as he says, "My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the male goats" (Zech 10:3), at the time that comfort comes to Israel, as he says, "For the Lord of hosts has visited His flock, the house of Judah" (Zech 10:3), a hint to the matter, "Behold, My servants shall sing for joy of heart, but you shall cry for sorrow of heart and shall wail for vexation of spirit" (Isa 65:14). And afterward, he connects the chapter, "Let there be lights" (Gen 1:14), with verses similar to the matter, and says the psalm, "Sing aloud to God our strength" (Ps 81:2), for the sake of "Blow the horn at the new moon, at the full moon, on our feast day" (Ps 81:4). And he arranges psalms that hint to the matter of the luminaries and the host of heaven, such as, "Praise the Lord! Praise the Lord from the heavens" (Ps 148:1), "Praise the Lord! Praise God in His sanctuary" (Ps 150:1), and concludes, "Save us, O Lord our God" (Ps 106:47), and completes all the prayer in order. And in the morning, upon reaching the psalm, "Be gracious to me, O God, according to Your kindness" (Ps 51:3), he adds a confession, "O Lord God of Israel, You are righteous" (Ezra 9:15), according to the addition of rebellion. And he says the psalm, "Praise the Lord! Praise the name of the Lord; praise, O servants of the Lord, (Ps 135:1) who stand in the house of the Lord" (Ps 135:2), an introduction to the psalm, "For I know that the Lord is great" (Ps 135:5), and this psalm is excellent and superior for the matter of redemption, just as He redeemed Israel from Egypt, that He will redeem them also from this exile, as he says, "For the Lord will judge His people, and He will repent for His servants. (Ps 135:14) The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of men's hands" (Ps 135:15), "Those who make them shall be like them" etc. (Ps 135:18), and concludes the psalm and stands and says, "Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul" (Ps 86:4), for this psalm also is for the matter of redemption. And because he wants to arrange the matter of the month in the sacrifice, he again arranges praise and thanksgiving and a practical narrative to confirm providence, and he arranges the sacrifice. And the matter of the praise is the psalm, "The Lord is my light and my salvation" etc. (Ps 27:1), which is praise for the matter of redemption. And the thanksgiving is the psalm, "I will praise You with my whole heart" (Ps 138:1). And the practical narrative to confirm providence is the matter of the song, for the Torah is only confirmed in the belief in providence, and the matter of the sacrifice is a matter of the Torah. And he arranges after the song the psalm, "Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven" (Ps 32:1), for the sake of "Therefore let everyone who is godly pray to You at a time when You may be found; surely in a flood of great waters, they shall not reach him" (Ps 32:6), and the psalm, "Sing joyfully, O righteous, in the Lord" (Ps 33:1), for the sake of "Gathering as a heap the waters of the sea, putting the depths in storehouses" (Ps 33:7). And he concludes, "Save us, O Lord our God" etc. (Ps 106:47). And he begins, "The Lord in Zion is great" (Ps 99:2), "Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel" etc. (Ps 72:18). He praises and blesses the Lord, may He be blessed, who gave the Torah, and he confirms the Torah, saying, "For the word of the Lord is upright" (Ps 33:4), "The beginning of Your word is truth" (Ps 119:160), "You have commanded Your precepts" (Ps 119:4), "Open my eyes, that I may behold" (Ps 119:18), "You are good and do good" etc. (Ps 119:68), and he begins the sacrifice, "And on the beginnings of your months" etc. (Num 28:11), and concludes with the verse, "And on the day of your gladness, and on your appointed feasts, and on the beginnings of your months" (Num 10:10), for in all the additional offerings, they would blow the trumpets. And he says a song, for at the time "when the burnt offering began, the song of the Lord began" (2Chr 29:27), and it is the psalm, "Sing aloud to God our strength" etc. (Ps 81:2), hinting to the matter of the month, "Blow the horn at the new moon" (Ps 81:4), and he falls on his face and says a confession, "And at the time when the burnt offering began, the song of the Lord began, and the trumpets" (2Chr 29:27), "And now, what shall we say, our God" (Ezra 9:10), and he connects verses, "Your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates" (Isa 1:14), saying, "when will the month be gone" (Amos 8:5), "And I will cause all her mirth to cease, her feast, her new moon, and her Sabbath, and all her appointed feasts" (Hos 2:13), all joy has ceased, etc. (Isa 24:11), like these verses and similar to them, which indicate the matter of the month. And he concludes with the matter of the request for forgiveness, "Turn from Your fierce anger" (Exod 32:12), and after that he says, "The kings of the earth did not believe, nor all the inhabitants of the world, that the adversary and the enemy could come into the gates" etc. (Lam 4:12), and he arises and says, "O God, the nations have come into Your inheritance" (Ps 79:1), for he needs in this arrangement to say, because the service has ceased in the additional sacrifice, and this was because they were obligated in exile, and the Temple was destroyed. And he also announces concerning the matter of redemption. And in all the appointed times, they say the psalm, "Why, O God, have You cast us off forever" (Ps 74:1), because of "Your enemies have roared in the midst of Your appointed place" (Ps 74:4), "They have burned all the appointed places of God in the land" (Ps 74:8). And the day of Rosh Chodesh (New Moon)is not an appointed time; therefore, they say the psalm, "O God, the nations have come into Your inheritance" (Ps 79:1), which is similar to its matter. And afterward, he arranges psalms hinting to the matter of the luminaries written in the evening, and the psalm, "The heavens declare" etc. (Ps 19:2), with the psalm, "O Lord, our Lord, how glorious is Your name" (Ps 8:2), for the sake of "When I consider Your heavens" (Ps 8:4). And he says a sanctification, and in the sanctifications, he connects verses hinting to the matter of the month, and he arranges the chapter, "And you shall love the Lord your God" (Deut 6:5), for the excellence of the day, and it appears that there is a judgment to say on all days this chapter, evening and morning, as other congregations conduct themselves. But I think that because of some reason, they shortened it for some manner that the Rabbanites intended in it; they wanted to distance that thought, and the understander will understand. And he says four acknowledgements and a fifth acknowledgement, and his new moons, in the sight of the moon, are true. And he arranges the Hallel, "O praise the Lord, all you nations" etc. (Ps 117:1), in its order, because every day that the people of the House were obligated in an additional sacrifice in the time of the Temple, the people of exile were obligated on that day in additional Hallel and praise, in the manner of "and we will render the bulls of our lips" (Hos 14:3), and he says the Hallel and concludes the prayer as is customary.

content.hebrew: פרק רביעי
content.english: Chapter Four

content.hebrew: סדר תפלת ערב שבת. בערב שבת בעוד היום בששי באים אל בית הכנסת בהשתחויה וכריעה להוסיף מחול על קדש שמירה לשבת. ומתחילים הקדמה "שְׁלַח-אוֹרְךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ,  הֵמָּה יַנְחוּנִי" וכו' (תהילים מג, ג) ואומר מזמור "מַה-יְּדִידוֹת מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֶיךָ" (תהילים פד, ב) מפני שרגילים היו להתועד במקדש בשבת משאר הימים לכך אומר זה המזמור על השתוקקות אהבה וחבה להתפלל לשם ית'. ואומר היחוד ראשי ענינים בפסוקים ראויים ואומר "שְׁמַע, יִשְׂרָאֵל" (דברים ו, ד) ומתחיל "ה', שִׁמְךָ לְעוֹלָם" (תהילים קלה, יג) עד "מֵאֵין כָּמוֹךָ, ה'" (ירמיהו י, ו) ואומר "כִּי-גָדוֹל אַתָּה, וְעֹשֵׂה נִפְלָאוֹת" (תהילים פו, י) ומשלים היחוד "וְרַב-חֶסֶד" (שמות לד, ו) ומחבר לענין קדוש השבת "וַיְכֻלּוּ הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ, וְכָל-צְבָאָם" כל הענין המסודר (בראשית ב, א). ואומר התמיד עם "מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר, לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת" (תהילים צב, א) וחותם בהעמדה ודוי "אִם-אֶשְׁכָּחֵךְ יְרוּשָׁלִָם" (תהילים קלז, ה) ובקשת מחילה "שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ" וכו' (שמות לב, יב). ואומר קדושה בקצרה ואומר ארבע הודאות והודאה חמישית ושבתותיו המקודשות אמת וחותם התפלה. והיה הרצון שלא להאריך בתפלה מפני שאינם מדליקים נר ומשתדלים לברך את השבת על השלחן בעוד נוגה היום לבוא עניניהם בתקון ממאכלם ומשקיהם:
content.english: The order of the prayer of the eve of the Sabbath. On the eve of the Sabbath, while it is still the sixth day, they come to the house of assembly with bowing and kneeling, to add from the profane to the holy, guarding the Sabbath. And they begin the introduction, "Send forth Your light and Your truth, let them lead me" etc. (Ps 43:3), and say the psalm, "How lovely are Your tabernacles" (Ps 84:2), because they were accustomed to gather in the Temple on the Sabbath more than other days; therefore, they say this psalm concerning the longing of love and affection The order of the prayer of the eve of the Sabbath. On the eve of the Sabbath, while it is still the sixth day, they come to the house of assembly with bowing and kneeling, to add from the profane to the holy, guarding the Sabbath. And they begin the introduction, "Send forth Your light and Your truth, let them lead me" etc. (Ps 43:3), and say the psalm, "How lovely are Your tabernacles" (Ps 84:2), because they were accustomed to gather in the Temple on the Sabbath more than other days; therefore, they say this psalm concerning the longing of love and affection to pray to God, may He be exalted. And they say the unity, the main points in appropriate verses, and say, "Hear, O Israel" (Deut 6:4), and begin, "O Lord, Your name is everlasting" (Ps 135:13), until "There is none like You, O Lord" (Jer 10:6), and say, "For You are great, and do wondrous things" (Ps 86:10), and complete the unity, "And abundantly kind" (Exod 34:6), and connect to the matter of the sanctification of the Sabbath, "And the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host," all the arranged matter (Gen 2:1). And he says the daily offering with "A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day" (Ps 92:1), and concludes with a standing confession, "If I forget you, O Jerusalem" (Ps 137:5), and a request for forgiveness, "Turn from Your fierce anger" etc. (Exod 32:12). And they say a sanctification in brief, and say four acknowledgements and a fifth acknowledgement, and His sanctified Sabbaths are true, and conclude the prayer. And the intention was not to lengthen the prayer because they do not light a lamp, and they strive to bless the Sabbath at the table while there is still light of day, to handle their matters in preparation for their food and drink.

content.hebrew: סדר חצות הקטון. ובחצות לילה קמים ואומרים חצות קטן. מתחיל ואומר מזמור "אֲבָרְכָה אֶת-ה'" (תהילים לד, ב) ועומד ואומר היחוד של עשרת ימי רחמים שהוא בלי מעריב ויוצר עם תוספת פסוקים ומשלימו כאשר נבארהו. ואומר הודאה כאשר היא מסודרת וחותם. ואחרי כן מסדר פסוקים לענין אזהרה וחותם. ואחרי כן מסדר פסוקים מענין תשובה וחותם. ואחרי כן מסדר פסוקים לענין תוכחה וחותם. ואחרי כן מסדר פסוקים ליום המיתה וחותם. ואחרי כן מסדר פסוקים ליום הדין וחותם. ואומר ודוי וחותם. זהו חצות הקטון:
content.english: The order of the small midnight. And at midnight, they arise and say the small midnight. He begins and says the psalm, "I will bless the Lord" (Ps 34:2), and stands and says the unity of the ten days of repentance, which is without bringing the evening and creating, with additions of verses, and completes it as we shall explain it. And he says the acknowledgement as it is arranged and concludes. And afterward, he arranges verses for the matter of admonition and concludes. And afterward, he arranges verses from the matter of repentance and concludes. And afterward, he arranges verses for the matter of rebuke and concludes. And afterward, he arranges verses for the day of death and concludes. And afterward, he arranges verses for the day of judgment and concludes. And he says a confession and concludes. This is the small midnight.

content.hebrew: סדר חצות הגדול. אך חצות הגדול מאריך בענין התוכחה ומסדר פסוקי הבטחה למחילה שהוא מוחל וסולח ואין זולתו. ומסדר פסוקי תשובה ומשלים בודוי ובקשה:
content.english: The order of the great midnight. But the great midnight lengthens in the matter of the rebuke and arranges verses of promise for forgiveness, that He pardons and forgives, and there is none beside Him. And he arranges verses of repentance and concludes with a confession and a request.

content.hebrew: סדר תפלת השחר. אמנם תפלת השחר מקדימים הקדמה כוללת ענין אזהרה ותוכחה ותשובה לפי קשר הפסוקים גם לענין העת כגון "אֱלֹהִים, אֵלִי אַתָּה--  אֲשַׁחֲרֶךָּ" (תהילים סג, ב) "לְהַגִּיד בַּבֹּקֶר חַסְדֶּךָ" (תהילים צב, ג) "עוּרָה, הַנֵּבֶל וְכִנּוֹר" (תהילים קח, ג) וכיוצא בהם וחותם "יוֹמָם, יְצַוֶּה ה' חַסְדּוֹ" (תהילים מב, ט) "אֲבָרֵךְ--אֶת-ה', אֲשֶׁר יְעָצָנִי" (תהילים טז, ז). ומתחיל מזמור "אֲבָרְכָה אֶת-ה' בְּכָל-עֵת" (תהילים לד, ב) ומשלימו. ואחרי כן מסדר מזמורים עם הקדמותיהם אם לענין היום אם לענין הפרשה אם לעלה לענין מילה אם לענין שמחה או הפכה וחותם "הוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (תהילים קו, מז) "בָּרוּךְ ה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" (תהילים קו, מח) "בָּרוּךְ ה' לְעוֹלָם" (תהילים פט, נג). זהו סדר תפלת השחר:
content.english: The order of the dawn prayer. However, the dawn prayer, they preface with a comprehensive introduction concerning the matter of admonition and rebuke and repentance, according to the connection of the verses, and also for the matter of the time, such as, "O God, You are my God; early will I seek You" (Ps 63:2), "To declare Your kindness in the morning" (Ps 92:3), "Awake, O harp and lyre" (Ps 108:3), and similar to them, and concludes, "By day the Lord will command His kindness" (Ps 42:9), "I will bless the Lord, who has counseled me" (Ps 16:7). And he begins the psalm, "I will bless the Lord at all times" (Ps 34:2), and completes it. And afterward, he arranges psalms with their introductions, whether for the matter of the day, whether for the matter of the portion, whether for the reason for a matter of circumcision, whether for the matter of joy or its opposite, and concludes, "Save us, O Lord our God" (Ps 106:47), "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel" (Ps 106:48), "Blessed be the Lord forever" (Ps 89:53). This is the order of the dawn prayer.

content.hebrew: סדר תפלת הבקר של שבת. ובבקר השכם מתחיל תפלת חובה עם פסוקים הראויים כגון "אֲדֹנָי, שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח;  וּפִי, יַגִּיד{{fn:32}} תְּהִלָּתֶךָ" וכו' (תהילים נא, יז) או לפי רצון המתפלל לחבר פסוקים הראויים אם להאריך אם לקצר או פיוט הראוי מחובר לפסוק "תְּהִלַּת ה', יְדַבֶּר-פִּי וִיבָרֵךְ כָּל-בָּשָׂר" (תהילים קמה, כא). ואומר "בָּרְכִי נַפְשִׁי,  אֶת-ה'" (תהילים קד, א) וחותם "בָּרוּךְ, ה' אֱלֹהִים--אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" (תהילים עב, יח). ועומד ואומר היחוד כפי שהוא מסודר עד "שְׁמַע, יִשְׂרָאֵל" (דברים ו, ד). מכניס פסוקים נאותים אל אותו החבור אם להאריך אם לקצר ואומר "שְׁמַע, יִשְׂרָאֵל" ומתחיל ה' אלהינו בוראנו. ומוסיף פסוקים לענין היחוד שראויים להורות על היחוד ומסיים היחוד ואומר ההודאה ומחבר לקדוש היום "זָכוֹר אֶת-יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, לְקַדְּשׁוֹ" (שמות כ, ח). ואומר "טוֹב, לְהֹדוֹת לַה'" (תהילים צב, ב) לחבר ענין הקרבן עם למזמור "ה' מָלָךְ, יִרְגְּזוּ עַמִּים" (תהילים צט, א). ונופל על פניו ואומר ודוי גדול בתוספת פסוקים הראויים לתוכחה כללית וחותם "שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ" (שמות לב, יב). ואחרי כן מחבר המזמורים "אֲמָרַי הַאֲזִינָה ה'" (תהילים ה, ב) עם סדר הפסוקים ומזמור "הַטֵּה-ה' אָזְנְךָ" (תהילים פו, א) אם ירצה עם הקדמותיהם. גם מזמור "תְּפִלָּה, לְעָנִי כִי-יַעֲטֹף" (תהילים קב, א) שגם הוא בקשה ותחנה למחילת עונותיהם. ואומרים עוד וידוי גדול "אֱלֹהַי בֹּשְׁתִּי וְנִכְלַמְתִּי" (עזרא ט, ו) ומחברים בו הודאה לשם ית' מזמור "הַלְלוּ-יָהּ הַלְלוּ, אֶת-שֵׁם ה'" (תהילים קלה, א) "מִי יְמַלֵּל, גְּבוּרוֹת ה'" (תהילים קו, ב). ואומר "זָכְרֵנִי ה', בִּרְצוֹן עַמֶּךָ" (תהילים קו, ד) ועומד ואומר "אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם,  לֹא-הִשְׂכִּילוּ נִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ" (תהילים קו, ז) כל המזמור. והודוי הראשון הוא במה שחל עליהם מצד עונותיהם מעניני הגלות וחרבן המקדש בעבור שביתת העבודה ובטול התמיד ושבר ציון וירושלם כאשר יורה כל הסדר. והנה מחבר מזמורים שהם בקשה ותחנה ואחרי כן מחבר זה הודוי אשר סדורו יורה שאין להם לשאת פנים מצד רוב עונותיהם וגודל אשמתם. ונותנים הודאה לשם ית' כי כל מה שחל עליהם כדין חל. ומשלים מזמור "אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְמִצְרַיִם,  לֹא-הִשְׂכִּילוּ" ומורה כי מה שחל להם לא חל אלא במריונם וקושי לבם הערל. וכשמשלימים המזמור עם תוכחות אחרות מחברים חבור "וָאֹמַר אֵלֶיהָ, יָמִים רַבִּים תֵּשְׁבִי לִי" (הושע ג, ג) שמורה ממה שיקרה לעתיד כגון שאמר "וָאֹמַר אֵלֶיהָ, יָמִים רַבִּים תֵּשְׁבִי לִי לֹא תִזְנִי, וְלֹא תִהְיִי לְאִישׁ" (הושע ג, ג). ואמר "וְיָמִים רַבִּים, לְיִשְׂרָאֵל  לְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי אֱמֶת" וכו' (דברי הימים ב טו, ג) והורה כי הם יעלו על ידי תשובה כאמרו "וַיָּשָׁב, בַּצַּר-לוֹ, עַל{{fn:33}}-ה', אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל; וַיְבַקְשֻׁהוּ, וַיִּמָּצֵא לָהֶם" (דברי הימים ב טו, ד). ומחבר הסדר כי מפני עני ישראל אין להם עצור ועזוב "יָדִין ה' עַמּוֹ;  וְעַל-עֲבָדָיו, יִתְנֶחָם" (דברים לב, לו). ומחבר הבשורות העתידות לבוא לישראל שהם בשורות נאמנות ומאשר לשם ית' "מִי-אֵל כָּמוֹךָ, נֹשֵׂא עָוֺן וְעֹבֵר עַל-פֶּשַׁע, לִשְׁאֵרִית, נַחֲלָתוֹ" (מיכה ז, יח) בעבור זכות האבות כאמרו "וְזָכַרְתִּי, אֶת-בְּרִיתִי יַעֲקוֹב" וגו' (ויקרא כו, מב) לגאלם גאולה גמורה עולמית כאשר אומר "זְכֹר עֲדָתְךָ, קָנִיתָ קֶּדֶם" וגו' (תהילים עד, ב) וחותם ויושב ונופל על פניו ומתחיל עוד ודוי גדול אנא ה' ברחמיך הרבים וכו' וסדר זה הודוי בהודאת החטא כי בקשת המחילה על החטא מפני הרחמים וכל זה הקדמה למזמור "חָנֵּנִי אֱלֹהִים כְּחַסְדֶּךָ" (תהילים נא, ג) הרמז במה שיעד בפסוק "וַיָּשָׁב, בַּצַּר-לוֹ, עַל-ה', אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל; וַיְבַקְשֻׁהוּ, וַיִּמָּצֵא לָהֶם" (דברי הימים ב טו, ד). ומאשר לשם ית' בנושא עון להביא הגאולה לישראל ואומר "הוֹשִׁיעָה, אֶת-עַמֶּךָ--  וּבָרֵךְ אֶת-נַחֲלָתֶךָ" (תהילים כח, ט). ואומר "עַם-זוּ יָצַרְתִּי לִי, תְּהִלָּתִי יְסַפֵּרוּ" (ישעיהו מג, כא) כי אחרי שמחל להם וגאלם הנה מספרים תהלתו אחרי שהוציאם מן הגלות והביאם אל ארצם כאשר אמר "לְסַפֵּר בְּצִיּוֹן, שֵׁם ה';  וּתְהִלָּתוֹ, בִּירוּשָׁלִָם" (תהילים קב, כב). ועומד ואומר מזמור "כִּי אֲנִי יָדַעְתִּי, כִּי-גָדוֹל ה'" (תהילים קלה, ה) שהוא מורה לגאולת ישראל עם מזמור "אֵלֶיךָ ה', נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" (תהילים כה, א) כאשר בארנו ענינו וחותם. ואחרי כן אם רוצה מסדר קצת הפרקים "אַשְׁרֵי תְמִימֵי-דָרֶךְ" (תהילים קיט, א) כי הנושעים הם צדיקים. ובעבור שרוצה לסדר המוסף ונעתק מפרק אל פרק מתחיל "עַל-חוֹמֹתַיִךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַם, הִפְקַדְתִּי שֹׁמְרִים" (ישעיהו סב, ו) כאלו שסדרי התפלה כמו החומות וכמו כן הפרקים. וענין הפרקים לאשר התודו ונמחל להם ונושעו בגאולה העתידה ועל כן מאשרם "אַשְׁרֵי תְמִימֵי-דָרֶךְ" ואומר גם כן שירי המעלות וחותם "הוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (תהילים קו, מז) כאשר תקנם המסדר. חלוקים הפרקים בכל יום ויום מימי השובע עם שירי המעלות שלהם. אחרי כן מתחיל מזמור "אֵלֶיךָ ה', נַפְשִׁי אֶשָּׂא" עם מזמור "ה', אוֹרִי וְיִשְׁעִי" (תהילים כז, א) אם ירצה עם הקדמותיהם והוא תמור שבח היחוד כמו שהרמזנו. ואומר הודאה "אוֹדְךָ בְכָל-לִבִּי" (תהילים קלח, א). ואם ירצה אומר מזמור "אֵלֶיךָ ה' אֶקְרָא--  צוּרִי" (תהילים כח, א) גם מזמור "קוֹלִי אֶל-אֱלֹהִים וְאֶצְעָקָה" (תהילים עז, ב) שיש להם חבור לענין השירה אם ירצה עם הקדמותיהם. ומתחיל שירת "וַיּוֹשַׁע ה'" (שמות יד, ל) ומשלימים השירה כפי הצורך שבארנו. ומחברים מזמורי "אַשְׁרֵי נְשׂוּי-פֶּשַׁע" (תהילים לב, א) ומזמור "רַנְּנוּ צַדִּיקִים, בַּה'" (תהילים לג, א) כפי שזכרנו. כל זה הסדר מענין השירה שהוא ענין מעשיי לאמת ההשגחה כפי מה שהעירונו לאמת התורה. וחותם "הוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ, ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (תהילים קו, מז) שכל מה שסדר הוא לענין ישועה ומרמיז גם על הישועה העתידה לבוא לישראל. ומתחיל באשור התורה "הָאֵל, תָּמִים דַּרְכּוֹ" ( תהילים יח, לא). ומתחיל הענין מעניני האזהרה על השבת. ואומר המוסף "וּבְיוֹם, הַשַּׁבָּת--שְׁנֵי-כְבָשִׂים" וכו' (במדבר כח, ט). ומתחיל מאשר ומשבח מעלת השבת באמור "וְעַל הַר-סִינַי יָרַדְתָּ" (נחמיה ט, יג). וכי יש שכר רב בעולם הזה לשומריה ומקיימיה כאשר אמר "אַשְׁרֵי אֱנוֹשׁ יַעֲשֶׂה-זֹּאת, וּבֶן-אָדָם יַחֲזִיק בָּהּ" (ישעיהו נו, ב). הנה שכרו רב בעולם הזה ועצום בעולם הבא כאמרו "אָז, תִּתְעַנַּג עַל-ה'" (ישעיהו נח, יד). ומשלים ענין זה ואומר "מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר, לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת" (תהילים צב, א) כי כן אומר "וּבְעֵת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה, הֵחֵל שִׁיר-ה' וְהַחֲצֹצְרוֹת" (דברי הימים ב כט, כז) ואולם לא היו תוקעים חצוצרות על כן  לא חייב המסדר לומר "וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶם" (במדבר י, י) אכן מאמר ""וּבְעֵת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה, הֵחֵל שִׁיר-ה'" (דברי הימים ב כט, כז) הטעם בעבור השיר ולא בעבור חצוצרות. ואחרי כן יושב ונופל על פניו ואומר "וּבְעֵת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה" ואומר הודוי "וְעַתָּה מַה-נֹּאמַר אֱלֹהֵינוּ" (עזרא ט, י) "יָדַעְנוּ ה' רִשְׁעֵנוּ" (ירמיהו יד, כ) ומסדר יעודים רעים אשר חלו עלינו מפני שהפרנו מצות שבת ומספר שיד החורים והסגנים הכהנים שהם מורי התורה היתה במעל הזה לחלל השבת כאמרו "כֹּהֲנֶיהָ חָמְסוּ תוֹרָתִי, וַיְחַלְּלוּ קָדָשַׁי--בֵּין-קֹדֶשׁ לְחֹל לֹא הִבְדִּילוּ, וּבֵין-הַטָּמֵא לְטָהוֹר לֹא הוֹדִיעוּ; וּמִשַּׁבְּתוֹתַי הֶעְלִימוּ עֵינֵיהֶם, וָאֵחַל בְּתוֹכָם" (יחזקאל כב, כו) ומסיים כל הודוי בבקשת מחילה "שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ" (שמות לב, יב) וחותם. ומתחיל המזמורים שהם בקשת תחנה למחול על עונותיהם כגון מזמור "קוֹלִי, אֶל-ה' אֶזְעָק" (תהילים קמב, ב) עם מזמור "ה', שְׁמַע תְּפִלָּתִי" (תהילים קמג, א) וחותם "הוֹשִׁיעָה, אֶת-עַמֶּךָ" (תהילים כח, ט) לענין הגאולה. ואומר הקדמה "רְעֵה עַמְּךָ בְשִׁבְטֶךָ, צֹאן נַחֲלָתֶךָ" (מיכה ז, יד) למזמור "רֹעֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַאֲזִינָה--  נֹהֵג כַּצֹּאן יוֹסֵף" (תהילים פ, ב). והיתה הכונה בעבור שסדר בתוכחות הנביאים והכהנים אשר הם רועי ישראל ומורי התורה כאלו נאמר זה המזמור על צד הבקשה שיהיה רועה נאמן להם ככתוב "אֲנִי אֶרְעֶה צֹאנִי וַאֲנִי אַרְבִּיצֵם" (יחזקאל לד, טו). ועוד שמסדר על הפורענות שבאו לישראל מצד עונותיהם וכי הוא יעוררם אל התשובה לקרב ימי הגאולה בביאת המשיח זהו טעם כל המזמור סמוך לו "רָצִיתָ ה' אַרְצֶךָ" (תהילים פה, ב) שהוא מורה אמתת הגאולה. ואחרי כן מחבר פסוקים לשבח מעלת משה רבינו ע"ה ולמעלת נבואתו כאשר סדרו בסדר "בְּחֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת, יְכֻפַּר עָוֺן" (משלי טז, ו) בעבור להזכיר מזמור "תְּפִלָּה, לְמֹשֶׁה" (תהילים צ, א). וכבר הקדמנו הבאור בטעם זה המזמור שהוא מזכיר שבחו של שם ית' והשגחתו עלינו והוא מעוררנו אל התשובה להנצל מדין יעודים הרעים לבקש ממנו לשוב אלינו ברחמים לגאלנו גאולת עולם כאמור "יֵרָאֶה אֶל-עֲבָדֶיךָ פָעֳלֶךָ" (תהילים צ, טז) "וִיהִי, נֹעַם אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהֵינוּ--  עָלֵינוּ" (תהילים צ, יז). ואחרי כן מחבר פסוקים על דרך בקשה כדי שיהמו רחמי השם עלינו לזכור הברית כאמרו "אַל-תִּנְאַץ לְמַעַן שִׁמְךָ" (ירמיהו יד, כא) הבט לברית (תהילים עד, כ). ולחמול עלינו מצד עניותנו כגון "אַל-יָשֹׁב דַּךְ נִכְלָם" (תהילים עד, כא). ולקנאתו בשביל אויבינו כגון שאמר "קוּמָה אֱלֹהִים, רִיבָה רִיבֶךָ" (תהילים עד, כב). "אַל-תִּשְׁכַּח, קוֹל צֹרְרֶיךָ" (תהילים עד, כג). ושיזכור חרפתם אשר חרפוהו כגון שאמר "זְכֹר ה' חֶרְפַּת עֲבָדֶיךָ". ושיזכור היסורים שעברו עלינו כגון שאומר "זְכֹר ה' מֶה-הָיָה לָנוּ" (איכה ה, א). ולקנאתו בשבילנו מפני שאנחנו מעשה ידיך כחומר ביד היוצר (ירמיהו יח, ו). ומסדר "אוֹמְרָה, לְאֵל סַלְעִי--  לָמָה שְׁכַחְתָּנִי" (תהילים מב, י) "כִּי-אַתָּה, אֱלֹהֵי מָעוּזִּי--  לָמָה זְנַחְתָּנִי" (תהילים מג, ב) הרצון שבטחוננו בשם ית'. ואומר "לָמָּה תַתְעֵנוּ ה' מִדְּרָכֶיךָ" (ישעיהו סג, יז) ר"ל מפני שאתה מתאפק לענוש הרשעים על רשעם נראה שאין השגחה עליונית על כן אמר "שׁוּב לְמַעַן עֲבָדֶיךָ" (ישעיהו סג, יז). ומספר בגדולות ובנפלאות שעשה השם ית' לישראל מהשגחתו הרבה עליהם ואומר "פָּגַעְתָּ אֶת-שָׂשׂ וְעֹשֵׂה צֶדֶק" (ישעיהו סד, ד) בשביל משה ואהרן "בִּדְרָכֶיךָ יִזְכְּרוּךָ" (ישעיהו סד, ד) כשהיית קוצף "הֵן-אַתָּה קָצַפְתָּ" (ישעיהו סד, ד) מפני שחטאנו והם היו עומדים בפרץ לפניך אמנם עתה אין קורא בשמך מתעורר להחזיק בך (ישעיהו סד, ו) וזה מפני עון כאמרו "כִּי-הִסְתַּרְתָּ פָנֶיךָ מִמֶּנּוּ, וַתְּמוּגֵנוּ בְּיַד-עֲוֺנֵנוּ" (ישעיהו סד, ו) אמנם יש לך לחוס עלינו מפני שאנחנו מעשי ידיך על כן "אַל-תִּקְצֹף ה' עַד-מְאֹד" (ישעיהו סד, ח) כי "עָרֵי קָדְשְׁךָ, הָיוּ מִדְבָּר" (ישעיהו סד, ט) "בֵּית קָדְשֵׁנוּ וְתִפְאַרְתֵּנוּ" (ישעיהו סד, י) "הַעַל-אֵלֶּה תִתְאַפַּק, ה'" (ישעיהו סד, יא). ומזכיר קנאת חלול שמו וחלול תורתו וקנאת חלול מקדשו וקנאת חרפת עמו בית ישראל ומזכיר "מִקְוֵה, יִשְׂרָאֵל, מוֹשִׁיעוֹ, בְּעֵת צָרָה" (ירמיהו יד, ח) הואיל ואנחנו נשענים עליך " לָמָּה תִהְיֶה כְּגֵר בָּאָרֶץ, וּכְאֹרֵחַ נָטָה לָלוּן" (ירמיהו יד, ח) "לָמָּה תִהְיֶה כְּאִישׁ נִדְהָם, כְּגִבּוֹר לֹא-יוּכַל לְהוֹשִׁיעַ; וְאַתָּה בְקִרְבֵּנוּ ה', וְשִׁמְךָ עָלֵינוּ נִקְרָא--אַל-תַּנִּחֵנוּ" (ירמיהו יד, ט). ומחבר מזמור "עַד-אָנָה ה', תִּשְׁכָּחֵנִי נֶצַח" (תהילים יג, ב) נתן הסבה מפני שמחת אויבים באמרו "פֶּן-יֹאמַר אֹיְבִי יְכָלְתִּיו" (תהילים יג, ה) וחותם. ומתחיל הקדושות ומחבר בכל קדושה פסוקים לפי רצון המתפלל אם נוגעים לענין פרשת היום או לענין שבח או לענין מה שהוא רוצה וחותם הקדושות ואומר "שְׁמַע, יִשְׂרָאֵל" (דברים ו, ד) "וְאָהַבְתָּ, אֵת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ" (דברים ו, ה). ואומר ארבע הודאות והודאה חמישית ושבתותיו המקודשות אמת. ואומר "כִּי-כֹה אָמַר ה', רָנּוּ לְיַעֲקֹב שִׂמְחָה, וְצַהֲלוּ, בְּרֹאשׁ הַגּוֹיִם" (ירמיהו לא, ז) לבקש ישועה מהשם באמרו "הוֹשַׁע ה' אֶת-עַמְּךָ" (ירמיהו לא, ז). ואומר מלכות שמים ויושב ומתחנן "יְהִי-לִבִּי תָמִים בְּחֻקֶּיךָ" (תהילים קיט, פ). ומבקש "וְעַתָּה אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהֵינוּ, אֲשֶׁר הוֹצֵאתָ אֶת-עַמְּךָ" (דניאל ט, טו). ומצדיק דין השם ית' באמרו "אֲדֹנָי, כְּכָל-צִדְקֹתֶךָ יָשָׁב-נָא אַפְּךָ וַחֲמָתְךָ" וכו' (דניאל ט, טז). ומשלים "שׁוּב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפֶּךָ" (שמות לב, יב) "שׁוּב לְמַעַן עֲבָדֶיךָ" (ישעיהו סג, יז) "הֲשִׁיבֵנוּ ה' אֵלֶיךָ" (איכה ה, כא) ואומר תפלה בלחש ואחרי כן אומר "קוּמָה, עֶזְרָתָה לָּנוּ" (תהילים מד, כז). ומשלים התפלה כסדרה וחותם. ואומר תפלה בלחש שנית ואחרי כן קמים ומשתחוים לשם ית' ונותנים שלום איש לרעהו וחוזרים הזקנים שלפני התבה ויושבים כלפי העם והעם פניהם נגד הזקנים. ואם יהיה ראש חדש בשבת הדין נותן להשלים התפלה עד מזמור "רֹעֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל" (תהילים פ, ב). ואחרי כן אומר סדר החדש כי לא יתכן אחר קרבן התמיד לומר קרבן ראש חדש כי הודויים לא תקנום המסדרים רק לפי עניני הקרבנות. והנה בקרבן התמיד סדר הודוי הראשון ועליו חברו פסוקים ופרק "עַל-מִשְׁמַרְתִּי אֶעֱמֹדָה" (חבקוק ב, א). "וְרָאִיתִי אֲנִי דָנִיֵּאל" (דניאל יב, ה) בעבור "וּמֵעֵת הוּסַר הַתָּמִיד" (דניאל יב, יא) גם "הוֹדִיעֵנִי ה', קִצִּי" (תהילים לט, ה) אדות קץ התמיד. גם מאמר "אֱלִי, כִּבְתוּלָה חֲגֻרַת-שַׂק" (יואל א, ח). ואיך אפשר להפסיק ביניהם ולומר מוסף של שבת:
content.english: The order of the morning prayer of the Sabbath. And in the early morning, he begins the prayer of obligation with appropriate verses, such as, "O Lord, open my lips; and my mouth will declare Your praise" etc. (Ps 51:17), or according to the will of the one who prays, to connect appropriate verses, whether to lengthen or to shorten, or an appropriate poem composed for the verse, "My mouth shall speak the praise of the Lord, and all flesh shall bless" (Ps 145:21). And he says, "Bless the Lord, O my soul" (Ps 104:1), and concludes, "Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel" (Ps 72:18). And he stands and says the unity as it is arranged until "Hear, O Israel" (Deut 6:4). He introduces verses appropriate to that composition, whether to lengthen or to shorten, and says, "Hear, O Israel," and begins, "The Lord our God, our Creator." And he adds verses for the matter of unity that are appropriate to indicate concerning the unity, and he concludes the unity, and says the acknowledgement, and connects to the sanctification of the day, "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it" (Exod 20:8). And he says, "It is good to give thanks to the Lord" (Ps 92:2), to connect the matter of the sacrifice with the psalm, "The Lord reigns, let the peoples tremble" (Ps 99:1). And he falls on his face and says a great confession with the addition of verses appropriate for general rebuke, and concludes, "Turn from Your fierce anger" (Exod 32:12). And afterward, he connects the psalms, "Give ear to my words, O Lord" (Ps 5:2), with the arrangement of the verses, and the psalm, "Incline Your ear, O Lord" (Ps 86:1), if he wishes, with their introductions. Also the psalm, "A prayer of the afflicted when he is faint" (Ps 102:1), which is also a request and a supplication for the forgiveness of their sins. And they say another great confession, "My God, I am ashamed and confounded" (Ezra 9:6), and they connect in it thanksgiving to God, may He be exalted, the psalm, "Praise the Lord! Praise the name of the Lord" (Ps 135:1), "Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord" (Ps 106:2). And he says, "Remember me, O Lord, with the favor of Your people" (Ps 106:4), and stands and says, "Our fathers in Egypt did not understand Your wonders" (Ps 106:7), all the psalm. And the first confession is about what befell them because of their sins from the matters of exile and the destruction of the Temple because of the cessation of the service and the nullification of the daily offering and the breaking of Zion and Jerusalem, as all the arrangement indicates. And behold, he connects psalms that are a request and a supplication, and afterward, he connects this confession, the arrangement of which indicates that they have nothing to be forgiven for, because of the multitude of their sins and the greatness of their guilt. And they give thanks to God, may He be exalted, that all that befell them, according to the law it befell them. And he completes the psalm, "Our fathers in Egypt did not understand," and indicates that what befell them befell only in their rebellions and the hardness of their uncircumcised heart. And when they complete the psalm with other rebukes, they connect the composition, "And I said to her, Many days you shall abide for me" (Hos 3:3), which indicates what will happen in the future, such as he says, "And I said to her, Many days you shall abide for me; you shall not commit harlotry, and you shall not be for another man" (Hos 3:3).
