And we would say that it wants to include all blood that comes out from the animal, such as the blood of limbs, the blood of slaughter, and the blood of washing, and we would think that no other blood would be prohibited except the mentioned blood, as it says in the prohibition of fat, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat, you shall not eat" (Lev 7:23), and it mentioned also the punishment, and only the fat of these mentioned animals would be prohibited. So it wanted also in the prohibition of blood on these mentioned, "for the bird and for the animal," it implies that in its saying, "And any blood you shall not eat," it answers on all kinds of blood that come out from the animal. And what it mentioned in the section of Re'eh in two places, there is no doubt that because it mentioned the meat of desire, and it wanted to explain that the blood would not be thrown on the altar, it warned in eating it, saying, "Only the blood you shall not eat," in order to say, "On the earth you shall pour it out like water," "Only be strong not to eat the blood," and it appears that it did not instruct in these statements in the prohibition of blood, except the blood of the meat of desire. But in the section of Acharei Mot, it said, "And any man of the house of Israel and of the strangers who sojourn among them, who eats any blood, I will set My face against the soul that eats" (Lev 17:10). And it is necessary to know that in this place, it mentioned punishment, and the Scripture would not punish unless it warned, if so, the warning is preceding in the verse, "Any fat and any blood, you shall not eat," and in saying, "And any blood you shall not eat, in all your habitations," and after there, it specified, "for the bird and for the animal," this too answers on the blood of the bird and the animal. And however, it repeated the statement here for forms, in order to include the stranger, and to divide the blood into two parts, blood that would be covered and blood that would not be covered, and in order to include two reasons in the prohibition of blood, the blood of the kinds from which they are offered to the altar, saying, "And I have given it to you on the altar" (Lev 17:11), because the blood is the dwelling place of the life, and to mention further a reason in its prohibition, saying, "For the life of the flesh, it is in the blood" (Lev 17:11), and to say that the blood is the life. And because of these reasons, it mentioned also the punishment of one who eats blood, saying, "whoever eats it shall be cut off" (Lev 17:14). And however, its saying, "For the life of the flesh, it is in the blood," because of a reason, in order to prohibit the blood of living things that are not offered to the altar, and we have to say in its giving the reason that the life of all flesh is in its blood, and it said, "For the blood, it is the life" (Deut 12:23), and it is impossible to eat the soul from its kind, and it is the animal soul, and as long as the reason is equal in all the living, that the existence of its life is in its blood, it would be in prohibition to eat that blood. And from here, the blood of fish and locusts is prohibited, even though it did not mention them by name, because their blood does not come out in slaughter, but in eating their flesh, and it said, "For the life of all flesh, its blood it is" (Lev 17:14) [or "For the life of the flesh, it is in the blood" (Lev 17:11)], and the fish are flesh, as it says, "From where shall I get meat" (Num 11:13), and it says, "Shall flock and herd be slaughtered for them, and will it be found for them? If all the fish of the sea were gathered to them, would it be found for them?" (Num 11:22). And locusts are swarming flying things, implying a verse, "And any blood you shall not eat," includes fish and locusts, and their blood comes out in salting, and even though it mentioned "for the bird and for the animal," it mentioned them, for they are the essence, because they are slaughtered, and the evidence is that it said, "Any soul that eats any blood," including the blood of the living things that are permitted in eating. It is the rule that it said in the section of Vayikra, "Any fat and any blood, you shall not eat," and it includes also blood that is found inside the egg, that if it is not woven inside the egg, he scrapes off the blood and eats the egg, and if he finds the blood on the connection of the white or the yolk, it is the connection of the seed of the male, and the egg is forbidden to be eaten, because the chick is formed. And the Scripture obligated that we be careful to strive in its removal from the meat, for thus the eating was said in blood, while he eats the meat without salt, and it said, "And you shall not eat the life with the flesh." And it is necessary in the beginning to leave the slaughtered until its blood is drained out well, and after that, he would do the piercing of the meat to take out the sources in which is the blood, as we have in the tradition. And after that, he would salt the meat with salt that would be neither thin nor thick, until the blood melts to come out from inside the meat, for if it would be very thin, immediately it would melt and not pass inside the meat to melt the blood. And it is necessary when he salts it, for it to be in a perforated vessel or on the back of plain vessels, like in the time of roasting, to take out from it the blood which is drained from the meat, for if not, the blood would still be absorbed in the meat, and the water that comes out from it would not be mixed with blood and would remain with the meat, but it would come out from the hole of the vessel. And after that, he would wash it well until the water comes out pure, and after that, he would cook it or roast it or dry it and eat it. And indeed, it is necessary that he be cautious when he cooks it, all who is very cautious in eating the blood, before, he would boil the water, and after that, he would cast the meat in the water, and the foam comes out in the boiling well, for the heat draws from inside it to take it out, and immediately it floats on the surface of the water. But if he puts the meat in cold or lukewarm water, the meat cooks little by little from the outside, and the blood is detained inside. But roasting on the fire draws the blood, and he should not put underneath it a thing to receive what the fire draws from it, which is a mixture of fat and blood, and it is prohibited. And on the blood of washing, the Torah warned so much, saying, "Only be strong not to eat the blood" (Deut 12:23), for it would be easy for a person to be negligent in this commandment, and therefore it promised the punishment in three places, that it said, "and the soul that eats any blood, that soul shall be cut off" (Lev 7:27), and it says, "I will set My face against the soul that eats" (Lev 17:10), and it says, "whoever eats it shall be cut off" (Lev 17:14), and there is to interpret, against the blood of limbs, the blood of slaughter, the blood of washing. And it is forbidden to feed the non-Israelite the blood, from the warning of the sons of Noah, as it says, "But flesh with its life, its blood, you shall not eat" (Gen 9:4), and the Scripture also promised the reward, saying, "You shall not eat it, that it may be well with you" (Deut 12:25). And because of the piercing of the sources of the head, to the form that they are wide, the salt was sufficient in them alone to take out the blood without piercing. But the bird, to the form that it is hollow, and the sources of blood empty the blood by means of salt, they are not piercing them. However, the liver and the spleen, the sages, peace be upon them, say that it should not be cooked, but roasted on the fire, it would be eaten after its cutting and salting, because the source of blood is in them, and after it is roasted, if he wants, it will be cooked. And it is not necessary to remove the sources of the liver, for after they are wide, they empty the blood, and the thin sources, when they are cut, they empty the blood by means of salting. And when he roasts them, he cuts them, and the heat draws out the blood, not according to the opinion of the Rabbanites, who said that if the blood separates from the liver, it would be prohibited because of the blood, but while it is in the liver, it is not prohibited because of blood. Furthermore, they permitted it if it is cooked with fire in vinegar without salting, because it does not emit, and the blood that is inside it, they permitted it, and this is a thing that is not possible, for if the blood does not separate from it, it would be permitted, and if it separates, it would be in prohibition, and the Scripture says, "And you shall not eat the life with the flesh." And the heart, if it was cooked before it is torn to take out its blood, it is forbidden to be eaten, not according to the opinion of the Rabbanites, who say that after it is cooked, he tears it and takes out its blood, and it is eaten, because the heart, as it swallows, so it emits. And it is necessary to know that because being easy from the many influences to eat the meat and their laziness to take out the blood, and the thing falling by means of great and small, men and women, the Scripture multiplied negative commandments and punishments, and promised also with reward, what is not so in the rest of negative commandments in the Torah, for the children of men to be very cautious, and it promised them for the perseverance of their seed and their goodness, as it says, "that it may be well with you and with your children" (Deut 12:25).
content.comments: 50 הִוא — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "for the life of all flesh is in the blood," but I have not found exactly this verse; rather, two verses in Lev 17: verse 14, "for the life of all flesh — its blood is its life," or verse 11, "for the life of the flesh is in the blood."

content.hebrew: פרק תשעה עשר
content.english: Nineteenth Chapter

content.hebrew: כבר העירונו בפתיחת עניננו זה כי התורה בנויה באמצעות הנבואה לפי חכמת המבטא ולפי בחינת הדבור יהא נודע רצון המדבר וצריך שיהיה שומע הדבור ההוא נבון לחש להבין מליצתו כאלו הוא עצמו המדבר הדבור ההוא ובאיזו מחשבה יהיה עומד בהוציאו הדבור ההוא. ואם אפשר היות דבור אחד ישוה לענינים רבים אי אפשר בלי תוספת ומגרעת לפי בחינת הדבור ההוא אל האמת וצריך להיות המעיין שוכן נפש לקבל איזו כונה ראויה לדבור ההוא בלי נטיה לאחת הסבות המטעות ואז יבחן הענין האמתי מן הבטל. וידוע כי החלב בא אסורו בכתוב בשני מקומות בפרשת ויקרא "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם, בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם--כָּל-חֵלֶב וְכָל-דָּם, לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ" (ויקרא ג, יז) ובפרשת צו "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז--לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ" (ויקרא ז, כג). וישראל נחלקו לשלש דעות בענין החלב. מהם אומרים כי לא אסר הכתוב רק חלב קדשים לא חלבי חולים שחלב חולים הוא בהתר וזהו דת משוי העכברי והנמשכים אחריו. ומהם אומרים שהחלבים הם שלשה אסורים מן החולים שהם החלב המכסה על הקרב ואשר על הקרב וחלב הכליות וזהו דעת הרבנים. ומהם אומרים שהחלבים האסורים מן החולים הם חמשה מן הבקר והעז וששה מן הכבש וזהו דעת הקראים. ואולם בתחלה ראוי לעיין בכתובים לפי משמע הפשט ואחרי כן לחלוק עם משוי העכברי שמתיר חלב חולים ואח"כ נשיב ידינו עם האוסרים השלשה לבד שהם הרבנים. ונאמר שהכתוב אמר בפרשת ויקרא בחתימת פרשת השלמים בקרבן העז "וְהִקְרִיב מִמֶּנּוּ קָרְבָּנוֹ, אִשֶּׁה לַה'--אֶת-הַחֵלֶב, הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת-הַקֶּרֶב, וְאֵת כָּל-הַחֵלֶב, אֲשֶׁר עַל-הַקֶּרֶב. (יקרא ג, יד) וְאֵת, שְׁתֵּי הַכְּלָיֹת, וְאֶת-הַחֵלֶב אֲשֶׁר עֲלֵהֶן, אֲשֶׁר עַל-הַכְּסָלִים; וְאֶת-הַיֹּתֶרֶת, עַל-הַכָּבֵד, עַל-הַכְּלָיֹת, יְסִירֶנָּה" (יקרא ג, טו) ואמר "וְהִקְטִירָם הַכֹּהֵן, הַמִּזְבֵּחָה--לֶחֶם אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ, כָּל-חֵלֶב לַה'" (יקרא ג, טז) וזה המאמר כולל כל חלב לה' בידוע שהוא על חלב קדשים אח"כ אמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם, בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם--כָּל-חֵלֶב וְכָל-דָּם, לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ" (יקרא ג, יז) וזה המאמר אינו עונה על חלב קדשים כי אם על חלב חולים כי בחלב קדשים הורה במאמר "כָּל-חֵלֶב לַה'" אך במאמר "כָּל-חֵלֶב וְכָל-דָּם" הוא באסור חלב חולים ואסר חלב חולים מפני כי הנקרב ממינם החלב נתן למזבח ועל כן חשש גם כן לאסור הדם מפני שגם הדם נתן למזבח מן הנקרבים והורה על החלב באמרו בפרשת צו "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז--לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ" ואמר "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה אִשֶּׁה לַה'" (ויקרא ז, כה). והורה על הדם בפרשת אחרי מות באמרו "וַאֲנִי נְתַתִּיו לָכֶם עַל-הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, לְכַפֵּר עַל-נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם:  כִּי-הַדָּם הוּא, בַּנֶּפֶשׁ יְכַפֵּר" (ויקרא יז, יא) והואיל וזאת היא העלה על כן הזכיר אסורם אצל הקדשים אחרי שהורה שהם נתנים על המזבח הורה גם כן אסורם בסמוך ואם אין כן הענין אבל במאמר "כָּל-חֵלֶב" אינו עונה רק על חלב קדשים מה טעם להורות באסור אכילתם אחרי שהוא נתן למזבח וכמו שלא חשש לאסור אבר מאברי העולה בעבור שהם נתנים למזבח כן לא היה ראוי להורות באסור אכילת החלב אחרי שהוא נשרף ולא עוד אלא אחרי כן אמר "וְכָל-דָּם לֹא תֹאכְלוּ" לאזרח ולגר וכפי דבריו היה עונה אסור הדם גם כן על הקדשים לבדו ובידוע שגם דם החולים באסור. צא ודע כמו שהדם אסור בין מן הקדשים בין מן החולים כן החלב אסור בין מן הקדשים בין מן החולים ולא עוד אלא  שאמר אחרי כן "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם, בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם" וחלב הקדשים אינו כי אם במקום המובחר במקדש ומה טעם "בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם" מלמד שאינו מרמיז רק על חלב חולים. וכדי להשבית טענת כל טוען לא אמר קודם לכן "כָּל-חֵלֶב וְכָל-דָּם" ואחרי כן שיאמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם" למצוא הטוען מקום לאמר שבכל מושבותיכם עונה על הדם ועוד שאמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם" וכל זה המאמר כולל בין זמן הבית בין זמן הגלות ובזמן הגלות אין קרבנות לאסור חלב קדשים ומה שכון באלו המאמרים בא בפרשת צו ובאר ואמר בשביל החלב "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז" והורה שהחלב אינו אסור רק מאלו השלשה מינים מפני שמאלו המינים נקרבים החלבים במזבח כאשר אמר "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה אִשֶּׁה לַה' וְנִכְרְתָה" (ויקרא ז, כה) ואין הרצון באמרו אשר יקריבו ממנה קרבן לה' מן הבהמה עצמה שמקריבים ממנה קרבן יהיה החלב אסור להאכל מפני שאינו דבור מחוכם לפי זאת הכונה כי אין לך בהמה קרבה לקרבן שאין החלב נתן למזבח וכיון שהחלב נתן קרבן אנה ימצא החלב להאכל ושימצא קרבן בהמה שינתן החלב ולא ינתן הבשר נמצא או שינתן החלב והבשר אבל שינתן דבר אחר זולתי החלב לא נמצא ואין יכון המאמר באמרו "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה אִשֶּׁה לַה'" נראה שדבר אחר היה נתן מן הבהמה קרבן והאוכל חלבה יהיה חייב כרת כי אם היה עונה מאמר אשר יקריבו על החלב הקרב מן הבהמה היה ראוי לומר כי כל אוכל חלב אשר יקריבנו קרבן לה' לא שיאמר כי כל אוכל חלב מן הבהמה אשר יקריבו ממנה קרבן לה':
content.english: We have already awakened in the opening of this matter of ours that the Torah is built by means of prophecy according to the wisdom of expression, and according to the examination of the speech, the will of the speaker would be known, and it is necessary that the hearer of that speech to be understanding in a whisper, to understand its eloquence, as if he himself were the speaker of that speech, and in what thought he would be standing in taking out that speech. And if it is possible for one speech to be equal to many matters, it is impossible without addition and subtraction, according to the examination of that speech to the truth, and it is necessary for the examiner to be calm in spirit to receive whatever intention is proper for that speech, without leaning to one of the causes that lead astray, and then he would test the true matter from the false. And it is known that the fat came, its prohibition in the Scripture in two places, in the section of Vayikra, "a statute forever for your generations, in all your habitations, any fat and any blood, you shall not eat" (Lev 3:17), and in the section of Tzav, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat, you shall not eat" (Lev 7:23). And Israel were divided into three opinions in the matter of fat. Some of them say that the Scripture did not prohibit except the fat of holy offerings, not the fat of ordinary animals, that the fat of ordinary animals is permitted, and this is the religion of Mashvi the Akbari and those who follow him. And some of them say that the fat is three prohibited from the ordinary animals, which are the fat that covers on the innards and that which is on the innards and the fat of the kidneys, and this is the opinion of the rabbis. And some of them say that the fat prohibited from the ordinary animals is five from the cattle and the goat and six from the sheep, and this is the opinion of the Karaites. And however, in the beginning, it is proper to examine the Scriptures according to the meaning of the plain, and after that, to argue with Mashvi the Akbari, who permits the fat of ordinary animals, and after that, we will return our hands with those who prohibit the three alone, who are the rabbis. And we say that the Scripture said in the section of Vayikra, in the sealing of the section of the peace offerings, in the sacrifice of the goat, "And he shall offer from it his sacrifice, a fire offering to the Lord, the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards (Lev 3:14). And the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is on the loins; and the caul on the liver, on the kidneys he shall remove it" (Lev 3:15), and it said, "And the priest shall burn them on the altar, food of the fire offering for a pleasant aroma, all fat to the Lord" (Lev 3:16), and this statement includes all fat to the Lord, it is known that it is on the fat of holy offerings. After that, it said, "A statute forever for your generations, in all your habitations, any fat and any blood, you shall not eat" (Lev 3:17), and this statement does not answer on the fat of holy offerings, but on the fat of ordinary animals, for regarding the fat of holy offerings, it instructed in the statement, "all fat to the Lord," but in the statement, "any fat and any blood," it is in the prohibition of the fat of ordinary animals, and it prohibited the fat of ordinary animals because what is offered from their kind, the fat is given to the altar, and therefore, it was also concerned to prohibit the blood, because also the blood is given to the altar from those who are offered. And it instructed on the fat, saying in the section of Tzav, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat, you shall not eat" (Lev 7:23), and it said, "For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers from it a fire offering to the Lord" (Lev 7:25). And it instructed on the blood in the section of Acharei Mot, saying, "And I have given it to you on the altar, to atone for your souls, for it is the blood that shall atone for the soul" (Lev 17:11). And after it instructed that they are given on the altar, it instructed also their prohibition, adjacent, and if that is not the matter, but in the statement, "all fat," it does not answer except on the fat of holy offerings, what is the reason to instruct in the prohibition of eating them after it is given to the altar? And just as it did not concern to prohibit a limb from the limbs of the burnt offering, because they are given to the altar, so it would not be proper to instruct in the prohibition of eating the fat after it is burned, and not further, but after that, it said, "And any blood you shall not eat," to the native and to the stranger, and according to his words, it would answer the prohibition of blood also on the holy offerings alone, and it is known that also the blood of ordinary animals is in prohibition. Go and know, just as the blood is prohibited, whether from the holy offerings or from the ordinary animals, so the fat is prohibited, whether from the holy offerings or from the ordinary animals, and not further, but it said after that, "a statute forever for your generations, in all your habitations," and the fat of holy offerings is only in the chosen place, in the Temple, and what is the reason, "in all your habitations," it teaches that it does not allude except to the fat of ordinary animals. And in order to quiet the argument of every arguer, it did not say before, "any fat and any blood," and after that, to say, "a statute forever for your generations," to find the arguer a place to say that "in all your habitations" answers on the blood. And furthermore, it said, "a statute forever for your generations," and all this statement includes, whether the time of the house or the time of exile, and in the time of exile, there are no sacrifices to prohibit the fat of holy offerings. And what it intended in these statements came in the section of Tzav and explained and said, for the sake of the fat, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat," and it instructed that the fat is not prohibited except from these three kinds, because from these kinds, the fat is offered on the altar, as it said, "For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers from it a fire offering to the Lord and shall be cut off" (Lev 7:25). And there is to know that in this place, it mentioned punishment, and the Scripture would not punish unless it warned, if so, the warning is preceding in the verse, "Any fat and any blood, you shall not eat," and in the statement, "a statute forever for your generations, in all your habitations, any fat and any blood, you shall not eat" (Lev 3:17).

content.hebrew: סוף המאמר יותר טוב היה ראוי לומר כי כל אוכל חלב הקרב ונכרתה לא שיאמר כל חלב שור וכבש ועז ולא שיאמר "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב" וכו' ואם חלב הקרב יהא באסור לבד מה טעם "וְחֵלֶב נְבֵלָה וְחֵלֶב טְרֵפָה, יֵעָשֶׂה לְכָל-מְלָאכָה" (ויקרא ז, כד) כי אחרי שהנבלה והטרפה באסור גם חלבם באסור ומה בא הכתוב ללמד ואם מפני שחלב חולים בהתר שלא נדין שחלב נבלה בהתר על כן בא לאסרו זאת הכונה לא יחשבנה רק מי שדומה לאוכל עשב. אך לפי כונתנו יש לישב הענין כי בעבור שחלב חולים באסור והאוכל חייב כרת שלא נחשוב שחלב נבלה כיון שאינו בהתר להאכל משום נבלה האוכל חלב נבלה יהיה עובר משום אוכל נבלה ולא יהיה חייב כרת משום אוכל חלב על כן הזכירו כדי להכלילו בכרת אך במה שאמר "יֵעָשֶׂה לְכָל-מְלָאכָה; וְאָכֹל, לֹא תֹאכְלֻהוּ" (ויקרא ז, כד) כדי שלא נחמיר עליו מפני שחל אסור על אסור ונאמר כמו שיהיה אסור באכילה יהיה אסור במלאכה ואפשר לסבור כי על כן אמר "יֵעָשֶׂה לְכָל-מְלָאכָה" כדי שלא נכון כיון שנאסר באכילה יהיה אסור בהנאה. ויש לחוש אחרי שהחקירה הוציאתנו שהכונה בחלב חולים מה טעם להזכיר בזה המקום אסור חלב חולים ויש לתת הטעם בעבור שהחלב עקר הסכמתו לשומן הלבן כפי שהוא ידוע המכסה ואשר על הקרב וחלב שעל הכליות וכבר הורינו שהעלה באסור החלבים מפני שהם קרבים למזבח וגזרה שוה לכל הקרבים שאין אחד מהם יתר ועדוף מזולתו והואיל והשלשה האחרים שהם הכליות והיותרת והאליה לא יקראו חלב מצד הלשון אכן מן התורה ידענו שהסכימה שמות לדברים אשר אינם לפי תקון עקר הלשון כמו חטאת ואשם ושלמים ומלואים וכיוצא בהם וקרא גם את אלו השלשה חלבים כמו שנבאר בהכרעת דעת הרבנים כאלו תקן תקון לשון כי אחרי שפרטם קראם בשם חלב כאמרו כל חלב לה' וכבר תדע במה שנבאר בפירוש העריות כי השמות המוסכמות מן התורה ידמו אל השמות המוסכמות מצד הלשון בענין אחד כמו שיועילו שמות הלשון אחרי הסכמתם כן יועילו שמות התורה אחרי הסכמתם להודיע לאחרים חפצם וכל מקום שיאמר חלב אחרי שהוסכם על הששה מהסכמת התורה יהיה כולל ששה מן הכבש וחמשה מן הבקר והעז. אך שלא ימצא הטוען מקום לחלוק ולומר כי שם חלב אם הוסכם על זולת השלשה על הקדשים לבד תהיה ההסכמה אבל בחולים לא כן על כן הזכיר אסור חלב חולים בסמוך אל הקדשים במה שהיתה ההסכמה להקרא חלבי הקדשים שפרטם בשם חלב כאמרו "כָּל-חֵלֶב וְכָל-דָּם, לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ"  כי כמו שתהיה ההסכמה על הקדשים להקרא בשם חלב אמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם, בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם--כָּל-חֵלֶב וְכָל-דָּם, לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ" (ויקרא ג, יז) כן תהיה ההסכמה על החולים להקרא בשם חלב לא שיהיה זה מוקש מזה כי אין מקישין על שמות התורה על כן כשבא בפרשת צו ואמר "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז" (ויקרא ז, כג) שלא נסתפק כי אולי לא יהיה כולל הששה אמר עוד "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה אִשֶּׁה לַה'" (ויקרא ז, כה) לבאר שחלבי חולים כמו חלבי קדשים שהם הששה והחמשה ועל כן פרט שמות המינים מפני שאינם שוים באסור החלבים:
content.english: The end of the matter, more good would be proper to say, "For whoever eats fat that is offered, and he shall be cut off," not that it would say, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat," and not that it would say, "For whoever eats fat" etc. And if the fat that is offered would be in prohibition alone, what is the reason, "And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a torn animal may be used for any work" (Lev 7:24), for after the carcass and the torn animal are in prohibition, also their fat is in prohibition, and what did the Scripture come to teach? And if because the fat of ordinary animals is permitted, so that we would not judge that the fat of a carcass is permitted, this intention would not be thought except by one who eats vegetation. But according to our intention, there is to settle the matter, for because the fat of ordinary animals is in prohibition, and one who eats it is liable to the punishment of excision, so that we would not think that the fat of a carcass, since it is not permitted to be eaten because of carcass, one who eats the fat of a carcass would be transgressing because of eating a carcass and would not be liable to excision because of eating fat, therefore it mentioned it in order to include it in excision. But in what it said, "may be used for any work; and you shall in no way eat it" (Lev 7:24), so that we would not be stringent on it because a prohibition falls on a prohibition and we would say, just as it would be prohibited in eating, it would be prohibited in work, and it is possible to think that therefore it said, "may be used for any work," so that we would not intend, since it was prohibited in eating, it would be prohibited in benefit. And there is to be concerned, after investigation brought us out that the intention is in the fat of ordinary animals, what is the reason to mention in this place the prohibition of the fat of ordinary animals? And there is to give the reason, because the fat, the essence of its agreement is for the white fat, as it is known, that covers and that is on the innards and the fat that is on the kidneys, and we have already instructed that the reason in the prohibition of the fat is because they are offered to the altar, and a decree equal to all those that are offered, that there is not one of them extra and additional above its fellow. And since the other three, which are the kidneys and the caul and the tail, are not called fat from the side of the language, however, from the Torah, we knew that it agreed names to things that are not according to the correction of the essence of the language, like sin offering and guilt offering and peace offering and consecrations and the like. And it called also these three fat, as we will explain in the decision of the opinion of the rabbis, as if it corrected a correction of language, for after it detailed them, it called them by the name of fat, as it said, "all fat to the Lord." And you already know in what we will explain in the interpretation of the prohibited sexual relations, that the names agreed-upon from the Torah resemble the names agreed-upon from the side of the language in one matter, as the names of the language help after their agreement, so the names of the Torah help after their agreement to inform to others their desire. And every place where it says fat, after it was agreed upon the six from the agreement of the Torah, it would include six from the sheep and five from the cattle and the goat. But so that the arguer should not find a place to argue and say that the name of fat, if it was agreed upon besides the three, on the holy offerings alone would be the agreement, but in ordinary animals, not so. Therefore, it mentioned the prohibition of the fat of ordinary animals adjacent to the holy offerings in what the agreement was for the holy offerings to be called fat, as it said, "Any fat and any blood, you shall not eat," for as would be the agreement on the holy offerings to be called by the name of fat, it said, "a statute forever for your generations, in all your habitations, any fat and any blood, you shall not eat" (Lev 3:17), so would be the agreement on the ordinary animals to be called by the name of fat. Not that this would be analogized from this, for one does not analogize on the names of the Torah. Therefore, when it came in the section of Tzav and said, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat" (Lev 7:23), so that we would not doubt that perhaps it would not include the six, it said further, "For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers from it a fire offering to the Lord" (Lev 7:25), to explain that the fat of ordinary animals is like the fat of holy offerings, which are the six and the five. And therefore, it specified the names of the kinds, because they are not equal in the prohibition of the fat.

content.hebrew: פרק עשרים
content.english: Twentieth Chapter

content.hebrew: אמנם מה שנסתפק משוי העכברי והתיר חלבי חולים הוא משלש ספקות. האחת מפני שאמר הכתוב "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה אִשֶּׁה לַה'" (ויקרא ז, כה) ואמר כי לא דבר הכתוב זה המאמר אלא כדי לאסור חלבי הקדשים לבד. ובטל רבינו יוסף הקרקסאני נ"ע זה המאמר כי באמרו "מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה" טעמו ממין הבהמה לא מן הבהמה עצמה כמוהו שאמר הכתוב "וְאִם-בְּהֵמָה--אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קָרְבָּן, לַה':  כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יִתֵּן מִמֶּנּוּ לַה', יִהְיֶה-קֹּדֶשׁ" (ויקרא כז, ט) והטעם ממין הבהמה ודקדקו החכמים בזה כי אחרי ששם בהמה בכלל ובפרט שתי הכונות יתכנו לה אם בכלל ואם בפרט זולתי שיש ראיה להסגיל אחת משתי הכונות ולולי הראיה אשר הסגילה מאמר "וְאִם-בְּהֵמָה--אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קָרְבָּן, לַה'" (ויקרא כז, ט) היינו לוקחים אותו על הפרט כמו שהיינו לוקחים אותו על הכלל אלא אחרי שאמר "וְאִם-הָמֵר יָמִיר בְּהֵמָה בִּבְהֵמָה" (ויקרא כז, י) הורה כי ענינו על הכלל ולא על הפרט ואמנם בפסוק "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה" כמו שיסבול הפרט כן יסבול הכלל אמנם להסגילו על הכלל מפני שאמר מקודם לכן "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז" והוא כולל לחולים ולקדשים. אכן יש לטוען שיטעון אמת שמאמר "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז" כלל ויהיה האוכל חלב חולים עובר בלאו אבל מאמר "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה" יהיה מרמיז לחלב הקדשים שיהיה חייב כרת אכן לא יצדק הטוען בעבור שאנחנו אמרנו שזה המאמר סובל שתי אמתות וחוב לקחת את שתיהן בעוד שלא תמצא ראיה להסגיל אחת משתי האמתות עכ"ז בעזרת השם במה שהקדמנו מן הפירושים נראה הענין כי לא כון הכתוב בזה המקום כי אם לחולין כפי שנראה מעצם הפסוק שהרי בארנו כי אם היה רצונו לאסור חלב הקדשים בלבד היה  לו לומר כי כל אוכל חלב הקרב או שיאמר כי כל אוכל חלב מן הבהמה אשר יקריבנו אשה לה' כי החלה עצמו נתן אשה. ואיך יכון המאמר "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה אִשֶּׁה לַה'" כנראה שדבר אחר זולתי החלב נתן מן הבהמה אשה לה' לא החלב עצמו כי מלת "יַקְרִיב" מקרה וצריך לעצם נושא מקרה ההקרבה וכיון שקדם העצם ר"ל החלב היה ראוי להשיא מקרה ההקרבה אליו כי מלת "אִשֶּׁה" גם היא תואר ואם לא היה מזכיר העצם היה המקרה נשוא על התואר אלא כיון שהזכיר העצם צריך מקרה הפעולה והתואר שיהיו נשואים על העצם וכיון שאמר "מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה" ועוד אמר "אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב מִמֶּנָּה" והורה לשני עצמים ולא יסבול הענין היות שניהם שבים לעצם אחד אבל הראוי לומר שמאמר "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה" רוצה המין כגון שאמר "מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, מִן-הַבָּקָר וּמִן-הַצֹּאן" וכבר קדם לנו כי לא היה ראוי לאסור חלב הקרב כמו שלא יאסור דבר מן העולה: ספקה אחרת למשוי. שהכתוב אמר "וְחֵלֶב נְבֵלָה וְחֵלֶב טְרֵפָה" וכו' (ויקרא ז, כד) וזה יחייב התר חלב זולתו שאינו נבלה ולא טרפה וזאת ראיה בטלה כי יש להקשות עליו ואלמלא לא אמר "וְחֵלֶב נְבֵלָה" מאיזה כח היה לנו בהתר לאכול חלב הנבלה הלא היינו אוסרים אותו כשאר גוף הנבלה שגם החלב הוא נבלה אבל לאיזה אופן הזכירו כיון שהוא אסור כבר קדם לנו הפירוש בו. ועוד שאם היה חפצו לאסור מה טעם מאמר "יֵעָשֶׂה לְכָל-מְלָאכָה" (ויקרא ז, כד): ספקה אחרת למשוי. משום כשהתיר בשר תאוה הזכיר אסור הדם לבד ולא הזכיר חלבו ולוא היה החלב אסור היה מזכיר אסורו. והתשובה בשכבר הזכיר אסור החלב באלו הפרשיות בפרשת ויקרא ובפרשת צו אמנם הזכיר בפרשת ראה אסור הדם לבד בעבור כי ישראל היו במדבר נזהרים מלאכול חולים והיו אוכלים זבחיהם שלמים כדי שלא ישפך הדם בחוץ רק במזבח וכשבאו ישראל לארץ והתיר להם לאכול חולים ורצה להזכיר שדמו ישפך בחוץ ובעבור שהיה הצורך כדי להזכיר שפיכת הדם על הארץ שאינו צריך מזבח הוצרך להזכיר גם כן אסורו ועל כן הזכיר אסור הדם לבדו באמרו "רַק הַדָּם, לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ:  עַל-הָאָרֶץ תִּשְׁפְּכֶנּוּ, כַּמָּיִם" (דברים יב, טז) ועל כן לא הוצרך להזכיר אסור החלב בשכבר הזכיר אסורו בפרשיות ויקרא וצו. ואולם במה שעזר אב"ן עזרא הרבן אחרי משוי העכברי להתיר חלב חולים מדין תורה באמור כיון שהזכיר אסור החלב בפרשיות הקדשים מכלל שהחלב אינו אסור רק מן הקדשים. כבר אנחנו הזכרנו העלה אשר הכריחה להזכיר אסור חלב חולים בתוך הקדשים ובארנו שבהכרח הוא חלב חולים מה שאין לנו צורך לשנות המאמרים. אמנם מה שפירש במה שנאמר "כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל" (דברים יב, טו) שאומר כי לא דמה הכתוב בשר חולים "כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל" אלא בעבור שצבי ואיל חלבם מותר להיות החולים חלבם מותר ודין היה לו להבין כי לא דמהו הכתוב "כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל" אלא בעבור שאמר "הַטָּמֵא וְהַטָּהוֹר, יַחְדָּו,  יֹאכְלֶנּוּ" (דברים יב, כב) בעבור שבמדבר לא התיר להם בשר חולים כי אם בשר שלמים והזהיר שלא יאכלנו טמא עתה אחרי שהתיר בשר תאוה הצרך לבאר ש"הַטָּמֵא, וְהַטָּהוֹר, יַחְדָּו, יֹאכְלֶנּוּ" שלא תהיה מניעה לטמא מלאכול כמו שבשר צבי ואיל נאכל לטמא ולטהור ואין הדמיון שוה בכל עניניו והלא זה דמו מכוסה וזה נשפך על הארץ ואם יאמר שזה נתבאר אבל בשאר עניניו יהיה דומה כבר התורה חייבה נתינת הזרוע והלחיים והקיבה מן הבהמה הטהורה ואינם חייבים לתתם מן צבי ואיל ולא די לו שדבריו כחרש הנשבר אלא התהלל שחלק עם קראי אחד ונצחו עד שחזר אותו הקראי ופצו שפתיו שבועה להסמך בדברי בעלי הקבלה מן העת ההיא. וצריך להעיר לענין השאלה ותשובת זה האיש. וזאת היא השאלה האליה אסורה מן התורה אם לא. ויען ויאמר אב"ן עזרא אמת כי האליה תקרא בשם חלב אבל רבותיו התירוה ואסרו כל חלב דעתו בזה שהחלב אסור מדברי קבלה וזה שקר גמור כי רבותיו מה שאסרו לא אסרוהו רק מן התורה כאמרם בתורת כהנים אסור החלב ממאמר "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה, אֲשֶׁר יַקְרִיב{{fn:51}} מִמֶּנָּה" אין לי אלא חלב תמימים הראויים ליקרב חלב בעלי מומין מנין תלמוד לומר מן הבהמה ואין לי אלא חלב קדשים חלב חולים מנין תלמוד לומר כי כל אוכל חלב אם כן למה נאמר אשר יקריבו ללמד שדוקא חלב שכמותו כשר ליקרב אסרתי לך יצא חלב שעל הדפנות נראה כי מה שאסרו הם לא אסרוהו רק מכח התורה ואמר כי האליה תקרא חלב ובטל דברי רבותיו שאינם מסכימים כי האליה תקרא חלב. ועוד שהם לא התירוה מן ההעתקה אלא כפי דעתם מכח התורה כאשר אמרו באמור הכתוב "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז" דבר שהוא שוה לשלשתם והאליה היא אסורה מן הכבש לבד ונראה כי מה שחשב על אלו האנשים בטענתו כלו הפך דבריהם. אז ענה הקראי ואמר הלא כל חלב אסור מן התורה שנאמר "כָּל-חֵלֶב וְכָל-דָּם, לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ" והראיה על זה שאמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם, בְּכֹל מוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם" ודעתו בזה כיון שאמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם" כנראה שיהיה אסור בגלות. השיב בן עזרא ואמר שהוא דבק לאסור חלב קדשים וטען שמאמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם" אין ראיה שכולל זמן הגלות כשאין קדשים והביא דמיון מן "וְלֶחֶם וְקָלִי וְכַרְמֶל לֹא תֹאכְלוּ, עַד-עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה--עַד הֲבִיאֲכֶם, אֶת-קָרְבַּן אֱלֹהֵיכֶם:  חֻקַּת עוֹלָם לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶם, בְּכֹל מֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם" (ויקרא כג, יד) ואומר שזה אינו כולל זמן הגלות כי אלו היה כלל זמן הגלות לא היה ראוי לאכול לחם כי לא הקרבנו עומר. ודין היה לו לעיין שמאמר "בְּכֹל מֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם" טענה גדולה שאינו רוצה על חלב קדשים רק על חלב חולים כי חלב קדשים אינו נמצא בכל המושבות רק חלב חולים הוא הנמצא בכל המושבות. ומה שאמר במאמר "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם" על הכתוב בעומר שהוא על זמן הבית ולא על זמן הגלות לא דבר נכונה שחקת עולם דבק במניעת האכילה לא בהבאת הקרבן והכתוב תלה מניעת האכילה לשתי סבות באמרו "עַד-עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" ואמר "עַד הֲבִיאֲכֶם" ונתן הזמן והקרבן כי בזמן הבית היה בחיוב הזמן והקרבן ובזמן הגלות יחייב הזמן לבד. והנה יהיה "חֻקַּת עוֹלָם" מתמיד ולא נאכל לחם מן החדש עד זמן הספירה שנאמר "וְלֶחֶם וְקָלִי וְכַרְמֶל לֹא תֹאכְלוּ, עַד-עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" (ויקרא כג, יד) הוא הדין באסור החלב. אחרי כן ענה הקראי שהכתוב "כָּל-חֵלֶב שׁוֹר וְכֶשֶׂב, וָעֵז" (ויקרא ז, כג) כולל חלב חולים. והשיב בן עזרא שגם זה דבק עם חלב זבח השלמים והעד "כִּי, כָּל-אֹכֵל חֵלֶב, מִן-הַבְּהֵמָה" וגו' (ויקרא ז, כה) להוציא חלב כל בשר שאינו קרב לשלמים והנה סתר דברי רבותיו שהם כוללים השלשה לבד מחלב חולים והוא מכליל כלם בחלבי השלמים והביא "וְחֵלֶב נְבֵלָה וְחֵלֶב טְרֵפָה" (ויקרא ז, כד) ומה שכתוב בבשר תאוה "כַּצְּבִי וְכָאַיָּל" וכל ראיותיו הפוכות כמו שבארנו. ובסוף אמר אז פקח הצדוקי את עיניו ופצו שפתיו שבועה שלא יסמך על דעתו בפירוש המצות רק ישען על העתקת הפירושים. ותמיה אני לאותו הקראי איך חזר מפני דברים שהם בנויים על תוהו לא לפירוש בעלי הקבלה ולא לפירוש בעלי מקרא שאם עמד כנגד דעת הקראים עוד לא הסכים לדעת רבותיו במה שפירשו מדין תורה לפי דעתם אלא החליף דעתם וסתר פירושיהם ואיך השלים הקראי להיות רבן בדברים בטלים שלא זכה אותם בחלוקתו ומאיזה כח ומאיזה הכרח ודין היה לו ללכת לפי דעת משוי העכברי אחרי שהודה שדברי בעלי הקבלה הפך דעת כונת התורה ואנחנו כיד אלהינו הטובה עלינו סתרנו ובטלנו דברי משוי וכל ההולכים אחריו כי כל דבריהם לא יועילו כי תוהו המה:
content.english: However, in what Mashvi the Akbari doubted and permitted the fat of ordinary animals, it is from three doubts. The first, because it said, the Scripture, "For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers from it a fire offering to the Lord" (Lev 7:25), and it said that the Scripture did not speak this statement but to prohibit the fat of holy offerings alone. And Rabbi Joseph the Kirkisani, may he rest in peace, nullified this statement, for in its saying, "from the animal," its meaning is from the kind of animal, not from the animal itself, like it, that the Scripture said, "And if an animal, from which they offer from it a sacrifice to the Lord; all that he gives from it to the Lord shall be holy" (Lev 27:9), and the meaning is from the kind of animal, and the sages were precise in this, for after the name of animal is in general and in particular, the two intentions would be possible for it, whether in general or whether in particular, except that there would be evidence to establish one of the two intentions, and without the evidence that established it, the statement, "And if an animal, from which they offer from it a sacrifice to the Lord" (Lev 27:9), we would be taking it on the particular, as we would be taking it on the general, but after it said, "If he shall exchange, animal for animal" (Lev 27:10), it instructed that its matter is on the general and not on the particular. And indeed, in the verse, "For whoever eats fat from the animal," just as it would bear the particular, so it would bear the general, but to establish it on the general, because it said before, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat," and it includes ordinary animals and holy offerings. However, there is for the arguer to argue, it is true that the statement, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat," included, and one who eats the fat of ordinary animals would be transgressing a negative commandment, but the statement, "For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers from it," would be alluding to the fat of the holy offerings, that one who eats it would be liable to excision. But there is to answer that we have said that this statement bears two truths, and there is an obligation to take both of them, as long as you do not find evidence to establish one of the two truths. Nevertheless, with the help of the Lord, in what we introduced from the explanations, it appears the matter that the Scripture did not intend in this place except for ordinary animals, as it appears from the essence of the verse, for if its intention would be to prohibit the fat of holy offerings alone, it would be for it to say, "For whoever eats fat that is offered," or to say, "For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers it, a fire offering to the Lord," for the fat itself was given as a fire offering. And how would the statement, "For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers from it a fire offering to the Lord," be aimed, it appears that another thing besides the fat was given from the animal as a fire offering to the Lord, not the fat itself, for the word "offers" is an incident, and it needs an essence that is the subject of the incident of the offering, and since the essence preceded, meaning the fat, it would be proper to attribute the incident of the offering to it, for the word "a fire offering" is also an attribute, and if it would not be mentioning the essence, the incident would be attributed to the attribute, but since it mentioned the essence, it is necessary that the incident of the action and the attribute be attributed to the essence. And since it said, "from the animal," and further said, "from which he offers from it," and it indicated to two essences, and the matter would not bear for both of them to return to one essence, but the proper thing to say is that the statement, "For whoever eats fat from the animal," wants the kind, such as it said, "from the animal, from the cattle, and from the flock" (Lev 1:2), and we have already preceded ourselves that it would not be proper to prohibit the fat that is offered, just as it would not prohibit anything from the burnt offering. Another doubt for Mashvi. That the Scripture said, "And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a torn animal" etc. (Lev 7:24), and this would oblige the permitting of fat besides it that is not a carcass and not a torn animal. And this proof is nullified, for there is to object to him, and if it would not say, "And the fat of a carcass," from what power would it be for us in permitting to eat the fat of the carcass? Is it not that we would have been prohibiting it like the rest of the body of the carcass, that also the fat is a carcass? But for what form did it mention it, since it is already prohibited? The explanation in it has already preceded us. Furthermore, if its desire would be to prohibit, what is the reason for the statement, "may be used for any work" (Lev 7:24)? Another doubt for Mashvi. Because when it permitted the meat of desire, it mentioned the prohibition of the blood alone and did not mention its fat, and if the fat would be prohibited, it would mention its prohibition. And the answer is that it already mentioned the prohibition of the fat in these sections in the section of Vayikra and in the section of Tzav. However, it mentioned in the section of Re'eh the prohibition of the blood alone, because Israel were in the wilderness, cautious from eating ordinary animals, and they were eating their sacrifices as peace offerings so that the blood would not be poured outside, but on the altar. And when Israel came to the land, and it permitted them to eat ordinary animals, and it wanted to mention that its blood would be poured outside, and because the need was to mention the pouring of the blood on the earth, that it does not need an altar, it needed to mention also its prohibition. And therefore, it mentioned the prohibition of the blood alone, saying, "Only the blood you shall not eat; on the earth you shall pour it out like water" (Deut 12:16), and therefore, it did not need to mention the prohibition of the fat, for it had already mentioned its prohibition in the sections of Vayikra and Tzav. And however, in what Ibn Ezra helped the rabbin after Mashvi the Akbari to permit the fat of ordinary animals from the law of the Torah, saying that since it mentioned the prohibition of the fat in the sections of the holy offerings, it implies that the fat is not prohibited except from the holy offerings. We have already mentioned the reason that compelled to mention the prohibition of the fat of ordinary animals inside the holy offerings, and we have explained that necessarily, it is the fat of ordinary animals, what we do not have a need to change the statements. However, what he interpreted in what it says, "as of the gazelle and as of the deer" (Deut 12:15), who says that the Scripture did not compare the meat of ordinary animals "as of the gazelle and as of the deer" except because the gazelle and deer, their fat is permitted, for the ordinary animals to be their fat permitted. And law would be for him to understand that the Scripture did not compare it "as of the gazelle and as of the deer" except because it said, "The unclean and the clean together may eat it" (Deut 12:22), because in the wilderness, it did not permit them the meat of ordinary animals except the meat of peace offerings, and it warned that the unclean should not eat it. Now, after it permitted the meat of desire, it needed to explain that "the unclean and the clean together may eat it," that there would not be a prevention for the unclean from eating, just as the meat of a gazelle and a deer is eaten for the unclean and the clean, and the comparison is not equal in all its matters. And is it not that this, its blood is covered, and this is poured on the earth? And if it says that this was explained, but in the rest of its matters, it would be similar, the Torah already obligated giving the foreleg and the jaws and the stomach from the pure animal, and they are not obligated to give them from the gazelle and deer, and it was not enough for him that his words are like broken pottery, but he boasted that he argued with a certain Karaite and defeated him, until that Karaite returned and his lips uttered an oath to rely on the words of the Rabbanites from that time. And it is necessary to awaken to the matter of the question and answer of this person. And this is the question: Is the tail prohibited from the Torah or not? And Ibn Ezra answered and said, it is true that the tail is called by the name of fat, but his teachers permitted it and prohibited all fat. His opinion in this is that the fat is prohibited from the words of a tradition, and this is a complete lie, for his teachers, what they prohibited, they did not prohibit it except from the Torah, as they say in the Sifra [Torat Kohanim], "The prohibition of the fat is from the statement, 'For whoever eats fat from the animal, from which he offers' (Lev 7:25). I have only the fat of unblemished ones who are proper to be offered, the fat of blemished ones from where? It is taught to say, 'from the animal.' And I have only the fat of holy offerings, the fat of ordinary animals from where? It is taught to say, 'For whoever eats fat.' If so, why is it said, 'from which they offer?' To teach that particularly fat, the like of which is proper to be offered, I prohibited to you. The fat that is on the sides is excluded." It appears that what they prohibited, they did not prohibit it except from the power of the Torah. And he said that the tail is called fat, and he nullified the words of his teachers, who do not agree that the tail is called fat. Furthermore, they did not permit it from the tradition, but according to their opinion, from the power of the Torah, as they said in the Scripture saying, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat," a thing that is equal to the three of them, and the tail is prohibited from the sheep alone. And it appears that what he thought about these people in his argument, all of it is the opposite of their words. Then the Karaite answered and said, is not all fat prohibited from the Torah, as it says, "Any fat and any blood, you shall not eat" (Lev 3:17)? And the proof on this is that it said, "a statute forever for your generations, in all your habitations," and his intention in this is that since it said, "a statute forever for your generations," it appears that it would be prohibited in exile. Ibn Ezra replied and said that it is attached to prohibit the fat of holy offerings, and he argued that the statement, "a statute forever," is no proof that it includes the time of exile, when there are no holy offerings, and he brought an analogy from, "And bread and roasted grain and fresh ears you shall not eat, until this very day, until you bring the offering of your God; it is a statute forever for your generations, in all your habitations" (Lev 23:14), and he says that this does not include the time of exile, for if it included the time of exile, it would not be proper to eat bread, for we did not offer an omer. And law would be for him to examine that the statement, "in all your habitations," is a great argument that it does not intend on the fat of holy offerings, but on the fat of ordinary animals, for the fat of holy offerings is not found in all the habitations, only the fat of ordinary animals is the one found in all the habitations. And what he said in the statement, "a statute forever," on the Scripture in the omer, that it is in the time of the house and not in the time of exile, he did not speak correctly, for "a statute forever" is attached to the prevention of eating, not in the bringing of the offering, and the Scripture hung the prevention of eating on two reasons, saying, "until this very day," and it said, "until you bring," and it gave the time and the offering, for in the time of the house, it would be in the obligation of the time and the offering, and in the time of exile, the time would obligate alone. And so it would be "a statute forever," continuous, and we would not eat bread from the new until the time of the counting, as it says, "And bread and roasted grain and fresh ears you shall not eat, until this very day" (Lev 23:14), the same rule in the prohibition of the fat. After that, the Karaite answered that the Scripture, "Any fat of a bull and a lamb and a goat" (Lev 7:23), includes the fat of ordinary animals. And Ibn Ezra replied that this also is attached with the fat of the sacrifice of peace offerings, and the evidence, "For whoever eats fat from the animal" etc. (Lev 7:25), to exclude the fat of all flesh that is not offered to peace offerings. And so it contradicted the words of his teachers, who include the three alone from the fat of ordinary animals, and he includes all of them in the fat of the peace offerings, and he brought "And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a torn animal" (Lev 7:24), and what is written in the meat of desire, "as of the gazelle and as of the deer," and all his proofs are the opposite, as we have explained. And in the end he said, then the Sadducee opened his eyes and his lips uttered an oath that he would not rely on his opinion in the interpretation of the commandments, but he would lean on the tradition of the interpretations. And I wonder about that Karaite, how did he return because of words that are built on emptiness, not for the interpretation of the Rabbanites and not for the interpretation of the Mikra'ites, for if he stood against the opinion of the Karaites, he still did not agree to the opinion of his teachers in what they interpreted from the law of the Torah, according to their opinion, but he exchanged their opinion and contradicted their interpretations, and how did the Karaite complete to be his teacher in vain words that did not merit them in his division, and from what power and from what necessity and law would be for him to go according to the opinion of Mashvi the Akbari, after he admitted that the words of the Rabbanites are the opposite of the opinion of the intention of the Torah? And we, with the good hand of our God upon us, contradicted and nullified the words of Mashvi and all who go after him, for all their words do not help, for they are emptiness.
content.comments: 51 יַקְרִיב — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "for whoever eats fat of the beast from which they offer," whereas the verse as cited (Lev 7:25) reads: "for whoever eats fat of the beast from which one offers." Similarly in several other instances in this chapter.
