And it said that the bet in "not at the time" is a bet of help, and it said, "If a woman has a discharge of blood" (Lev 15:25), and it did not say "and if she has a discharge" because it joins it to "a woman has a discharge," and it means that if the woman sees the blood of menstruation and has a discharge of blood for many days with not the time of her menstrual impurity, that is, the beginning of the eighth, and they are called many days with this time, as it says, "lest he add to his beating above this with many blows," not that if he hit him once more, it is many blows, but the meaning is with those forty, they would be many blows, and so too in saying many days, for the sage did not intend the time of the eighth to be many days, but with the days of the seven, and it said, "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity," if the blood stopped and was renewed at the beginning of the eighth. And what they agreed upon, that the blood should be at the beginning of the eighth, that if she rose pure from the time of immersion, she would not be a woman with a discharge but a menstruating woman because if it goes out of that time, there is no reason for it to stand on a border, and it said, how is it possible that she immersed and rose pure and touched holy things, and afterward she saw blood? How would she be a woman with a discharge, and the things she touched would be pure? In short, this sage does not see there being a time of purity between a menstruating woman and a woman with a discharge. And the sage Rabbi Joseph said that all the Karaites did not differ regarding one whose blood touched on the eighth and on the seventh, but she is a woman with a discharge according to the revelation from the statement "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity," but if she sees on the eighth after her blood was cut off on the seventh, it is under the advice and the investigation, whether we should go to what the investigation would yield, or whether we should take the matter strongly to be stringent, but in the statement "not at the time of her menstrual impurity," even though the sages disagreed, for he did not find a fitting reason and did not find a condition added to the statement "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity." And it seems to me that the scripture indicated a matter that we would not have understood if it had not mentioned it, and it is that just as the scripture judged that the first blood of menstruation is different from the second, and it said, "She shall be in her menstrual impurity seven days," we would also judge if the woman sees blood other than the seven, perhaps there would be an excess for the first over the second. Therefore, it said "for many days," that all of it is in one law, between the first and the second and the third. Therefore, it said "for many days," except for the eighth day only, she would not be a woman with a discharge. Therefore, it said, "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity," whether on one day after her menstrual impurity or on many days, she is a woman with a discharge. And Rabbi Joseph, of blessed memory, said, just as the Karaites discarded one condition, which is "not at the time of her menstrual impurity," so the rabbis discarded one condition, which is "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity," because they say eleven days between a menstruating woman and the beginning of a menstruating woman is a law given to Moses at Sinai, because they did not indicate this in the sight of the scripture, until they spoke strange words, and they say, days—two, many—three, and if she sees in these three consecutive days, she is a woman with a major discharge, and she is obligated in seven clean days and a sacrifice, but if she sees for one day or two days, she is a woman with a minor discharge, and she keeps one day only. If she saw on the eighth, she keeps the ninth; if she saw on the eighth and the ninth, she keeps the tenth; if she saw on the eighth and the ninth and the tenth, she counts seven clean days and is obligated in a sacrifice, until they said that these are many days after the time of menstruation, which is not the time of her menstrual impurity. Say on the eighth, on the ninth, on the tenth, these are many days, and she is a woman with a major discharge, and she counts seven clean days, and this is a woman with a discharge consecutive to a menstruating woman. If she saw on the eleventh, it is the beginning of menstruation. But they said, "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity" is when she saw on the ninth of her menstruation and is separated from her menstruation by one day. Therefore, they said eleven days between a menstruating woman and a menstruating woman. And these are things, the import of the scripture does not indicate them in any way. To conclude the matter, their view in the statement "not at the time of her menstrual impurity" is on the eleven days between a menstruating woman and a menstruating woman, which is the time of a discharge, and this is if she saw on the twelfth day, she is at the beginning of menstruation, and if she sees in these days three consecutive days, she is a woman with a major discharge and is obligated in seven clean days and a sacrifice, and if one day or two days, she keeps one day and immerses and emerges to purity and does not need a sacrifice, with strange interpretations, and this is in tradition for them, as they say, and it is not from the force of the scripture, but on the contrary, the scripture stands against them. And our sages, of blessed memory, said, if their statement were true for eleven days, we would also do it, but after their tradition is not true, and furthermore, there is a contradiction in the scripture. Therefore, we have returned to what is appropriate from the force of the scripture. And the rabbis themselves have returned from what the Torah decreed and from what they have in tradition, and they have made all women to be in the presumption of women with discharges, who count seven clean days, and they do not have a menstruating woman or a woman with a minor discharge according to their law, and they are transgressing the statement, "You shall not add to the thing which I command you, nor take away from it" (Deut 4:2). But according to the view of the Karaite sages who follow the plain meaning of the scripture from all the intentions that we have explained, the statement that is close on the two things which the Torah has conditioned "for many days," "not at the time of her menstrual impurity," "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity," that the statement "or if it runs beyond her menstrual impurity" is also not at the time of her menstrual impurity. But we have explained, between whether she will have a discharge for many days and the blood is the first blood, that she will have a discharge beyond her menstrual impurity, it is under one law, and the scripture came to distinguish that her law is not like the law of a menstruating woman, who from the first seeing counts seven days, and there is no difference between the seeing of the first day over the seeing of many days, for when the blood stops, she counts seven clean days, as it says, "And if she is cleansed of her discharge, then she shall count for herself seven days" etc. (Lev 15:28). Therefore, the Torah said two things. However, the law of a discharge in its beginning is in one matter, that is, on the eighth day. But the division of the sages is whether the seeing would be in the beginning of the eighth, which touches on the seventh, or whether it would be the entire eighth day. However, what she saw at the beginning of the eighth, whether the bloods of the eighth are attached to the bloods of the seventh or whether the bloods of the seventh are attached to the time of the eighth, there is no division among the sages, that she is a woman with a discharge. However, the division is that after the beginning of the eighth has passed, what she sees the entire eighth day, whether she is a woman with a discharge or a menstruating woman, and we have already explained the decisions between the two groups, and we do not need to repeat them. However, what we have to explain is the law of the priest Rabbi Sahl, of blessed memory, is more appropriate that it would be attached to the blood of the seventh, and the difference between them is that what she sees after the beginning of the eighth has passed, the law of the priest is that it is the blood of menstruation, and one who touches it is unclean for seven days, and she is a menstruating woman and does not count seven clean days. And the Levite says that what she sees the entire eighth day, she is a woman with a discharge, and one who touches it will be unclean for a day, and she counts seven clean days. And I saw that Rabbi Toviah the Translator, of blessed memory, related that they were conducting themselves until his time according to the view of the Levite, and the view of the priest seemed to him more appropriate. And I saw that to Rabbi Aaron, of blessed memory, the view of the Levite seemed to him. However, he related that the people were conducting themselves in a custom other than the two views, for as long as the woman did not immerse, even until the ninth day, and she saw blood, she would be a woman with a discharge, and this is not the law of the Torah, for immersion does not distinguish between a menstruating woman and a woman with a discharge, and according to the view of the priest, it was only at the time when she needs immersion, which is the end of the seventh day, whether she immersed or did not immerse, after that time has passed, she is a menstruating woman and not a woman with a discharge. And what is appropriate to rule, since the matter is in doubt, is to put upon her the stringencies of a menstruating woman and the stringencies of a woman with a discharge. What she sees the entire eighth day, she washes from the first blood that she sees on the eighth, for as long as she does not wash from it, she would be unclean from the time of touching, with the impurity of seven days, and to put upon her the counting of seven clean days according to the law of a woman with a discharge, to take the matter stringently; thus I saw that Levi ben Japhet judged. And Rabbi Joseph the Seer, of blessed memory, said, and happy is one who is stringent. And he said, "All the days of the discharge of her uncleanness shall be as the days of her impurity. She is unclean." Since one who is counting has seven clean days, she is comparable in the stringency of the impurity, not in days, that is, that she makes a bed and a seat and a saddle unclean, and they make others unclean, and she needs seven clean days, and afterward she is cleansed and her cleansing is with running water according to the statute of the person with a discharge, and there is one comparison for all severe impurity, for just as it was silent about the woman with a discharge regarding her purification and relied on what was explained about the person with a discharge, so it was silent about the menstruating woman and relied on comparing her to the person with a discharge.

content.hebrew: פרק שמיני
content.english: Chapter Eight

content.hebrew: היולדת הכלילה הכתוב במשפט טמאת הנדה שנאמר "כִּימֵי נִדַּת דְּוֺתָהּ תִּטְמָא" (ויקרא יב, ב) ואין טמאתה מפני הדם שרואה עם הנדה רק מפני הלידה שהרי טמאה הכתוב שבועים לנקבה ואשר יקרה ותטמא האשה קודם הלידה ביום ויומים ותחלת השבעה והשבועים מעת הלידה לא מעת שראתה דם. ומי שאומר כי לא מצאנו יולדת מבלי דם ואפשר שתהיה טמאה מפני הדם ומפני הלידה כבר הראינו שיחות זה המאמר ועוד כבר סופר על משפחת דורקטי שאין על הנשים דם בתולים ודם נדה ודם לידה. ומה שראוי לפסוק על דעת מי שאומר כי דם ראשון מטמא שבעה תטמא המילדת טמאת שבעה כל עוד שלא תראה דם קודם הלידה אלא אם תראה דם קודם הלידה תטמא המילדת יום אחד ואשרי המחמיר. ילדה בעוד שהיא נדה אין לה אחרי השלים זמן נדותה זמן זיבות שהרי נעתקה ממשפט הנדה למשפט היולדת ואחרי שבעה לזכר ושבועים לנקבה דן אותם הכתוב בדמי טוהר ואין לה זמן זיבות ואם לא פסק הדם ביום ארבעים ואחד וביום שמונים ואחד צריך לדין שהיא נדה והדם שראתה ביום ארבעים ואחד וביום שמונים ואחד הוא דם ראשון ומטמא טמאת שבעה הוא הדין אם לא ראתה דם קודם הלידה וראתה ביום ארבעים ואחד וביום שמונים ואחד היא נדה כי הזיבות לא תהיה רק אחר הנדה לא אחרי דמי טוהר. אלא אם בזיבה ילדה ופסק הדם תוך זמן ילידתה וסופרת שבעה ימים נקיים ובהשלים זמן ילידתה ארבעם לזכר ושמונים לנקבה טובלת ונטהרת משתי הטמאות. וזה הנקייה קודם ארבעים ושמונים ואחד ואחד טובלת ונטהרת משתי הטמאות ומביאה שתי קרבנות קרבן זבה וקרבן יולדת לא פסק הדם עד יום ארבעים ואחד ועד יום שמונים ואחד היא זבה. המפלת נפל שיש בו צורה אנושית היא טמאה טמאת לידה אלא המפלת נפל שהוא חתיכת בשר ולא נארג בשום צורה לא תטמא אלא טמאת שבעה. ואולם דעות החכמים על שני דרכים מהם אומרים כי המפלת נפל אפילו שהוא חתיכת בשר תטמא טמאת לידה. ומהם אומרים מעת שתראה בו צורה. והאומרים אפילו שהוא חתיכת בשר דנים אותו בחזקת נקבה לחמרא וזה אי אפשר כי הכתוב אמר "וְיָלְדָה זָכָר" (ויקרא יב, ב) וילדה נקבה{{fn:74}}  ומרמיז להיות בו צורה אנושית ואיך אפשר לדין על חתיכת בשר טמאת לידה. אכן האומרים מעת שתראה בו צורה זה מה שאין לחלוק לפי גלויו של כתוב ואפילו אם יולד ויראה בו צורת אדם ולא יבדל בין זכר לנקבה דנים אותו במשפט הנקבה. ואם תלד זכר ונקבה תטמא שמונים יום. ואם תלד הזכר קודם בימים ואחרי כן תלד הנקבה תתחיל מן הילידה האחרונה ואם תלד צורה אחרת דנים אותו אם זכר במשפט זכר ואם נקבה במשפט נקבה כי כן אמר "וְיָלְדָה זָכָר" "וְאִם-נְקֵבָה תֵלֵד" (ויקרא יב, א) ולא אמר להסגל צורת אדם:
content.english: The woman who has given birth, the scripture included her in the statute of the impurity of a menstruating woman, as it says, "as in the days of her menstrual impurity she shall be unclean" (Lev 12:2), and her impurity is not because of the blood that she sees with the menstruation but because of the birth, for the scripture made her unclean for two weeks for a female, and if it should happen that the woman becomes unclean before the birth for a day or two days and the beginning of the seven and the two weeks from the time of the birth, not from the time she saw blood. And one who says that we do not find a woman who gives birth without blood, and it is possible that she would be unclean because of the blood and because of the birth, we have already shown the weakness of this statement, and furthermore, it has already been related about the Durkati family that the women have no blood of virginity and no blood of menstruation and no blood of childbirth. And what is appropriate to rule, according to the view of one who says that the first blood makes one unclean for seven days, the midwife should be unclean with the impurity of seven days, as long as she does not see blood before the birth, but if she sees blood before the birth, the midwife is unclean for one day, and happy is one who is stringent. If she gave birth while she was a menstruating woman, she does not have after completing the time of her menstruation a time of a discharge, for she was transferred from the statute of a menstruating woman to the statute of one who has given birth, and after seven days for a male and two weeks for a female, the scripture judged them to be in the blood of purification, and she does not have a time of a discharge, and if the blood did not stop on the forty-first day and on the eighty-first day, it is necessary to judge that she is a menstruating woman, and the blood that she saw on the forty-first day and on the eighty-first day is the first blood and makes one unclean with the impurity of seven days. The same applies if she did not see blood before childbirth and she saw on the forty-first day and on the eighty-first day, she is a menstruating woman, for a discharge will only be after a menstruating woman, not after the blood of purification. But if she gave birth in a state of a discharge, and the blood stopped during the time of her childbirth, and she counts seven clean days, and when completing the time of her childbirth, forty for a male and eighty for a female, she immerses and is cleansed from the two impurities. And this cleansing before forty and eighty-one days, she immerses and is cleansed from the two impurities and brings two sacrifices, a sacrifice of a woman with a discharge and a sacrifice of one who has given birth. If the blood did not stop until the forty-first day and until the eighty-first day, she is a woman with a discharge. One who miscarries a stillborn that has human form is unclean with the impurity of childbirth, but one who miscarries a stillborn that is a lump of flesh and is not formed in any form is not unclean except with the impurity of seven days. And regarding the views of the sages, there are two ways: some of them say that one who miscarries a stillborn, even if it is a lump of flesh, is unclean with the impurity of childbirth. And some of them say, from the time she sees a form in it. And those who say even if it is a lump of flesh, they judge it in the presumption of a female stringently, and this is impossible, for the scripture said, "And she gives birth to a male" (Lev 12:2) and gives birth to a female, and it hints that there should be a human form in it, and how can it be appropriate to judge a lump of flesh with the impurity of childbirth? Indeed, those who say, from the time she sees a form in it, this is what there is no disagreement about according to the revelation of the scripture, and even if it is born and there appears a human form in it and one cannot distinguish between a male and a female, they judge it according to the statute of a female. And if she gives birth to a male and a female, she is unclean for eighty days. And if she gives birth to the male first in days and afterward gives birth to the female, she begins from the latter birth, and if she gives birth to another form, they judge it if it is a male, according to the statute of a male, and if it is a female, according to the statute of a female, for so it said, "And she gives birth to a male," "And if she gives birth to a female" (Lev 12:1), and it did not say to specify the form of a person.
content.comments: 74 נקבה — Lev 12:2 reads: "and if she bears a female," not as it stands in *Gan Eden*, "and she bore a female."

content.hebrew: פרק תשיעי
content.english: Chapter Nine

content.hebrew: מה שאמרה התורה "כִּימֵי נִדַּת דְּוּתָהּ תִּטְמָא" (ויקרא יב, ב) "וְטָמְאָה שְׁבֻעַיִם כְּנִדָּתָהּ" (ויקרא יב, ה) אין ההקשה בימים אלא בחמר הטמאה שהרי אמר "וְטָמְאָה שְׁבֻעַיִם כְּנִדָּתָהּ". ועוד אמר על הזבה "כִּימֵי נִדָּתָהּ תִּהְיֶה טְמֵאָה הִוא" (ויקרא טו, כה) מלמד שהקישה בחמר הטמאה שהיא מטמאה משכב ומושב ומרכב ועושה אותם אב הטמאה. ואחרי שהפליג הכתוב שלשים ושלשה ימים מן השבעה וששים וששה מן שבועים אי אפשר היותם בשער הטמאה אחד כי מה טעם לומר על שבעה ימים "כִּימֵי נִדַּת דְּוֺתָהּ תִּטְמָא". ובעבור שהפליג הכתוב אלה הימים ר"ל שלשים ושלשה וששים וששה ודברה תורה מלות מסופקות נחלקו החכמים. מהם החמירו השבעה והקלו השלשים ושלשה. ומהם החמירו השלשים ושלשה והקלו השבעה. ומהם השוו אותם בשער הטמאה. ואשר החמירו אותם השבעה מן השלשים ושלשה סמכו ואמרו הואיל והפליג הכתוב השבעה מן השלשים ושלשה ואמר בהם "כִּימֵי נִדַּת דְּוֺתָהּ תִּטְמָא" להקישה בחמר הטמאה ואמר על השלשים ושלשה "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" (ויקרא יב, ד) מלמד שזאת באה במחנה שאם היתה חוץ למחנה מה טעם "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" אלא מלמד שזאת באה במחנה. ועוד שהכתוב קראם דמי טוהר מלמד שהקל אותם מן הטמאה הראשונה ואשר קראם דמי טוהר לא רצה שהם טהורים אלא בערך הטמאה הראשונה אך לא בארה התורה איכות טמאתה אם היא כטמאת בעל קרי או פחות או יותר. אך החכמים הקישוה לסופר זב. ואני רואה מכח הכתוב שנראים הדברים הואיל וזאת נכנסת במחנה אי אפשר שלא פיחת הכתוב מטמאותה שאם היא בשער הטמאה אחד והכתוב אמר "וְלֹא יְטַמְּאוּ אֶת-מַחֲנֵיהֶם" (במדבר ה, ג) צריך שלא תכנס במחנה גם זאת. וזאת לפי הראיה שהביאו נכנסת במחנה מכלל הקל אותה מן הטמאה הראשונה. וחכמים הקישו אותה במצורע המטהר שנאמר עליו "וְיָשַׁב מִחוּץ לְאָהֳלוֹ, שִׁבְעַת יָמִים" (ויקרא יד, ח) כי קלת הטמאה היא להכנס במחנה ותהיה נפרדת מן הטהורים משום שהיא מטמאת אותם אחר אשר נאמר "תֵּשֵׁב בִּדְמֵי טָהֳרָה" (ויקרא יב, ד)  שהרי המטהר בשבתו חוץ מביתו מטמא את בגדיו. ומהם הקלו טמאתה שמשכבה ומושבה מטמאים ברחיצה לא בכבוס. ומהם אומרים שנטמאים ואינם מטמאים. וחכמי הרבנים אמרו על המטהר שאין לו משכב ומושב שמטמא אך הם טמאים שהרי בגדיו טמאים ואין לקחת ראיה הואיל וטמא בגדיו מכלל שמשכבו ומושבו מטמאים אך להיותם טמאים הדין נותן. והאומרים שהיא בשער הטמאה אחד בין בשבעה בין בשלשים ושלשה מפני שנאמר בזאת "וְטָהֲרָה, מִמְּקֹר דָּמֶיהָ" (ויקרא יב, ז) ונאמר בנדה "וְהִוא, גִּלְּתָה אֶת-מְקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ" (ויקרא כ, יח) ונאמר "תֵּשֵׁב בִּדְמֵי טָהֳרָה" והישיבה היא עכוב הנגיעה מן הטהורים. ומה שנאמר "בִּדְמֵי טָהֳרָה" אין הטעם שהם טהורים אלא הטעם דמיה שמנקים אותה לצאת לידי טהרה ונאמר "וְטָהֲרָה, מִמְּקֹר דָּמֶיהָ". וחכמים אומרים דמים שנסגרו בבטנה בעודה הרה והיתה טהורה וע"כ אמר דמי טהרה ואין מאמרם נכון. ומה שנאמר "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" (ויקרא יב, ד) מהם אמרו מפני שזאת תחלת הטמאות על כן הזהיר מן הקדש וזה אינו מאמר נאות כי לא הזהיר אלא למה שהוא בשלשים ושלשה לא שהיא תוך השבעה והשבועים. ועוד קודם נושא ונוגע את הנבלה והם מוזהרים מגעת הקדש ומביאת המקדש. ומהם אמרו  שטעם הקדש הוא על המעשר שהוא חוצה מן המחנה שנאמר "בִּעַרְתִּי הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִן-הַבַּיִת" (דברים כו, יג) והמקדש הוא מחנה ישראל ואלו דברים סברות והם דברים מסופקים. ועוד מה טעם להפליג השבעה מן השלשה ושלשים והשבעה דמם כדמי הנדה והשלשים ושלשה קראם דמי טוהר. ולפי זאת הדעת צריך להיות לכלם אשור אחד ועוד לומר "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" הסגל על שלשים ושלשה ימים שהם ימי טוהר חוץ מן השבעה והאומרים שהיא בטמאה חמורה בשלשים ושלשה יותר מן השבעה מפני שמאמר "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" טעמו בכל טהור מן מענה "וַיִּהְיוּ כְלֵי-הַנְּעָרִים קֹדֶשׁ" (שמואל א כא, ו) שטעמו טהורים. והנה היא אסורה לגעת בטהורים והמקדש הוא מחנה ישראל כי אחר שהיא חוצה למחנה מה טעם "וְאֶל-הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לֹא תָבֹא" (ויקרא יב, ד) והיא חוצה למחנה והמקדש בתוך המחנה וזאת דעת חלושה ויותר רחוקה מהדעות הראשונות. ואמנם חכמי הרבנים טהרוה והתירוה לבעלה אפילו שופכת דם כנהר והדם אם נפל בככר של תרומה לא טמאו והרי הוא כטבול יום שאסור לאכול מן התרומה עד שיעריב שמשו לאכול מן הקדש עד שתביא כפרתה ולא חייבו לה טבילה בסוף ימי טוהר אלא הזמן מכשירה להביא כפרתה ולאכול מן הקדש. וחלוקה ביניהם שמהם טמאוה כנדה להמנע מן הדלקת הנר והצעת המטה ומזיגת הכוס וכל זה שתמנע מן תשמיש המטה. ואשר פסקו לפי הכונה הראשונה לא ניחה לאחרונים עד שחייבו הטבילה בסוף ימי טוהר הואיל ומטמאת את הקדש ואנחנו רואים כפי דינם שטבול יום אינו צריך טבילה אחרת לאכילת התרומה אלא הערב השמש ואין להכשרת הקדש רק הבאת כפרה אם היה מחוייב כפרה אלא אינו מחוייב טבילה והואיל וחייבה התורה טבילה בסוף ימי טוהר אין טבילה רק מטמאה כי המוכשר לנגיעת החולים אינו צריך טבילה לפי דעתם לנגיעת הקדש. ויש לחוש בדבר שמכלל היא טמאה ואין להם ראיה נכוחה לטהרתה בדינם הואיל והם חולקים. אכן מה שיש לנו לומר אחר שזאת מחוסרת כפרה היא כדין כל מחוסרי כפרה וארבעה הם מחוסרי כפרה וצריך להיותם שוים בדינם. ואלו הם הזב והזבה היולדת והמצורע כל אחד  מהם שני מינים בטמאה שיש זב וסופר זבה וסופרת מצורע ומטהר הנה יולדת ודמי טוהר. וכאשר מצאנו דין תורה בסופר וסופרת מפורש שהיא באה במחנה אבל על איכות טמאתה החקירה הוציאתנו שהיא מטמאת משכב ומושב כמו שמטמאים בגדים והם אינם מטמאים אחרים ועל המטהר מצאנו שבא כתוב מפורש שהוא  במחנה ובאר איכות טמאתו שמטמא בגדיו ועל דמי טוהר הקיץ במאמר "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" (ויקרא יב, ד) שהיא באה במחנה ולא בארה התורה איכות טמאתה ודין לנו מדין החקירה להקיש אחד מאחד. ומה שראוי לפסוק שאין בין טמאה ראשונה לטמאה שניה אלא ביאת המחנה. שעל טמאה ראשונה אמר "וְלֹא יְטַמְּאוּ אֶת-מַחֲנֵיהֶם" (במדבר ה, ג) ואין מענה "וְלֹא יְטַמְּאוּ אֶת-מַחֲנֵיהֶם" משום שהם נוגעים את הטהורים אלא שמטמאים בביאה אלא בטומאה שניה אינם מטמאים. ועוד שאין עושים משכב ומושב אב הטמאה אלא שהם טמאים לבד הקש לבגדיהם וזהו ההבדל בין טמאה לטמאה וממאמר הכתוב שאמר על המטהר "וְיָשַׁב מִחוּץ לְאָהֳלוֹ, שִׁבְעַת יָמִים" (ויקרא יד, ח) למדנו אסור ביאת האשה ר"ל שלא ישכב טמא עם טהורה  ונאמר ביולדת "תֵּשֵׁב בִּדְמֵי טָהֳרָה" (ויקרא יב, ד) ומורה זה המאמר מניעתה מביאת איש ונאמר עליה "וְטָהֲרָה, מִמְּקֹר דָּמֶיהָ" (ויקרא יב, ז) ונאמר על הנדה "וְהִוא, גִּלְּתָה אֶת-מְקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ" (ויקרא כ, יח) ומן שווי המלות למדנו אסור הביאה ואין מאמר "וְטָהֲרָה" לביאתה באיש רק לאכילת הקדשים כי הרחיצה הכשירה לביאתה באיש והנה תאר הימים במקור דמים והרחיצה הכשירה לביאה והכפרה לאכילת הקדש ואמר "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" בעבור שהיא באה במחנה ואין הכונה בעבור שהאזהרה מנגיעת הקדש מכלל אינה מטמאת הטהורים. אבל הכונה על הקדש עובר בלאו ומחוייב אבל באמת שהיא מטמאת את הטהורים נראה לי שלא נתחייבו אלה הארבעה כפרה אלא מפני שהם באים במחנה והם טמאים ולא כן הנדה שהיא חוץ למחנה ועוד שהיולדת לא חייבה הכתוב להביא כפרה אלא בעבור ימי טוהר לא בעבור השבעה והשבועים שכן אומר הכתוב "וּבִמְלֹאת יְמֵי טָהֳרָהּ" (ויקרא יב, ו) הדין נותן שאלו הארבעה טמאים ראוי שיוקש אחד מאחד וכן רואים חכמי התושיה הפוסקים אחרי חפוש וחקירה ודין להתנהג עמהם על צד החומרא והחוזק הואיל ודברה התורה דברים מסופקים. אך בבואם אל המחנה נראה שיש להם רחיצה הקש מן המצורע ונאמר על הזב "וְכִי-יִטְהַר הַזָּב, מִזּוֹבוֹ" (ויקרא טו, יג) ואם תאמר כי לא נתבאר ביולדת יש להשיב כי אולי על כן אמר "ִּדְמֵי טָהֳרָה" וכן נמי בסוף ימי טהרה לא הזכיר לה רחיצה כמו שלא הזכיר בראש ימי טהרה. מה שנאמר על הזכר "בִּדְמֵי טָהֳרָה" ובנקבה "עַל-דְּמֵי טָהֳרָה" בעבור שעל הזכר ימים מועטים אפשר שלא יפסק הדם אלא על הנקבה רוב ימים  ויפסק הדם על כן אמר על הזכר "בִּדְמֵי"  ועל הנקבה אמר "עַל-דְּמֵי" ובאמרו "דְּמֵי טָהֳרָה" אין הטעם דמים טהורים כי אחרי דין הלשון הסמוך חוץ מעצם הנסמך ואינו כדרך בני בליעל אחרי שיש לו פירוש נאות לפי תקונו ור"ל דמים שמוציאים אותה לידי טהרה שהיא תנקה מלידה מבטן ומהריון מפני שמלת "טָהֳרָה" שם מקרה מצטרף לה ואינו תואר על דמי וכן נאמר "וְטָהֲרָה, מִמְּקֹר דָּמֶיהָ". יש מן החכמים שאמרו על דרך סברא כי לכך אמר "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע" מפני שדמה אותה בשבעה ימים "כִּימֵי נִדַּת דְּוֺתָהּ תִּטְמָא" ואחרי הנדה יש זבה כדי שלא יעלה על דעת שהיא זבה אחרי השבעה ותספור שבעת ימים נקיים וחייבת קרבן לבוא אל המקדש על כן אמר "בְּכָל-קֹדֶשׁ לֹא-תִגָּע". ובעבור שאמר הכתוב ארבעים לזכר ושמונים לנקבה יש שתי דעות האחת מפני שהזכר יבש בטבעו ועל כן תפסק הליחה בקרוב והנקבה ליחה בטבעה ועל כן יארכו הימים להפסק הדם והליחה על כן שם ארבעים יום לזכר ושמונים יום לנקבה. והדעת השנית אומרת מפני שצורת הזכר נגמרת בארבעים ואחד יום והנקבה בשמונים ואחד יום על כן תהיה הטמאה כפי זמן תשלום הצורה:
content.english: What the Torah said, "as in the days of her menstrual impurity she shall be unclean" (Lev 12:2), "And she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her menstruation" (Lev 12:5), the comparison is not in days but in the stringency of impurity, for it said, "And she shall be unclean two weeks, as in her menstruation." And furthermore it said concerning the woman with a discharge, "like the days of her menstruation, she shall be unclean" (Lev 15:25), teaching that it compared her in the stringency of impurity, that she makes a bed and a seat and a saddle unclean and makes them to be a primary source of impurity. And after the scripture made a distinction of thirty-three days from the seven and sixty-six from the two weeks, it is impossible for them to be in one category of impurity, for what is the point of saying about seven days, "as in the days of her menstrual impurity she shall be unclean"? And because the scripture made a distinction regarding these days, that is, thirty-three and sixty-six, and the Torah spoke words of doubt, the sages disagreed. Some of them made the seven more severe and the thirty-three more lenient. And some of them made the thirty-three more severe and the seven more lenient. And some of them equated them in the category of impurity. And those who made the seven more severe than the thirty-three relied and said, since the scripture made a distinction between the seven and the thirty-three, and said about them, "as in the days of her menstrual impurity she shall be unclean," to compare her in the stringency of impurity, and it said about the thirty-three, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing" (Lev 12:4), teaching that this one comes into the camp, for if she were outside the camp, what is the point of saying, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing"? This teaches that this one comes into the camp. And furthermore, the scripture called them the blood of purification, teaching that it made them more lenient than the first impurity, and those which it called the blood of purification, it did not mean that they are pure, but in relation to the first impurity, but the Torah did not explain the nature of her impurity, whether it is like the impurity of one who has had a seminal emission, or less, or more. But the sages compared her to one who is counting the days after his discharge. And I see from the force of the scripture that the matters appear that since this one enters the camp, it is impossible that the scripture did not reduce from her impurity, for if she were in one category of impurity, and the scripture said, "And they shall not defile their camps" (Num 5:3), it would be necessary that she should not enter the camp, this one too. And this, according to the proof that they brought, enters the camp, implying that it has made her more lenient than the first impurity. And sages compared her to a leper who is being purified, about whom it says, "And he shall stay outside his tent seven days" (Lev 14:8), for the leniency of impurity is to enter the camp and be separate from the pure because she makes them unclean, after it is said, "She shall remain in the blood of her purification" (Lev 12:4), for the one who is being purified, in his staying outside his house, makes his garments unclean. And some of them made her impurity more lenient, that her bed and her seat make things unclean with washing but not with washing of clothes. And some of them say that they are unclean and do not make things unclean. And the rabbinical sages said about one who is being purified that he does not have a bed and a seat that makes things unclean, but they are unclean, for his garments are unclean, and there is no need to take a proof, since his garments are unclean, that implies that his bed and his seat make things unclean, but for them to be unclean, the law so indicates. And those who say that she is in one category of impurity, both in the seven and in the thirty-three, because it says about this one, "And she shall be cleansed from the fountain of her blood" (Lev 12:7), and it said about a menstruating woman, "And she has uncovered the fountain of her blood" (Lev 20:18), and it said, "She shall remain in the blood of her purification," and "to remain" means to be kept away from touching the pure. And what is said, "in the blood of her purification," the meaning is not that they are pure, but the meaning is the blood that cleanses her to emerge to purity, and it said, "And she shall be cleansed from the fountain of her blood." And sages say, blood that was closed up in her womb while she was pregnant and she was pure, and therefore it said, the blood of purification, and their statement is not correct. And what is said, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing" (Lev 12:4), some of them said, because this one is the beginning of impurities, therefore it warned about the consecrated, and this is not a fitting statement, for it only warned about what is in the thirty-three, not what is within the seven and the two weeks. And furthermore, previously, one who carries and touches a carcass, and they are warned against touching the consecrated and coming to the sanctuary. And some of them said that the meaning of consecrated is on tithes, which are outside the camp, as it says, "I have removed the consecrated from the house" (Deut 26:13), and the sanctuary is the camp of Israel, and these things are conjectures, and they are matters of doubt. And furthermore, what is the point of making the seven distinct from the thirty-three, and the blood of the seven is like the blood of menstruation, and it called the thirty-three the blood of purification? And according to this view, there needs to be one prohibition for all of them, and furthermore, to say, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing," it specified the thirty-three days, which are the days of purification, outside the seven. And those who say that she is in severe impurity in the thirty-three more than in the seven, because the statement "She shall not touch any consecrated thing" means anything pure, from the expression "And the young men's vessels are holy" (1Sam 21:6), which means pure. And she is forbidden to touch pure things, and the sanctuary is the camp of Israel, for since she is outside the camp, what is the point of saying, "And she shall not come into the sanctuary" (Lev 12:4)? And she is outside the camp, and the sanctuary is inside the camp, and this is a weak view and more distant than the first views. And indeed, the rabbinical sages purified her and permitted her to her husband, even pouring blood like a river, and the blood, if it falls on a loaf of terumah (priestly portion), they did not make it unclean, and she is like one who has immersed during the day, who is forbidden to eat from the terumah until his sun sets, to eat from the consecrated until she brings her atonement, and they did not obligate her to immerse at the end of the days of her purification, but the time makes her fit to bring her atonement and to eat from the consecrated. And there is a division among them that some of them made her unclean like a menstruating woman to refrain from lighting the lamp and making the bed and mixing the cup, and all this so that she would refrain from intercourse. And those who ruled according to the first intention, the latter ones were not satisfied with it, until they obligated immersion at the end of the days of purification, since she makes the consecrated unclean, and we see according to their law that one who has immersed during the day does not need another immersion to eat terumah, but only sunset, and there is nothing that makes the consecrated permissible except bringing atonement, if one was obligated in atonement, but one is not obligated in immersion, and since the Torah obligated immersion at the end of the days of purification, immersion is only for one who is unclean, for one who is prepared to touch ordinary things does not need immersion, according to their view, to touch the consecrated. And there is a concern about the matter, that it implies that she is unclean, and they have no upright proof for her purification in their law, since they disagree. Indeed, what we have to say, after she lacks atonement, she has the law of all who lack atonement, and there are four who lack atonement, and they need to be equal in their law. And these are the man with a discharge and the woman with a discharge, the woman who has given birth, and the leper. Each of them has two types in impurity, for there is a man with a discharge and one who is counting, a woman with a discharge and one who is counting, a leper and one who is being purified; thus a woman who has given birth and the blood of purification. And as we found the law of the Torah for one who is counting and one who is being counted explicitly that she comes into the camp, but regarding the nature of her impurity, the investigation has led us to the fact that she makes a bed and a seat unclean just as she makes garments unclean, and they do not make others unclean, and regarding one who is being purified, we found that a verse comes explicitly that he is in the camp, and it explained the nature of his impurity that he makes his garments unclean, and regarding the blood of purification, it alluded in the statement, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing" (Lev 12:4) that she comes into the camp, and the Torah did not explain the nature of her impurity, and it is a law for us from the law of investigation to compare one to the other. And what is appropriate to rule is that there is no difference between the first impurity and the second impurity except coming into the camp. For regarding the first impurity, it said, "And they shall not defile their camps" (Num 5:3), and the meaning of "And they shall not defile their camps" is not because they touch the pure, but they make things unclean in coming, but in the second impurity, they do not make things unclean. And furthermore, they do not make a bed and a seat to be a primary source of impurity, but they are only unclean, a comparison to their garments, and this is the difference between impurity and impurity, and from the statement of the scripture that said about one who is being purified, "And he shall stay outside his tent seven days" (Lev 14:8), we learn the prohibition of coming upon a woman, that is, that an unclean person should not lie with a clean woman, and it said about a woman who has given birth, "She shall remain in the blood of her purification" (Lev 12:4), and this statement indicates her prevention from a man coming upon her, and it said about her, "And she shall be cleansed from the fountain of her blood" (Lev 12:7), and it said about the menstruating woman, "and she has uncovered the fountain of her blood" (Lev 20:18), and from the equivalence of the words, we learn the prohibition of coming upon her, and the statement "And she shall be cleansed" is not for her coming upon a man but for eating consecrated things, for the washing made her fit for coming upon a man, and it described the days in the fountain of blood, and the washing made her fit for coming upon him, and the atonement for eating the consecrated, and it said, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing" because she comes into the camp, and the intention is not because the warning against touching the consecrated implies that she does not make the pure unclean. But the intention is regarding the consecrated, one transgresses a negative commandment and is obligated, but in truth, that she makes the pure unclean, it seems to me that these four were not obligated in atonement except because they come into the camp and they are unclean, and not so the menstruating woman, who is outside the camp, and furthermore, that the woman who has given birth, the scripture did not obligate her to bring atonement except because of the days of purification, not because of the seven and the two weeks, for so the scripture says, "And when the days of her purification are fulfilled" (Lev 12:6), the law so indicates that these four unclean ones should be compared one to the other, and thus the wise men of sound judgment who rule after research and investigation see, and it is a law to conduct oneself with them on the side of stringency and strength, since the Torah spoke words of doubt. But in their coming into the camp, it appears that they have washing like the comparison from the leper, and it said about the man with a discharge, "And when he who has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge" (Lev 15:13), and if you say that it was not explained regarding the woman who has given birth, one can answer that perhaps therefore it said "the blood of her purification," and likewise at the end of the days of her purification, it did not mention washing for her as it did not mention at the beginning of the days of her purification. What is said about the male, "in the blood of her purification," and about the female, "for the blood of her purification" (Lev 12:5), it is because for the male, the days are few, and it is possible that the blood would not stop, but for the female, most days, and the blood stops. Therefore, it said about the male, "in the blood," and about the female, it said, "for the blood," and in saying "the blood of her purification," the meaning is not pure blood, for after the rule of the language, the adjacent is outside the essence of what it is adjacent to, and it is not like "sons of wickedness" since it has a fitting interpretation according to its arrangement, and it means blood that brings her out to a state of purity, that she is cleansed from childbirth, from the womb, and from conception, because the word "her purification" is the name of an event that is attributed to her, and it is not an adjective for blood, and so it said, "And she shall be cleansed from the fountain of her blood." There are sages who said as a conjecture that therefore it said, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing," because it compared her in the seven days, "as in the days of her menstrual impurity she shall be unclean," and after menstruation there is a discharge, so that it should not arise in one's mind that she is a woman with a discharge after the seven, and she should count seven clean days and be obligated in a sacrifice to come to the sanctuary. Therefore, it said, "She shall not touch any consecrated thing." And because the scripture said forty for a male and eighty for a female, there are two views. One is that the male is dry by nature, and therefore the moisture stops soon, and the female is moist by nature, and therefore the days are lengthened for the blood and the moisture to stop. Therefore, it placed forty days for a male and eighty days for a female. And the second view says that because the form of the male is completed in forty-one days and the female in eighty-one days, therefore the impurity would be according to the time of the completion of the form.

content.hebrew: פרק עשירי
content.english: Chapter Ten

content.hebrew: לא מצאנו מבעלי עינות הטמאה במין האדם שתהיה טמאתו קלה רק מי שיצא ממנו שכבת זרע שנאמר "וְאִישׁ, כִּי-תֵצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת-זָרַע--וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם אֶת-כָּל-בְּשָׂרוֹ, וְטָמֵא עַד-הָעָרֶב"{{fn:75}} (ויקרא טו, טז) ואינו עושה משכב ומושב ומרכב ואינו מטמא דבר אחר. אכן הנוגע בשכבת זרע טמא כטמאת מי שיוצאה ממנו והיא מטמאה בעוד שהיא ליחה והראיה ממה שאמר הכתוב "כִּי-תֵצֵא" ולא אמר כי יגע בשכבת זרע ולא תארה בשם טמא כעין שנאמר על הזב "מִבְּשָׂרוֹ--זוֹבוֹ, טָמֵא הוּא" (ויקרא טו, ב). ועוד שנאמר "וְכָל-בֶּגֶד וְכָל-עוֹר, אֲשֶׁר-יִהְיֶה עָלָיו" (ויקרא טו, יז) מכלל ששכבת זרע אינה מטמאה רק בלכלוך לבן. הכתם אשר לא יעבור מן הבגד אינו מעכב הבגד מטהרתו כי אמר "וְרָחַץ" ולא אמר וקרע כמו שנאמר על צרעת הבגד.  ומה שאמר הכתוב אשר "תֵצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת-זָרַע" ר"ל אשר תצא ממנו בלתי רצונו ובאמרו "וְאִשָּׁה, אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אִישׁ אֹתָהּ שִׁכְבַת-זָרַע" (ויקרא טו, יח) מלמד אשר יצא ממנו ברצון והם שני מינים. הטפה שיוצאת רטיבות לבד אשר לא יתם ולד ממנה וטפה שיתם ולד ממנה ושניהם נכללים במלת "שִׁכְבַת-זָרַע" שהוא ענין שפיכות מלשון "וְנִבְלֵי שָׁמַיִם, מִי יַשְׁכִּיב" (איוב לח, לז) ואינו רוצה רטיבות שיוצאת עם השתן. ואמר "וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם אֶת-כָּל-בְּשָׂרוֹ" (ויקרא טו, טז) ולא אמר ורחץ בשרו מלמד שלא תספיק הרחיצה באבר שיוצאת ממנו שכבת זרע לבד אלא הרחיצה תהיה לכל בשרו. ואמנם הטהרה היא בערב אבל זמן הרחיצה לא הורה הכתוב מתי תהיה מכלל היום ובמשנה תורה הורה שהיא לפנות ערב ופנות ערב הוא זמן סמוך לערב כנגד זה לפנות בקר לשם אומר "וַיְהִי, בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר" (שמות יד, כד) ואמר "כִּי-פָנָה הַיּוֹם" (ירמיהו ו, ד) לערוב ואומר "וּכְבֹא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ, יָבֹא אֶל-תּוֹךְ הַמַּחֲנֶה" (דברים כג, יב). לא לפי דעת הרבנים שאומרים שכל היום ראוי לטבילה בתחלת הלילה עד הערב השמש מפני שפירשו " וְהָיָה לִפְנוֹת-עֶרֶב" (דברים כג, יב) תחלת הלילה. לא תאבה לשמוע להם ואפילו עבר אותו העת צריך ביום אחר שיהיה עוד לפנות ערב. יש מן החכמים שאומרים שלא רצה במשנה תורה אלא לבעל קרי. ויש להשיב שבעל קרי הזכר בפסוק "וְאִישׁ, כִּי-תֵצֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שִׁכְבַת-זָרַע" (ויקרא טו, טז) שהרי מי שהוא ברצון הזכר בפסוק "וְאִשָּׁה, אֲשֶׁר יִשְׁכַּב אִישׁ אֹתָהּ שִׁכְבַת-זָרַע" (ויקרא טו, יח) ונאמר לזה "וְרָחֲצוּ בַמַּיִם, וְטָמְאוּ עַד-הָעָרֶב" (ויקרא טו, יח) ונאמר לראשון "וְרָחַץ בַּמַּיִם אֶת-כָּל-בְּשָׂרוֹ" (ויקרא טו, טז) צא ודע הואיל ששניהם שוים במלת רחיצה ולאחד מהם נאמר "וְהָיָה לִפְנוֹת-עֶרֶב, יִרְחַץ בַּמָּיִם" (דברים כג, יב) מכלל ששניהם לפנות ערב. וזאת התשובה תפיל טענת מי שאמר כי אל מחנה קטון צריך פנות ערב. ויש תשובה אחרת על זה שבעל קרי אינו צריך רחיצה אלא בעבור המקדש ואם על מחנה קטון צריך פנות ערב אל המקדש למה לא יהיה צריך פנות ערב ונמצא מחנה קטון עדוף מן המקדש ולא עוד אלא מי שרחץ באיזה עת שנזדמן לא בפנות ערב ונזדמן אל מחנה קטן לא יכנס במחנה עד שירחץ בפנות ערב. האשה ששכבה איש אותה שכבת זרע היא טמאה והלא ההקש יחייב שאם הבגד שנפל שכבת זרע עליו הוא טמא הוא הדין לאשה אלא למד הכתוב האשה ששמשה עם איש והיה שכבת זרע היא טמאה כי אע"פ שפרשה ממנו ולא נתלכלכה משום שהורה כחץ כי נגיעת בית הסתרים אינה נגיעה אלא היא טמאה משום השמוש אע"פ כן חכמינו ע"ה אמרו אי אפשר בלי לכלוך מכלל מצד הלכלוך היא טמאה. אכן אחרי האמת אלו לא נתלכלכה היא טמאה כך עולה מכח הכתוב ואם שמשו בלי שכבת זרע אינם טמאים:
content.english: We do not find, of those with fountains of impurity in the type of man, that his impurity would be minor, except for one from whom semen has come out, as it says, "And any man, when a seminal emission goes out from him, he shall wash all his body in water, and be unclean until evening" (Lev 15:16), and he does not make a bed and a seat and a saddle unclean, and he does not make another thing unclean. Indeed, one who touches semen is unclean like the impurity of one from whom it comes out, and it makes things unclean while it is moist, and the proof is from what the scripture says, "when it goes out," and it did not say, "when he touches semen," and it did not describe it with the name "unclean," as it said about the person with a discharge, "from his flesh, his discharge is unclean" (Lev 15:2). And furthermore, it said, "And every garment and every skin on which there is semen" (Lev 15:17), implying that semen only makes things unclean with white soiling. A stain that does not go away from the garment does not prevent the garment from its purification, for it said, "and he shall wash," and it did not say "and he shall tear," as it said about the leprosy of a garment. And what the scripture said, "when a seminal emission goes out from him," it means that goes out from him without his will, and in saying, "Also, when a man lies with a woman with seminal emission" (Lev 15:18), it teaches that which came out from him with his will, and they are two types. The drop that comes out, moisture only, which a child is not completed from it, and a drop from which a child would be completed, and both of them are included in the term "seminal emission," which is an expression of pouring, from the expression "and who can lay flat the bottles of heaven" (Job 38:37), and it does not mean moisture that comes out with urine. And it said, "And he shall wash all his body in water" (Lev 15:16), and it did not say "and he shall wash his body," teaching that washing is not sufficient for the organ from which the seminal emission comes out only, but the washing should be for all of his body. And indeed, the purification is in the evening, but the time of washing, the scripture did not indicate when it should be from the day, implying the whole day, and in Deuteronomy, it indicated that it is at the approach of evening, and the approach of evening is a time close to evening, equivalent to "when morning comes" for which it says, "And it came to pass, in the morning watch" (Exod 14:24), and it said, "For the day has declined" (Jer 6:4) toward evening, and it said, "And when the sun sets, he may come into the camp" (Deut 23:12). Not according to the view of the rabbis, who say that all day is appropriate for immersion from the beginning of the night until sunset, because they interpreted "Then it shall be, when evening comes" (Deut 23:12) as the beginning of the night. Do not consent to listen to them, and even if that time has passed, it is necessary on another day that it should be at the approach of evening. There are sages who say that it did not mean in Deuteronomy except for one who has had a seminal emission. And one can answer that one who has had a seminal emission is mentioned in the verse, "And any man, when a seminal emission goes out from him" (Lev 15:16), for one who does it intentionally is mentioned in the verse, "Also, when a man lies with a woman with seminal emission" (Lev 15:18), and it said for this one, "both of them shall wash with water, and be unclean until evening" (Lev 15:18), and it said for the first one, "he shall wash all his body in water" (Lev 15:16). Know that since they are equal in the term "washing," and for one of them it said, "Then it shall be, when evening comes, that he shall wash with water" (Deut 23:12), implying that both of them are at the approach of evening. And this answer will cause the fall of the argument of one who says that to the small camp one needs the approach of evening. And there is another answer to this, that one who has had a seminal emission does not need washing except because of the sanctuary, and if for the small camp one needs the approach of evening, for the sanctuary why should one not need the approach of evening? And we find the small camp superior to the sanctuary, and not only this, but one who washed at whatever time occurred, not at the approach of evening, and it happened to the small camp, one would not enter the camp until one washed at the approach of evening. A woman with whom a man has lain with seminal emission, she is unclean, and doesn't the comparison require that if a garment on which seminal emission has fallen is unclean, so too for a woman? But the scripture taught that a woman who had intercourse with a man, and there was seminal emission, she is unclean, for even though she separated from him and was not soiled, because it shot like an arrow, for touching in hidden places is not touching, but she is unclean because of the intercourse. Nevertheless, our sages, of blessed memory, said, it is impossible without soiling, implying that because of the soiling she is unclean. Indeed, after the truth, if she was not soiled, she is unclean; thus it arises from the force of the scripture, and if they had intercourse without seminal emission, they are not unclean.
content.comments: 75 עַד-הָעָרֶב" — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "and a man from whom a discharge of seed goes forth, and he bathes his body in water — he is unclean until evening," whereas Lev 15:16 reads: "and a man from whom a discharge of seed goes forth — he shall bathe all his body in water, and be unclean until evening."

content.hebrew: נשלמו דיני טמאה וטהרה בזב נדה וזבה ויולדת ובעל קרי
content.english: The laws of impurity and purity regarding one with a discharge, a menstruating woman, a woman with a discharge, a woman who has given birth, and one who has had a seminal emission are now complete.

content.hebrew: ברוך ה' צורי
content.english: Blessed is the Lord, my Rock.

content.hebrew: XV # ואחל לכתוב דיני נגעי צרעת בשם החונן לאדם דעת
content.english: XV # And I shall begin to write the laws of leprosy afflictions in the name of the One who grants knowledge to man.

content.hebrew: משפטי נגעי צרעת נתבארו בתורתנו הקדושה באיזו צורה צריך הכהן לטמא ולטהר. והנה על האדם מצאנו נגעי הצרעת לשבעה חלקים ואלו הם. שאת ספחת בהרת של עור ובשר שאת ובהרת של מכוה שאת ובהרת של שחין ושאת של קרחת וגבחת והנתק של ראש והזקן והתורה בארה סימנים באיזה צורה יהיה טמא לכל אחד מאלו החלקים ועכ"ז יהיה בדבור הכהן כמו שיתבאר. סימני הבהרת שלשה הלובן והעומק ושער לבן. כשיהיה עם הלובן עומק או שער לבן מחליטו מיד אלא כשיהיה הלובן לבדו מסגירו וזו היא ספחת והראשונה בהרת הוא הנאמר עליה "וְרָאָה הַכֹּהֵן אֶת-הַנֶּגַע בְּעוֹר-הַבָּשָׂר וְשֵׂעָר בַּנֶּגַע הָפַךְ לָבָן, וּמַרְאֵה הַנֶּגַע עָמֹק מֵעוֹר"{{fn:76}} (ויקרא יג, ג). והראיה שזו בהרת ממאמר "וְאִם-בַּהֶרֶת לְבָנָה הִוא בְּעוֹר בְּשָׂרוֹ, וְעָמֹק אֵין-מַרְאֶהָ מִן-הָעוֹר"{{fn:77}} (ויקרא יג, ד) מלמד שגם היא בהרת לבנה כי לא שלל ממנה אלא העומק ושער לבן. והספחת היא הנזכרת במאמר "וְאִם-בַּהֶרֶת לְבָנָה" בלי שער ולובן וצריכה הסגר שבוע אחד ואם פשתה מחליטין אותו ואם פשתה וכהתה פוטרין אותו. אלא אם לא פשתה ועכ"ז עמד בעיניו הנגע נותנין לו הסגר שבוע שני ואם פשה מחליטין אותו או אם לא כהה ואם כהה אחרי שלא פשה מטהרין אותו ואם שב ופשה אחרי הטהרה אינו צריך הסגר אלא מחליטין אותו. והשאת היא הנזכרת בפסוק "נֶגַע צָרַעַת, כִּי תִהְיֶה בְּאָדָם; וְהוּבָא, אֶל-הַכֹּהֵן. (ויקרא יג, ט) וְרָאָה הַכֹּהֵן, וְהִנֵּה שְׂאֵת-לְבָנָה בָּעוֹר" (ויקרא יג, י) ואשורה בלובן ושער לבן להיות נשואה מעור הבשר וסימן טמאתה ב"מִחְיַת בָּשָׂר חַי, בַּשְׂאֵת" (ויקרא יג, י) אך אם צמחה הצרעת בכל הגוף ואין בו בשר חי טהור וביום הראות בו בשר חי יטמא ואם שב הבשר החי ללבן עוד טהור הוא. שאת ובהרת של שחין בין בהרת של שחין ובין בהרת של עור בשר שזאת אדמדמת וסימן הטמאה במראה בעומק ושער לבן אך אם אין עומק ושער לבן והמראה כהה צריך הסגרה ואם פשה טמא לא פשה טהור וההסגרה שבוע אחד לבד. שאת ובהרת המכוה היות לבנה אדמדמת בעומק ושער לבן לא היה בה שער לבן ועומק והיא כהה צריך הסגרה שבוע אחד ואם פשה הוא טמא ואם לא פשה יהיה טהור. ושאת של קרחת וגבחת כי כן סימן טמאתה היות לבנה אדמדמת. ההבדל בין שאת וספחת ובהרת השאת היא נשואה מן העור והבהרת עמוקה מן העור והספחת שוה עם העור. והנתק של ראש וזקן סימניו בשער צהוב ודק ועומק ואם אין לו אלו הסימנים צריך הסגרה שבוע. ואם ראה בסוף השבוע ולא פשה הנתק ואין לו לא עומק ושער צהוב צריך גלוח סביבות הנתק והסגר שני שבוע אחד ואם יראה בסוף השבוע השני ולא פשה ואין לו עומק יהיה טהור ואם יפשה אחר הטהרה יהיה טמא אף אם צמח שער שחור משבוע ראשון יהיה טהור שהשער השחור סימן טהרה בנתקים. בעלי הקבלה אמרו ארבע מראות נגעים בהרת וספחתה שאת וספחתה. והלא ספחת אחת נזכרת אלא דקדקו שטעם ספחת טפלה והורה שהיא ספחת של בהרת מכלל שיש ספחת לשאת ובתורה לא נזכרו אלא שלשה שמות בהרת ספחת ושאת. דרשו במאמר "וְהָיָה בְעוֹר-בְּשָׂרוֹ, לְנֶגַע צָרָעַת"{{fn:78}} (ויקרא יג, ב) שהיא רביעית והלא לא נזכרו בתורה רק שלשה פרקים שאת ספחת ובהרת ואלו היה מאמר לנגע צרעת בראשו והיה ראוי לזכור הפרק שלו רק מאמר "וְהָיָה בְעוֹר-בְּשָׂרוֹ, לְנֶגַע צָרָעַת" חוזר לכל אחת מאלו השלשה אף כי אמרו ארבע מראות נגעים בהרת עזה כשלג. כהה מזאת כצמר הלבן היא השאת. כהה מזאת כסיד ההיכל היא ספחת הבהרת. כהה מזאת כקרום ביצה שהיא תחת הקליפה היא ספחת השאת. והמעיין היטב ידע בלבול דבריהם כי היה ראוי לתפוש מן הבהרת לרדת עד  קרום הביצה או להפך אלא מה עשה הכתוב תפש מן המראה השנית שהיא כצמר הלבן שהיא השאת ואחרי כן השלישית שהיא כסיד ההיכל שהיא הספחת אחרי כן דלג על הראשונה שהיא עזה כשלג שהיא הבהרת וכמו שהיא שלישית בכתוב כן היא שלישית למראה תלמוד לומר לבנה היא שאין למעלה הימנה ואדרבא יש לומר מצד פחיתות המראה על כן תארם בלובן ואחרי כן חזר עוד אל הרביעית שהיא כקרום ביצה במאמר "וְהָיָה בְעוֹר-בְּשָׂרוֹ, לְנֶגַע צָרָעַת" (ויקרא יג, ב) ואומרים למטה מקרום הביצה הוא הבהק. עוד אמרו כי סימני הטמאה שלשה שער לבן ומחיה ופשיון והכתוב באר השלשה סימנים כל אחד לפרק אחד שער לבן על הבהרת פשיון על הספחת מחיה על השאת והם אומרים כל אחד מאלו הסימנים יהיה סימן טמאה לכל אחת מארבע מראות ולא כן רצון הכתוב אלא לכל אחד מן הנגעים סימן מוסגל מה שאין לזולתו. עוד אמרו כי העומק כעומק החמה מן הצל ואינו ענין חפירה והעומק לא יהיה אלא מצד לבנונית והלא לפי דינם כקרום הביצה יהיה עמוק והוא אינו לובן חזק אף על הבהרת שהיא ספחת לבנה אומר ומראהו איננו עומק מן העור. עוד אמרו כי מה שאמרה התורה לבנה אדמדמת על הבהרת של שחין ושל מכוה הוא הנקרא פתוך וזה יהיה לכל אחת מן ארבע מראות ושערו לכל אחת מארבע מראות מעין האודם הם אומרים ארבעה טיפין דם בכוס חלב פתוך של מראה ראשונה וחמשה טיפין של מראה שניה ושנים עשר טיפין של מראה השלישית וששה עשר טיפין של מראה הרביעית. ודברו דברים שלא דברה התורה ונתנו שעור לנגע הצרעת שהוא כגריס שהוא שש שעורות אורך ושש שעורות רוחב פחות מזה לא יהיה צרעת. ודברו דברים בשעור המחיה והשער ומנהגם ידוע בענין השעורים מה שלא רמזה התורה ואין לנו לעסוק בדבריהם יותר. אך מה שהרמזנו הוא להעיר שעור יציאתם ממה שגזרה התורה אך אנחנו נמשך אחר הפשט להורות דין תורה בנגעי הצרעת:
content.english:
The statutes of leprosy afflictions have been explained in our holy Torah, in what form the priest needs to declare unclean and to purify. And on a person, we find the leprosy afflictions in seven parts, and these are: a swelling, a scab, a bright spot of skin and flesh, a swelling and a bright spot of a burn, a swelling and a bright spot of a boil, and a swelling of baldness of the front or the back of the head, and a scale of the head and the beard, and the Torah explained the signs in what form it would be unclean for each of these parts, and nevertheless, it would be by the speech of the priest, as will be explained. The signs of a bright spot are three: whiteness, depth, and white hair. When there would be with the whiteness depth or white hair, he declares him definitively unclean immediately, but when there would be the whiteness alone, he quarantines him, and this is a scab, and the first one is a bright spot, which is what is said about it, "And the priest shall examine the affliction in the skin of the flesh, and the hair in the affliction has turned white, and the appearance of the affliction is deeper than the skin" (Lev 13:3). And the proof that this is a bright spot is from the statement, "And if a bright spot is white in the skin of his flesh, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin" (Lev 13:4), teaching that it too is a white bright spot, for it only negated from it the depth and white hair. And the scab is the one mentioned in the statement, "And if a bright spot is white," without hair and whiteness, and it requires quarantine for one week, and if it spreads, they declare him definitively unclean, and if it spreads and becomes dim, they release him. But if it did not spread and nevertheless the affliction remained as it was, they give him quarantine for a second week, and if it spread, they declare him definitively unclean, or if it did not become dim, and if it became dim after it did not spread, they purify him, and if it returns and spreads after the purification, it does not require quarantine but they declare him definitively unclean. And the swelling is the one mentioned in the verse, "When the leprosy affliction shall be on a person, he shall be brought to the priest. And the priest shall look, and behold, a white swelling is in the skin" (Lev 13:9-10), and its assurance is with whiteness and white hair, being raised from the skin of the flesh, and the sign of its impurity is in "living flesh in the swelling" (Lev 13:10), but if the leprosy flourished on the whole body and there is no living flesh in it, it is pure, and on the day when living flesh appears in it, it will be unclean, and if the living flesh returns to white again, it is still pure. A swelling and a bright spot of a boil, whether a bright spot of a boil or a bright spot of skin of flesh, this one is reddish white, and the sign of impurity in appearance in depth and white hair, but if there is no depth and white hair and the appearance is dim, it requires quarantine, and if it spread, it is unclean; if it did not spread, it is pure, and the quarantine is one week only. A swelling and a bright spot of a burn is to be white reddish in depth and white hair; if it did not have white hair and depth and it is dim, it requires quarantine for one week, and if it spread, it is unclean, and if it did not spread, it will be pure. And the swelling of baldness of the front or the back of the head, this is the sign of its impurity, being white reddish. And a scale of the head and the beard, the signs of it are in yellow and thin hair and depth, and if it does not have these signs, it requires quarantine for a week. And if he saw at the end of the week and the scale did not spread and it does not have depth and yellow hair, it requires shaving around the scale and quarantine for a second week for one week, and if he sees at the end of the second week and it did not spread and it does not have depth, it will be pure, and if it spreads after the purification, it will be unclean, even if black hair grew from the first week, it will be pure, for black hair is a sign of purity in scales. The Rabbanites said that there are four appearances of afflictions: a bright spot and its attachment, a swelling and its attachment. And isn't only one attachment mentioned in the Torah? But they inferred that the meaning of attachment is subsidiary, and it indicates that it is the attachment of the bright spot, implying that there is an attachment to the swelling, and in the Torah only three names are mentioned: the bright spot, the attachment, and the swelling. They expounded on the statement, "And it becomes in the skin of his flesh a swelling or a scab or a bright spot" (Lev 13:2), that it is the fourth, and haven't only three sections been mentioned in the Torah? Swelling, scab, and bright spot, and if the statement "for a leprosy affliction" were at its beginning, and it would be appropriate to mention its section, but only the statement "And it becomes in the skin of his flesh a leprosy affliction" returns to each of these three, even though they said that there are four appearances of leprosy afflictions: a bright spot as intense as snow. Dimmer than this, like white wool, it is the swelling. Dimmer than this, like the plaster of the temple, it is the attachment of the bright spot. Dimmer than this, like the membrane of an egg that is under the shell, it is the attachment of the swelling. And one who examines well knows the confusion in their words, for it would be appropriate to take from the bright spot to descend to the membrane of the egg, or the opposite, but what did the scripture do? It took from the second appearance, which is like white wool, which is the swelling, and after that the third, which is like the plaster of the temple, which is the attachment, after that it skipped over the first one, which is intense as snow, which is the bright spot, and just as it is third in the scripture, so it is third in appearance, that is, a lesson from the word "white," that there is nothing above it, and on the contrary, one can say from the side of the deficiency of the appearance he described them in whiteness, and after that he returned again to the fourth, which is like the membrane of an egg, in the statement, "And it becomes in the skin of his flesh a leprosy affliction" (Lev 13:2), and they say lower than the membrane of the egg is the bohak (a harmless skin condition). Furthermore, they said that the signs of impurity are three: white hair, living flesh, and spreading, and the scripture explained the three signs, each for one section, white hair for the bright spot, spreading for the attachment, living flesh for the swelling, and they say each of these signs would be a sign of impurity for each of the four appearances, and this is not the intention of the scripture, but for each of the afflictions, there is a sign dedicated to it that the others do not have. Furthermore, they said that the depth is like the depth of the sun from the shade, and it is not a matter of digging, and the depth will only be from the side of whiteness, and according to their law, one like the membrane of an egg would be deep, and it is not strong whiteness, and also regarding the bright spot, which is an attachment, it says, "and its appearance is not deep" (Lev 13:4) Furthermore, they said that what the Torah said, white reddish, on the bright spot of a boil and of a burn is what is called "mixed," and this would be for each of the four appearances, and they judged for each of the four appearances the source of redness, they say, four drops of blood in a cup of milk is the mixture of the first appearance, and five drops of the second appearance, and twelve drops of the third appearance, and sixteen drops of the fourth appearance. And they spoke things that the Torah did not speak, and they gave a measure for the leprosy affliction, that it is like a Cilician bean, which is six barleycorns in length and six barleycorns in width; less than this would not be leprosy. And they spoke things about the measure of the living flesh and the hair, and their custom is known regarding the matter of measurements that the Torah did not hint at, and we have no need to engage in their words further. But what we have hinted at is to awaken measurement of their departing from what the Torah decreed, but we will follow the plain meaning to indicate the law of the Torah regarding leprosy afflictions.

.
content.comments: 76 מֵעוֹר" — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "and the priest examined the affliction, and the hair in the affliction had turned white, and its appearance was deeper than the skin," whereas Lev 13:3 reads: "and the priest shall look upon the affliction in the skin of the flesh, and the hair in the affliction has turned white, and the appearance of the affliction is deeper than the skin of his flesh." 77 מִן-הָעוֹר" — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "and if it is a white bright spot, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin," whereas Lev 13:4 reads: "and if it is a white bright spot in the skin of his flesh, and it is not deeper than the skin in appearance." 78 צָרָעַת" — The wording of the verse has been corrected. The same below.

content.english: Chapter One

content.hebrew: הכתוב אמר "וַיְדַבֵּר ה', אֶל-מֹשֶׁה וְאֶל-אַהֲרֹן" בעבור שנגע הצרעת תלוי לכל מראה עיני הכהן על כן הכליל הדבור עם אהרון ואמר "אָדָם, כִּי-יִהְיֶה בְעוֹר-בְּשָׂרוֹ" (ויקרא יג, ב) ואמר "אָדָם" להכליל איש ואשה שהם מתטמאים בנגעים ואמר "שְׂאֵת אוֹ-סַפַּחַת אוֹ בַהֶרֶת" (ויקרא יג, ב) ואין זה הפרק כולל זולת המיחדים מפני שתלה ענין הצרעת במראה הכהן וחייב הקרבן לכל וכל זה תלוי על המיחד והזכיר שאת ספחת בהרת והיה לנגע צרעת חוזר לכל אחד משלשת הנגעים. וטעם שאת שהיא נשואה מעור הבשר וספחת שאינה לא נשואה ולא עמוקה ובהרת שהיא עמוקה מעור הבשר. והחל הכתוב בבהרת ממה שהשלים כמנהג הכתוב ואמר "וְהוּבָא אֶל-אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן, אוֹ אֶל-אַחַד מִבָּנָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים" (ויקרא יג, ב) כיון שלא אמר אשר יעמוד תחתיו מכלל שהכהנים המשנים ראויים לדין בנגעי הצרעת. ואמר "וְהוּבָא אֶל-אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֵן" שאם לא יבוא ברצונו יובא בעל כורחו "וְרָאָה הַכֹּהֵן אֶת-הַנֶּגַע בְּעוֹר" (ויקרא יג, ג) שהיא בהרת כי כן אמר "וְאִם-בַּהֶרֶת לְבָנָה" (ויקרא יג, ד). ויש אומרים שהיא כהה כיון שאמר "וְאִם-בַּהֶרֶת לְבָנָה" הפך מאמר בעלי הקבלה שהיא עזה כשלג ויש לומר שגם היא לבנה אם לא באר הכתוב ידענו זה מן מאמר "וְשֵׂעָר בַּנֶּגַע הָפַךְ לָבָן" (ויקרא יג, ג). ומה שאמר "וְשֵׂעָר בַּנֶּגַע הָפַךְ לָבָן" מלמד שהיה בו שער ונהפך ללבן לא שצמח עתה ומראה הנגע עמוק מן העור כטעם חפירה והטעם בהיות אחד משני הסימנים יהיה טמא שאם בהיות שניהם יהיה טמא הנה בהעדר אחד מהם לא הורה משפטו וזה אי אפשר מכלל שסימן אחד משניהם מטמא. ואם יאמר אומר והיה ראוי לומר מאמר ומראהו איננו עמוק מן העור או מראהו איננו עמוק יש לומר שאם היה אומר או מראהו הייתי דן שאם בסימן אחד יהיה טמא בשני סימנים צריך שיהיה לו משפט יתר ועל כן אמר "וּמַרְאֵהוּ" וכן נמי בשלילת שני הסימנים שאמר "וּמַרְאֵהוּ, אֵינֶנּוּ עָמֹק מִן-הָעוֹר" (ויקרא יג, לד) "וּשְׂעָרָה, לֹא-הָפַךְ לָבָן" (ויקרא יג, ד) ולא אמר או שערה לא הפך לבן מפני שהייתי אומר כי בסימן אחד היה צריך הסגר ואנחנו כפי שבארנו הוא טמא מוחלט וזה בהכרח מפני שאם בהמצא שניהם החליט ובהעדר שניהם הסגיר ובהעדר אחד מהם לא יצר משלשה פנים אם הוא מוחלט או מוסגר או פטור. ולהיותו פטור אי אפשר מפני כי בהעדר שני הסימנים יעדו להסגר ובהעדר אחד מהם יהיה פטור ולהיותו מוסגר אי אפשר כי הכתוב לא יעד להסגר אלא בהעדר שני הסימנים מכלל שהוא טמא מוחלט כסימן אחד ואם אין אחד משניהם רק הלובן לבדו יעדו להסגר שבעת ימים שנאמר "וְאִם-בַּהֶרֶת לְבָנָה הִוא בְּעוֹר בְּשָׂרוֹ{{fn:79}}, וְעָמֹק אֵין-מַרְאֶהָ מִן-הָעוֹר, וּשְׂעָרָה, לֹא-הָפַךְ לָבָן--וְהִסְגִּיר הַכֹּהֵן אֶת-הַנֶּגַע, שִׁבְעַת יָמִים" (ויקרא יג, ד). תמיה אני לבעלי הקבלה אשר אמרו שהעומק אינו סימן טמאה ועוד חזרו ואמרו שכל נגע שאין לו עומק אינו נדון נגע והכתוב אומר "וּמַרְאֵהוּ, אֵינֶנּוּ עָמֹק" "וְרָאָהוּ הַכֹּהֵן, בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי, וְהִנֵּה הַנֶּגַע עָמַד בְּעֵינָיו, לֹא-פָשָׂה"{{fn:80}} (ויקרא יג, ה) טעמו בשעורו מלשון "וְלֹא כִהָה, בָּם" שהרי אמר "לֹא-פָשָׂה" ולא אמר ולא פשה אלא הוא באור למה שאמר "עָמַד בְּעֵינָיו" ואין הטעם במראהו מפני שאם יהיה זה במראהו יהיה טעם "וְהִיא כֵהָה" במראהו ויהיה טעם מפני שעמד על כן יהיה צריך הסגרה שבוע שני ומפני שכהה בשני אחר שלא פשה יהיה טהור מכלל אם עמד בעיניו בשני מה משפטו היהיה צריך הסגר שבוע אחד והלא לא מצאנו הסגר יותר משתי שבועות והכתוב לא באר אם עמד בעיניו בשני מה משפטו ולא אם כהה בראשון מה משפטו וחכמים אומרים כל זמן שהוא עומד במראהו צריך הסגר. והאמת מכח המאמרים הוא מה שנבאר כי אחרי שטהרו אם כהה בשני הוא הדין לטהרו אם כהה בראשון. אך אם עמד בשני במראהו אם הראשון יעדו להסגר בשני יהיה מוחלט כמו שנפרש בצרעת בתים. בעלי הקבלה אמרו שמאמר "וְהִיא כֵהָה" הטעם בו במראהו וכפי דבריהם איננו נראה כן מדין החקירה שאם יהיה זה הכהוי למטה מקרום הביצה אפילו אם פשה הוא טהור ומה טעם והיא כהה ולא פשה ואם הטעם בו שהיתה עזה כשלג ונעשית כקרום הביצה שהרי בדבריהם אין עזות המראה ולא בהיותה לאחד מארבע מראות סימן טמאה אלא השער והפשיון והמחיה ואע"פ כן ראיתי לפרשן אחד מהם שסתר את דבריהם באמרו האחד אם עומד במראהו או פשה יהיה טמא. ולפי הפשט אם לא פשה וכהה בהסגר שבוע שני יהיה טהור שכן אומר "וְטִהֲרוֹ הַכֹּהֵן מִסְפַּחַת הִוא, וְכִבֶּס בְּגָדָיו וְטָהֵר" (ויקרא יג, ו) יעדו בכבוס בגדים והוא מטמא אדם וכלים כיון שנסגר. וזאת הטהרה היא טהרה שלמה לקדש וקדשיו אינו מחוייב למה שנתפרש בפסוק "זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצֹרָע" (ויקרא יד, ב) ואומר "וְאִם-פָּשֹׂה תִפְשֶׂה הַמִּסְפַּחַת בָּעוֹר, אַחֲרֵי הֵרָאֹתוֹ אֶל-הַכֹּהֵן לְטָהֳרָתוֹ" (ויקרא יג, ז) וזו ראיה על דעת מי שאומר כי הפשיון לבד מטמא ולא עמידת מראהו שהרי לא אמר או שב למראהו ואמר "וְנִרְאָה שֵׁנִית, אֶל-הַכֹּהֵן" (ויקרא יג, ז) אין הטעם במאמר שנית אחרי הטהרה עד שיהיה פעם שלישית רק הטעם קודם הטהרה שנראה פעם שנית ונטהר ואם פשתה אחרי כן יטמאנו הכהן מצורע מוחלט. וקראה מספחת מלשון "וְנִסְפְּחוּ עַל-בֵּית יַעֲקֹב" (ישעיהו יד, א) ענינו האסיפה והקבוץ כיון שאמר והיא כהה ולא פשה שהרי היא נכללת בשם בהרת שנאמר "וְאִם-בַּהֶרֶת לְבָנָה הִוא" (ויקרא יג, ד). ולשון בהרת מלשון "בָּהִיר הוּא, בַּשְּׁחָקִים" (איוב לז, כא) שהוא ענין שנוי מראה ואינו לובן כי על כן  אמר "בַּהֶרֶת לְבָנָה" ותארה בלובן ועל כן לא שם אותה פרק בראשה:
content.english: The scripture said, "And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron"; because the leprosy affliction is dependent on all the appearances to the eyes of the priest, therefore it included the speech with Aaron, and it said, "When a man shall have in the skin of his flesh" (Lev 13:2), and it said "a man" to include a man and a woman, that they become unclean with afflictions, and it said, "a swelling or a scab or a bright spot" (Lev 13:2), and this section does not include except what are specific, because it made the matter of leprosy dependent on the appearance of the priest, and it obligated the sacrifice for all, and all this is dependent on what is specific, and it mentioned a swelling, a scab, and a bright spot, and it "will become a leprosy affliction" returns to each of the three afflictions. And the meaning of a swelling is that it is raised from the skin of the flesh, and a scab is neither raised nor deep, and a bright spot is deeper than the skin of the flesh. And the scripture began with the bright spot, from what it concluded, as is the custom of the scripture, and it said, "And he shall be brought to Aaron the priest, or to one of his sons the priests" (Lev 13:2), since it did not say "who will stand in his place," implying that the secondary priests are appropriate to judge in leprosy afflictions. And it said, "And he shall be brought to Aaron the priest," for if he will not come willingly, he will be brought against his will. "And the priest shall look at the affliction in the skin" (Lev 13:3), which is a bright spot, for so it said, "And if a bright spot is white" (Lev 13:4). And there are those who say that it is dim, since it said, "And if a bright spot is white," contrary to the statement of the Rabbanites, that it is intense as snow, and there is to say that it too is white, if the scripture did not explain, we would know this from the statement, "and the hair in the affliction has turned white" (Lev 13:3). And what it said, "and the hair in the affliction has turned white," teaches that there was hair in it and it turned white, not that it grew now, and "the appearance of the affliction is deeper than the skin," in the sense of a pit, and the meaning is, in there being one of the two signs, it would be unclean, for if in there being the two, it would be unclean, then in the absence of one of them, it did not indicate its statute, and this is impossible, implying that one sign of the two makes unclean. And if one were to say, and it would have been appropriate to say the statement "or his appearance," one can say that if it had said "or his appearance," I would have judged that if in one sign it would be unclean, in two signs it would be necessary for it to have an additional statute, and therefore it said "and his appearance," and likewise in the negation of the two signs, it said, "and its appearance is not deeper than the skin" (Lev 13:34), "and its hair has not turned white" (Lev 13:4), and it did not say "or its hair has not turned white," because I would say that in one sign it would require quarantine, and according to what we have explained, it is definitively unclean, and this necessarily because if in the presence of both it declares unclean and in the absence of both it quarantines, and in the absence of one of them one of three aspects is not formed, whether it is definitively unclean or quarantined or exempt. And for it to be exempt is impossible, because in the absence of two signs, I designated it for quarantine, and in the absence of one of them, it would be exempt, and for it to be quarantined is impossible, for the scripture did not designate for quarantine except in the absence of two signs, implying that it is definitively unclean with one sign, and if there is not one of the two, only the whiteness alone, it designated it for quarantine for seven days, as it says, "And if a bright spot is white in the skin of his flesh, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, then the priest shall shut up the affliction seven days" (Lev 13:4). I am astonished at the Rabbanites who said that the depth is not a sign of impurity, and then they returned and said that any affliction that does not have depth is not judged an affliction, and the scripture says, "and its appearance is not deeper," "And the priest shall look at him on the seventh day, and behold, the affliction has remained in his appearance, it has not spread" (Lev 13:5), its meaning is in its measure, from the expression "and did not dim them" that it already said "it has not spread," and it did not say "and it has not spread," but it is an explanation of what it said, "has remained in his appearance," and there is no meaning in its appearance, for if this were in its appearance, the meaning of "and it has become dim" would be in its appearance, and it would be the meaning because it has remained, therefore it would be necessary for a quarantine for a second week, and because it has become dim in the second after it did not spread, it would be pure, implying if it remained in its appearance in the second, what would be its law? Would it need a quarantine for another week? And we have not found a quarantine for more than two weeks, and the scripture did not explain if it remained in its appearance in the second, what would be its law? And not if it became dim in the first, what would be its law? And sages say that whenever it stands in its appearance, it requires quarantine. And the truth from the force of the statements is what we will explain, for after they purified it if it became dim in the second, the same applies to purify it if it became dim in the first. But if it stood in the second in its appearance like the first, they designated it for quarantine in the second, it would be definitively unclean, as we will explain in leprosy of houses. The Rabbanites said that the statement "and it has become dim" means in its appearance, and according to their words, it does not appear so from the law of inquiry, for if this dimness is lower than the membrane of an egg, even if it spread, it is pure, and what is the point of saying "and it has become dim and has not spread"? And if the meaning is in it that it was intense as snow and has become like the membrane of an egg, for there is no intensity of appearance in their words and not in its being to one of the four appearances a sign of impurity, except the hair and the spreading and the living flesh, and even though I saw one interpreter among them who contradicted their words, saying the one, if it stands in its appearance or spreads, it would be unclean. And according to the plain meaning, if it did not spread and became dim in quarantine in the second week, it would be pure, for so it says, "then the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a scab, and he shall wash his clothes and be clean" (Lev 13:6). It designated him to wash clothes, and it makes a person and vessels unclean, since it was quarantined. And this purification is complete purification for the consecrated and its holy things; it is not obligated to what was explained in the verse "This shall be the law of the leper" (Lev 14:2). And it says, "And if the scab has spread on the skin, after he was seen by the priest for his cleansing" (Lev 13:7), and this is a proof for the view of one who says that spreading alone makes unclean and not the standing of its appearance, for it did not say "or returns to its appearance," and it said, "and he shall be seen again by the priest" (Lev 13:7); the meaning is not in the statement again after the purification, until it would be a third time, but the meaning is before the purification, that it is seen a second time and is purified, and if it spread afterward, the priest will declare him a leper who is definitively unclean. And it called it an attachment, from the expression "And they shall join the house of Jacob" (Isa 14:1), its meaning is gathering and collecting, since it said "and it has become dim and has not spread," for it is included in the name of a bright spot, as it says, "And if a bright spot is white" (Lev 13:4). And the language of a bright spot is from the expression "It is bright in the skies" (Job 37:21), which is the matter of a change of appearance, and it is not whiteness, for therefore it said, "a white bright spot," and it described it with whiteness, and therefore it did not make it a section unto itself.
content.comments: 79 בְּשָׂרוֹ — In *Gan Eden* the verse from Lev 13:4 is quoted, only without the words "in the skin of his flesh." 80 לֹא-פָשָׂה" — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "and if on the seventh day it had not spread, nor faded, but stood in its appearance." I have not found such a verse. I have found Lev 13:5: "and the priest shall look upon him on the seventh day; and behold, the affliction stood in its appearance, the affliction had not spread in the skin."
