בֵּית אָבִיהָ" (במדבר ל, יז) אין הטעם בעוד שהיא נערה תוך ששה חדשים שמאמר נערה אמור על הבוגרת שנאמר "מִן-הַנַּעֲרָה, הַזֹּאת" (רות ד, יב) והיא שכובה. לא כפי דעת בעלי הקבלה שאמרו כי לא נשאת ועדיין היא נערה. ואיך יתכן גם כן שמאמר "וְאִם-הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ" (במדבר ל, ז) שהוא מרמיז על זמן היותה נערה ארושה בעודה בבית אביה שהאב והבעל מפירים עד שתבגור לא שמעו נדריה עד שתבגור אינם יכולים להפר ואין צריך לומר שנדרה בזמן הבגרות בעוד שהיה לה מארש ואב ואם ונשאת אין יכול הבעל להפר אלא מה שתדור בביתו. וכן אמרו שהאב והבעל מפירים ואם מת המארש האב מפר ואם מת האב הבעל אינו מפר והנה המארש מפר קודם שתכנס לחפה בשותפות עם האב ואחר שנשאת אין יכול המארש להפר מה שנדרה מקודם שתנשא ואלו דברים שאין להם שעור. ולא קלקלם כי אם מאמר "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" (במדבר ל, יא) שאם מאמר "וְאִם-הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ" בנשואה הכתוב מדבר מה טעם "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה":
content.english: In the section on vows, we find a change from other sections in that the speech of God to Moses is not mentioned, "And the Lord spoke to Moses," but rather it mentions Moses' speech to Israel and concludes with "this is the thing that the Lord commanded Moses." And there is reason to give for this because he concluded in the previous section: "These you shall prepare for the Lord in your appointed feasts, besides your vows and your freewill offerings" (Num 29:39). Thus, the procedures of vows were arranged, and it concludes: "And Moses spoke to the children of Israel concerning the appointed feasts of the Lord" (Lev 23:44), and therefore "Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, saying: 'This is the thing that the Lord has commanded'" (Num 30:2) is connected with what was said to him in the statement "besides your vows." However, we found that the commandments were transmitted in three ways. The first way is how God speaks to Moses and Moses speaks to Israel, for example, "And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: 'Speak to the children of Israel,'" and it does not mention that Moses spoke to Israel. And the second, we found that God speaks to Moses and does not mention the mission to Israel as it is, but that speech is understood from other statements, as was said to him on Mount Sinai, "Keep My Sabbaths" (Lev 26:2), and its matter was arranged in the section of Vayakhel, not in the form of those words. And the third, that it mentions that God spoke to Moses and mentions that he says them to Israel, such as in the section on appointed feasts, and it says, "And Moses declared to the children of Israel the appointed feasts of the Lord" (Lev 23:44). And it seems that this is a fourth category, for it mentions that he said them to Israel and does not mention elsewhere that it was said to him from the mouth of God, and we say that when he said "besides your vows," in this statement he explained to him the section on vows, and therefore "Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, saying..." was connected. And behold, he showed one correction, and it is a source for all the commandments, as it says, "And Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes." And there are those who say that he spoke to the heads of the tribes for the sake of the children of Israel, that they should tell their children the children of Israel. And there are those who say to add a "vav," and the meaning is "and to the children of Israel." And behold, the interpreters disagreed; there are those who say that Moses would speak to the heads of the congregation, and they would speak to Israel. Or we may say that before that he would speak to the heads of the tribes, and after that he would call Israel and arrange for them, and the heads of the tribes would also be listening. And there are those who say that at first he would arrange it for Aaron, and after that for the princes, and after that for all Israel, and Aaron and the princes and the elders would be there. It turns out that Aaron heard four times, and all of them heard from the mouth of Moses, as it says, "And Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the princes of the congregation returned to him" (Exod 34:31). And when it says here "to the heads," it includes everyone; what is the reason for mentioning here the heads of the tribes? To teach that anyone who wants to vow consults with the sages of the generation, and they give him proper advice. Or because the heads should be watchful and observant of everyone who makes a vow to fulfill it and not to violate the oath. And it says, "When a man makes a vow" (Num 30:3), and the term "man" applies to the mature person who is intelligent whose vow is a vow. And regarding the sign of maturity, the sages differ; some say that the sign of maturity is the years, and it is when he is twelve years old and the woman is twelve years old, and some say that the sign is the hair, and in women, the sign is the hair and the breasts, as it says, "Your breasts were formed and your hair grew" (Ezek 16:7). And the term "mature" is a term of translation where they call a hairy man "bagra." And others say that the sight of blood for a woman and semen for a man is a sign of maturity. And others say that the obligation of commandments is only for a person who has intelligence, and if so, the completeness of intelligence is a sign of maturity, and therefore there are those who have given the sign from the time of seeing a dream. And the truth is that when a person is intelligent, he is twelve years old, and this time is when hair appears, and therefore the examination of the appearance of hair is a sign of maturity. And we have already explained elsewhere the opinion of the Rabbanites. And it says, "When a man makes a vow," and the meaning of a vow is in a permitted thing, for things divide into three ways: obligatory, forbidden, and optional. And the obligatory is divided into that which is obligatory by reason and that which is obligatory by the Torah. And also the forbidden is divided into that which is forbidden by reason and that which is forbidden by the Torah. And the third category is the optional, and the optional is divided into that for which the doer is praised and the abandoner is not blamed, and that for which the doer is not praised and the abandoner is not blamed. And the matter of vows is from the third category, as it says, "But if you refrain from vowing, there shall be no sin in you" (Deut 23:23). And the true vow is to the name of the Lord. And there is a difference between a vow and a freewill offering. And the sages said that a vow is when he utters it with his mouth, and when he does not utter it with his mouth, it is a freewill offering, as it says, "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep and perform, according as you have vowed to the Lord your God, a freewill offering, which you have promised with your mouth" (Deut 23:24). And the Rabbanites said in saying "upon me a vow," and without "upon me" it is a freewill offering, and for vows one is liable for responsibility, and for a freewill offering one is not liable for responsibility, the reason being that what is found before him is a vow, and since it is lost, he is not liable for anything. And there are those who say that a vow would be conditional, whether precedent or subsequent. The precedent is like "If You will indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities" (Num 21:2), and like "If God will be with me" (Gen 28:20). And the subsequent like "If I come into the tent of my house, if I go up into the bed of my couch" (Ps 132:3). And what a person vows and is not dependent on a condition is called a freewill offering, and it is the third part of a vow, such as when a person vows to fast on Monday and Thursday or something else, and it is in the form of the optional. And there is a difference between a vow and a freewill offering, that for a vow, the doer is praised and the abandoner is blamed, and for a freewill offering, the doer is praised and the abandoner is not blamed. And what seems to be the truth is that this last type obligates a person even without a condition, and if he abandons it, he deserves blame. And the truth is that whether he says it with his mouth or does not say it with his mouth, whether it is conditional or without condition, if he does not obligate it upon himself but leaves it to the completion of his nature, it is called a freewill offering. And after saying "When he makes a vow," it says, "or swears an oath" (Num 30:3), and it is necessary to explain what is the reason for a vow and what is the reason for an oath, and this is not an argument, for just as we find an oath in what is in the way of obligation, as it says, "I have sworn and I will perform it" (Ps 119:106), so even though he is obligated by a vow, he is also obligated by an oath, as it says, "Who has sworn to the Lord and vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob" (Ps 132:2). And one who transgresses will be punished for both the vow and the oath, as it says, "Do not allow your mouth to cause your flesh to sin" (Eccl 5:5). And from the law of the oath, but the intention here in saying "or swears an oath" does not refer back to what it says, "When a man makes a vow," which is dedicated to the name of the Lord, but in saying "or swears an oath," it does not refer back because of the vow, therefore it dedicated the vow to the name of the Lord. But the oath would be about something else, such as swearing not to eat this food or not to drink this wine or not to speak with so-and-so, and therefore it says, "or swears an oath to bind himself" (Num 30:3), and therefore it did not say to the name of the Lord. And behold, the verse taught that it permitted him to forbid what is permitted and not to permit what is forbidden. And it needs to be among the possibilities, that he should not swear that he will stand in the sun all day during the heat or that he will not eat for seven consecutive days, for it says, "to bind himself," and if he stipulates in a matter to remove his soul, behold, his soul is not with him, and what will he bind upon his soul? And the Rabbanites distinguished between a vow and an oath in four ways: that in an utterance oath, an oath does not take effect upon an oath, but a vow takes effect upon a vow, such as one who says, "a sacrifice is upon me if I eat this, a sacrifice is upon me if I eat this," he is liable for two sacrifices. One who is appeased with an oath is exempt, but one who is appeased with a vow is liable, such as if a person vowed not to eat meat and another person heard and said, "and I am like him," and similarly for everything that is appeased and another matter between the one who vows and the vowed. A vow takes effect on a matter of commandment as on a matter of permission, but an oath only on permission, such as if he vowed not to eat matzah on Passover eve and not to sit in a sukkah, even though sitting in a sukkah is obligatory, sitting in a sukkah is forbidden to him, but an oath would not take effect on the commandment because the commandment is already established by the oath at Mount Sinai, and an oath does not take effect upon an oath, because one who swears forbids himself from the thing about which he swears, but one who vows forbids the vowed thing upon himself, and that thing is not sworn and standing from Mount Sinai, but our sages, may they rest in peace, do not judge so, for just as it is not proper to swear to nullify a commandment, so it is not proper to vow to nullify a commandment. They further said that a vow is on a thing that has substance, but not so an oath, such as saying, "my speech is forbidden to you." And the truth is that one law applies to both a vow and an oath, for in what the vow is fulfilled, the oath is fulfilled, and in what the oath is not proper, the vow is not proper, for so it says, "When a man makes a vow to the Lord or swears an oath" (Num 30:3), and it says, "he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth" (Num 30:3), and it includes both of them in the obligation as one. But in judgment they are divided, and behold, a vow does not take effect upon a vow. And a vow in speech is the thought of the heart, and if he uttered with his mouth something that his heart does not agree with, it is not a vow, and the Scripture says, "in order to capture the house of Israel by their heart" (Ezek 14:5), and his heart needs to be with his mouth together, for if he intended in his heart and did not utter with his mouth, it is nothing, because matters of the heart are not matters. And one who is appeased with a vow is appeased with an oath, such as one who says, "I swear such and such," and another hears and says, "and I am like you," it is an utterance of an oath, for behold, the princes swore in the matter of the Gibeonites, and all Israel were obligated. It is not proper to vow to nullify a commandment, and even if he forgot and vowed, and in his vow he nullifies a commandment, his vow is void. Vows of constraint, vows of inadvertence, vows of exaggeration, all are permitted, and the term "exaggeration" means foolishness; the translation of "What is the high place to which you go?" (Ezek 20:29) is "being foolish." After one who vows himself or another imposes a vow on him and he consents. A person cannot vow to permit the forbidden, but only to forbid the permitted, therefore anyone who says, "Any vow that I will vow shall be void," has not benefited by his speech, for so it says, "to bind himself." And one who vows conditionally or swears conditionally, if the condition is not fulfilled, the vow is void, such as one who heard that his servant had stolen and swore to sell him, and it was found that he was not a thief, he will not sell him, for he swore on a condition, and similarly for all like it. If he saw people eating his fruits and thought they were strangers and swore to punish them, and it was found to be his son or his brother, his oath is permitted because his intention was only on the condition that they were strangers. Or if he saw them eating his fruits, and among the strangers was also his son, and he swore to punish them, and when he saw that his son was there and he did not want to punish him had he known it was him, he is permitted, and the rest are forbidden. One who vows regarding things that he will not benefit from them should not forbid everything that comes from them because each one by itself has a name, such as if he vowed not to eat grapes, he drinks the wine; not to eat olives, he eats the oil, and vice versa. Anyone who vows not to eat for one day or month or year, or not to do work, if he says "this day, this month, this year," the meaning will be even if only a little remains of the day or month or year, his prohibition will be in that little time. But in saying "one day, one month, one year," the intention will be from day to day. And it says, "he shall not break his word" (Num 30:3), its interpretation is to profane, from the term profanation, and if it comes with a patach because it is from the emphatic form, like "And God led the people around" (Exod 13:18) from the causative form, and they do not fill the chet, and so "I will not profane," and the intention of the grammarians is not that it is from the emphatic form as Rabbi Aaron, may he rest in peace, thought. Or it is possible to say that they came with a patach to distinguish between them and "he shall begin to deliver Israel" (Judg 13:5), which is a term of beginning. And the one who interprets it as a term of hiding, like the meaning of "you shall not delay to pay it" (Deut 23:22), from the root of "and he will not wait for men" (Mic 5:6), the grammar did not want it, because the yod of the root of the verb is not omitted when it connects with the yod of the future tense except when a vav enters upon it to quiet the sheva, and even though there is an argument from the statement "and they shall cast lots upon Jerusalem" (Obad 1:11), it is a doubtful grammar, and if so, the meaning of "he shall not break" is he shall not profane, similar to "I will not break My covenant; and what My lips have uttered I will not alter" (Ps 89:35). But the Rabbanites said, he does not annul, but others annul for him, and they themselves say the annulment of vows and oaths has no root in the written Torah, and therefore they say the annulment of vows and oaths is floating in the air, but they say rabbi from rabbi up to Moses our teacher, may he rest in peace, and how they change the words of the living God! And it says, "he shall do according to all that proceeds out of his mouth" (Num 30:3), whether to do harm or to do good, and the meaning of "to do harm" is to harm himself, that he denies himself food and drink, everything that is for the affliction of the soul, and it says, "according to all that proceeds," excluding inadvertent, deaf, and mute. And in saying "according to all that proceeds out of his mouth" without addition and diminution and without change, such as if he vowed to fast and says, "I will give charity to the poor and avoid the affliction." And it is necessary to consider its time, if he specified a time for it, and if he forgot, he should fulfill it after that time, and in its essence and quality and quantity. And if he forgot, he needs to hold to the stricter interpretation that is stronger in his heart, in saying "according to all that proceeds out of his mouth," he needs to follow according to the agreement of any language what is appropriate from his speech alone, provided that there is the agreement of the heart, such as one who says, "I will not eat meat," and the understanding is beef and sheep meat; "I will not rise from my place," except when necessity comes. And behold, anyone who vows a vow needs to have the condition outside of the commandment, for anyone who makes a condition against the Torah, his condition is void and his vow is valid, and the condition is according to custom even though it is in the manner of transgression. And one who swears to nullify a commandment, his oath is void. And what the princes of Israel swore to the Gibeonites and upheld it, and nullified the negative commandment, "you shall not let any soul live" (Deut 20:16), the sages explained that this was conditional, that if they would come into their religion, as it says, "lest they teach you" (Deut 20:18). However, in the matter of Jonathan, it already says, "But Jonathan had not heard when his father made the people swear" (1Sam 14:27). And if it is written, "And the people rescued Jonathan" (1Sam 14:45), with their argument that they did not obligate him to judgment, for the success that was through him would testify that he did not sin, and this interpretation is not appropriate, for it is known that the Lord did not answer him because Jonathan did what he did, and also a difficulty in that the Scripture informed that Jonathan did not know, but what can be said is that after it became known to him that he made light of the commandment in the matter of the oath, what his father vowed, and therefore what happened happened. From here we can know that one who is negligent in vows and prohibitions is not acceptable before the Lord. However, after it says, "And the people rescued Jonathan," the sage says that the oath of the people adds to the oath of the king, and it is not proper to swear to nullify an oath, and the truth is that this is an inadvertent oath, not a deliberate oath, and he is liable to a sliding scale offering, and therefore the Lord aroused him until his sin was known to atone for the iniquity. And what it says, "And the people rescued Jonathan" means that they gave a reason for the matter that he was not deliberate, for the salvation came through him, and if he had been deliberate, the salvation would not have come through him. And it is permitted to vow and swear for others who are under one's authority and rule, such as what Hannah vowed for her son and Jephthah for his daughter and the heads of the people for the people, such as Saul and Ezra, and the meaning is not in saying "to bind himself" and not for others. But therefore it says "himself" because it refers to things that afflict the soul, as it says, "All vows and all binding oaths to afflict the soul" (Num 30:14). And after completing what a man vows or swears by himself, he wanted to explain the vow and oath of others, and said, "And when a woman makes a vow to the Lord" (Num 30:4), and this is for the mature woman who vowed a vow, for the vow of minors is not a vow, and if the opinion of the Talmudists who said, she is neither a minor nor a mature woman. I am astonished at this, for the Scripture says, "When a man makes a vow," and it refers to the mature man, and how in the statement "And when a woman makes a vow" would it not refer to a mature woman, but to less than a mature woman? And furthermore, the Scripture did not give a sign until what time the father will annul before she marries, but we learned from the Scripture that until she does not marry, she is under the authority of the father. And the truth is that she is mature after her vows have been validated. And if the Scripture says, "in her youth in her father's house" (Num 30:17), the meaning is not while she is a young woman within six months, for the term "young woman" is said for the mature woman, as it says, "from this young woman" (Ruth 4:12), and she was lying down, not according to the opinion of the Rabbanites who said that she had not married and was still a young woman. And how is it also possible that the statement "And if she is married to a husband" (Num 30:7) is hinting at the time when she is a young woman engaged while still in her father's house, that the father and the husband annul until she matures; if they did not hear her vows until she matures, they cannot annul, and there is no need to say that she vowed at the time of maturity while she had a fiancé and father and mother, and after she married, the husband cannot annul except what she vowed in his house. And so they said that the father and the husband annul, and if the fiancé died, the father annuls, and if the father died, the husband does not annul, and behold, the fiancé annuls before she enters the bridal chamber in partnership with the father, and after she is married, the fiancé cannot annul what she vowed before she was married, and these are things without measure. And what caused the problem for them is the verse, "And if in her husband's house she vowed" (Num 30:11), for if the statement "And if she is married to a husband" refers to a married woman, what is the reason to say, "And if in her husband's house she vowed"?
content.comments: 174 אֶת-יוֹנָתָן — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "and the people redeemed Yehonatan," whereas in 1Sam 14:45 it reads: "and the people redeemed Jonathan."

content.hebrew: ועתה נחפש דברי אלהים חיים כמשמעם אמר הכתוב "וְאִשָּׁה, כִּי-תִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַה', וְאָסְרָה אִסָּר בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ, בִּנְעֻרֶיהָ" (במדבר ל, ד). ואמר "וְשָׁמַע אָבִיהָ אֶת-נִדְרָהּ, וֶאֱסָרָהּ אֲשֶׁר אָסְרָה עַל-נַפְשָׁהּ" (במדבר ל, ה) בכל שמיעה ששמע ואמר "וְהֶחֱרִישׁ לָהּ, אָבִיהָ--וְקָמוּ, כָּל-נְדָרֶיהָ" (במדבר ל, ה). ואמר "בְּיוֹם שָׁמְעוֹ" ואינו מעת אל עת אלא יום כימי הבריאה באיזה עת  יהיה מן היום עד שישלם היום ואמרו חכמים שיש לו רשות כל היום להתיר ולאסור ואם הפר אותם יהיו מופרים וה' יסלח לה. ויש חכמים אומרים בעת שמעו עד שיאמר הין או לאו כל היום יש לו רשות. ואמר "וְאִם-הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ, וּנְדָרֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ, אוֹ מִבְטָא שְׂפָתֶיהָ" (במדבר ל, ז) ענין השבועה שנאמר לבטא בשפתים להרע או להטיב (ויקרא ה, ד). וצריך לחפש על מה שנאמר "וּנְדָרֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ" מה הם הנדרים אם נדרים שהוקמו בבית אביה או נדרים שלא הוקמו ולא הופרו. והנראה מכח הפשט שכולל בין נדרים שהוקמו בין אותם הנדרים שלא הוקמו ולא הופרו ורצה לבאר כי אחרי שתהיה לאיש מאז אין רשות לאב להפר כי אם הבעל אחרי כי מה שקיים האב מפר הבעל והנה אם הוא מפר שבביתו קל וחומר אע"פ כן יש חכמים שאמרו כי אינו רוצה רק על נדרים שלא הוקמו ולא הופרו כי על שהוקמו כיון שאמר "וְקָמוּ" איך יופרו.  ואמר "וְנֵדֶר אַלְמָנָה, וּגְרוּשָׁה--כֹּל אֲשֶׁר-אָסְרָה עַל-נַפְשָׁהּ, יָקוּם" (במדבר ל, י) אחד ארושה ואחד בעולה אחרי שנתאלמנה אין רשות לאב להפר. ואחרי כן אמר "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" (במדבר ל, יא). וצריך להבין על איזה צד מרמיז אחר שאמר "וְנֵדֶר אַלְמָנָה" וכנראה שהוא מרמיז על זאת האלמנה כשהיתה בבית בעלה ונדרה נדרים וקימם בעלה או הפרם אחרי שיצאה מרשות בעלה אל רשותה שלא תקיימם עוד. אלא  נדרים שנדרה בזמן אלמנותה לבד שלא תסבור כי כמו שיצאה מרשות האב אל רשות הבעל הבעל מפר אע"פ שקיים האב שלא תאמר כיון שמת בעלה ויצאה מרשותו אל רשותה אם הפר אותם הבעל תקיים אותה היא. והרצון בו הנדרים שנדרה בזמן אלמנותה תקים אבל מה שנדרה ביותה בעולה והפר אותם בעלה לא תקום בזמן אלמנותה. ואולם בזה הפסוק רבו הפירושים כפי הדעות החלוקות. לפי דעת בעלי הקבלה אחרי שאמר "וְאִם-הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ" מה טעם לומר "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" מכלל שהראשון מדבר על המאורשה והשני מדבר על הבעולה. והבדל יש בין המאורשה ובין הנשואה שבמאורשה מפר האב והמארש אבל המארש לא יפר לבדו. והלא מגלוי הכתוב שתלה הרצון לגמרי על המארש לפי דעתם להפר ולקיים ועוד שאם הכונה בכך למה התויך דבר האלמנה בין המאורשה ובין הבעולה אלא היה ראוי להקדים זכר הבעולה ואחרי כן האלמנה. ועוד שלפי דעתם המאורשה אם נתאלמנה בעוד שהיא נערה האב יפר. אך לפי דעת ר' סהל האומר כי נדריה עליה על נדרים שלא הוקמו ולא הופרו בין על דעת ר' יפת ז"ל אפילו על נדרים שהוקמו אומרים אין הטעם באמור "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" נקשר עם מאמר "וְאִם-הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ" כי מה בא הכתוב ללמד שאם בקודמין הוא מפר שבביתו קל וחומר על כן מפרשים מאמר "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" שנאמר אחרי "וְנֵדֶר אַלְמָנָה" כי תנשא האלמנה לבעל שני להורות שאין הבעל יכול להפר נדרי אלמנה. כי הנדרים שבביתו יפר לא הנדרים שנדרה בזמן אלמנותה. והכריע רבינו אהרן נ"ע לשתי הדעות שאם כונת הכתוב מפני שיצאה מרשות האב לרשות הבעל יפר הבעל הוא הדין כיון שיצאה מרשותה אל רשות הבעל יפר הבעל. וכנראה שזאת הטענה תאות לפי דעת ר' יפת נ"ע מפני שר' סהל אומר "וּנְדָרֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ" על נדרים שלא הוקמו ולא הופרו אך דבריו אינם נראים. ועם ההשלמה לפי דעתו מה בא הכתוב ללמד שאם נדרים שקיים אביה אינו מפר גם מה שקיימה היא בזמן אלמנותה ונשאת לא יפר אותם הבעל ואיך יהיה עולה בדעת פן ידמו נדרי האלמנה לנדרי הפנויה שלא הוקמו ולא הופרו כיון שהיא תלויה ברשות האב על כן בא הכתוב להורות כי זה לא היה עולה בדעת ומה בא הכתוב להבדיל. והחכם רבינו אהרן נ"ע אמר כי בפירוש הנכון אין ראוי לומר שמאמר "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" הכונה שתנשא האלמנה בבעל שני ופירש כי הכונה בו באמור "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" שלא יאמר האיש בשעת מותו לאשתו כל נדר שתדרי עד שאת שומרת מטתי יהיו מופרים אלא הנדרים שנדרה בביתו יפר. וכן נמי ההולך למדינת הים מפני שאמר "בְּיוֹם שָׁמְעוֹ" ואינו נראה כן אחרי הפשט כי לפי זה הפירוש כנראה שאמר זה המאמר ללמד בדבר אחר וזה לא יתכן. אכן הכונה בעבור שאמר "וְנֵדֶר אַלְמָנָה, וּגְרוּשָׁה--כֹּל אֲשֶׁר-אָסְרָה עַל-נַפְשָׁהּ, יָקוּם". והיה נראה שאם נדרה בעוד שהיא בעולת בעל ונפל הנדר בזמן אלמנותה הורה הכתוב שאותו הנדר שנדרה בבית אישה יהיה כפי רשות בעלה אם קיים ואם הפר אע"פ שנופל הנדר בזמן אלמנותה ועל כן חשש לומר "וְאִם-בֵּית אִישָׁהּ, נָדָרָה" וזהו הפירוש הנכון אחרי הפשט. והנשים הם לארבעה חלקים האחת פנויה השנית יתומה השלישית בעולה והרביעית אלמנה וגרושה והנה האב יש לו להפר ולא האם. אמר הכתוב "כָּל-נֵדֶר וְכָל-שְׁבֻעַת אִסָּר, לְעַנֹּת נָפֶשׁ" (במדבר ל, יד) שחבר זה המאמר אצל הפרת הבעל הבדילו בין נדרים שיפר הבעל שנשא האלמנה לפי דעתם ובין נדרים שיפר האב כי הבעל לא יפר אלא כל מה שתלוי בענוי הנפש כגון צום וזולתו. והאמת שכלל זה המאמר למד מסופו ולכלם דין אחד כי כל מה שיש לו ענוי נפש יש לו רשות להפר. ובעלי הקבלה אמרו באמור הכתוב "אֵלֶּה הַחֻקִּים, אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה' אֶת-מֹשֶׁה" (במדבר ל, יז) הוקשו כלם יחד. נדרה ושמע האב או הבעל והפר והיא לא ידעה שהפרו ועברה על נדרה או על שבועתה חייבת משום שנתכונה להתיר האסור. נדרה ועברה קודם שיפר לה בעלה או אביה אע"פ שיפר בו ביום חייבת. שמע האב או הבעל את נדרה ולא ידעו כי הם מפירים או לא ידעו כי אותו הנדר צריך הפרה ובעת שהכירו יש להם להפר. וצריך הבעל או האב לומר לה מופר נדרך בטלה שבועתך לא שיבטלם בלבו לבד אפילו שלא יאמר אלא נדרה שלא תאכל בשר והוא נתן לה בשר לאכול בטל נדרה. אין רשות לבעל או לאב לומר כל נדר שתדרי וכל שבועה שתשבעי יהיו בטלים כי הכתוב אמר "בְּיוֹם שָׁמְעוֹ" וקודם שמעו איך יפר ואפילו עבר מזמן הנדר זמן רב מפר בעת שישמע והפרה תהיה בין על ידי עצמו בין על ידי כתב בין על ידי שליח. נדרה נדר והפר מקצתו וקיים מקצתו מה שהפר מופר ומה שקיים קיים ואמר הכתוב "וְאִם-הַחֲרֵשׁ יַחֲרִישׁ לָהּ אִישָׁהּ, מִיּוֹם אֶל-יוֹם" וגו' (במדבר ל, טו) הורה הכתוב שאם עמד האב או הבעל ולא הפר בו ביום יהיו נדריה קימים. ואמר "וְאִם-הָפֵר יָפֵר אֹתָם, אַחֲרֵי שָׁמְעוֹ" (במדבר ל, טז) הטעם אחרי יום שמעו ואמר "וְנָשָׂא, אֶת-עֲוֺנָהּ" הטעם ענשה. ואמר "אֵלֶּה הַחֻקִּים, אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה' אֶת-מֹשֶׁה" וגו' בעבור שענין הנדר ענין ראוי וכשר קודם בוא התורה כאשר מצאנו מענין יעקב אבינו ע"ה ואברהם אבינו ע"ה אבל לא יהיו על פי התנאים האלה ועל כן שם נדר הוא שם של תורה אע"פ שעקרו מן הלשון בעבור התנאים שנוספו לו מדין תורה. והתורה הכשירה ענין הנדר במקומות רבים כאשר אמרה "לְפַלֵּא-נֶדֶר אוֹ בִנְדָבָה" (במדבר טו, ג). ואמר "נְדָבָה תַּעֲשֶׂה אֹתוֹ, וּלְנֵדֶר לֹא יֵרָצֶה" (ויקרא כב, כג). ואמר "אֵלֶּה תַּעֲשׂוּ לַה', בְּמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם--לְבַד מִנִּדְרֵיכֶם וְנִדְבֹתֵיכֶם" (במדבר כט, לט) ובעבור שבאה התורה והוסיפה תנאים מה שלא תסכים הדעת בהם על כן אמר "אֵלֶּה הַחֻקִּים, אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה' אֶת-מֹשֶׁה, בֵּין אִישׁ, לְאִשְׁתּוֹ" (במדבר ל, יז) ממה שהשלים החל "בֵּין-אָב לְבִתּוֹ" ואמר "בִּנְעֻרֶיהָ בֵּית אָבִיהָ" (במדבר ל, יז):
content.english: And now let us search the words of the living God according to their meaning. The Scripture says, "And when a woman makes a vow to the Lord or binds herself by a bond in her father's house in her youth" (Num 30:4). And it says, "And her father hears her vow and her bond that she has bound upon her soul" (Num 30:5) in any hearing that he heard, and it says, "and her father keeps silent to her, all her vows shall stand" (Num 30:5). And it says, "on the day he hears," and it is not from time to time but a day like the days of creation, at whatever time it may be from the day until the day is completed, and the sages said that he has permission all day to permit and to forbid, and if he annulled them, they will be annulled, and the Lord will forgive her. And there are sages who say at the time he hears until he says yes or no, all day he has permission. And it says, "And if she is indeed married to a husband, and her vows are upon her, or the utterance of her lips" (Num 30:7), the matter of the oath that is said to utter with the lips to do harm or to do good (Lev 5:4). And it is necessary to search about what is said, "and her vows are upon her," what are these vows, whether vows that were established in her father's house or vows that were neither established nor annulled. And what appears from the force of the plain meaning is that it includes both vows that were established and those vows that were neither established nor annulled, and he wanted to explain that after she is married to a husband, from then on the father has no authority to annul, only the husband, since what the father established, the husband annuls, and behold, if he annuls what is in his house, all the more so, nevertheless there are sages who said that he only refers to vows that were neither established nor annulled, for regarding those that were established, since it says, "shall stand," how will they be annulled? And it says, "And a vow of a widow or a divorced woman, all that she has bound upon her soul shall stand" (Num 30:10), whether engaged or married, after she became a widow, the father has no authority to annul. And after that it says, "And if in her husband's house she vowed" (Num 30:11). And it is necessary to understand in what way it refers, after saying, "And a vow of a widow," and it seems that it refers to this widow when she was in her husband's house and vowed vows, and her husband established them or annulled them, after she left the authority of her husband to her own authority, that she would not establish them again, but only vows that she vowed during the time of her widowhood, so that she should not think that just as she left the authority of the father to the authority of the husband, the husband annuls even though the father established, that she should not say, since her husband died and she left his authority to her own authority, if the husband annulled them, she will establish them herself. And the intention is vows that she vowed during the time of her widowhood will be established, but what she vowed while she was married and her husband annulled them, she will not establish in the time of her widowhood. However, on this verse, interpretations are many according to the different opinions. According to the opinion of the Rabbanites, after saying, "And if she is indeed married to a husband," what is the reason to say, "And if in her husband's house she vowed," which implies that the first speaks of the engaged woman and the second speaks of the married woman? And there is a difference between the engaged woman and the married woman, that for the engaged woman, the father and the fiancé annul, but the fiancé will not annul alone. But from the plain meaning of the text, it depends entirely on the fiancé according to their opinion to annul and establish, and furthermore, if the intention is such, why did he insert the matter of the widow between the engaged woman and the married woman, but it would have been proper to mention the married woman first and then the widow? And furthermore, according to their opinion, the engaged woman, if she became a widow while she is still a young woman, the father will annul. But according to the opinion of Rabbi Sahl, who says that "her vows are upon her" refers to vows that were neither established nor annulled, or according to the opinion of Rabbi Yefet, may his memory be blessed, even to vows that were established, they say that the meaning of "And if in her husband's house she vowed" is not connected with the statement "And if she is indeed married to a husband," for what has the Scripture come to teach? That if in the former cases he annuls those in his house, all the more so for those now. Therefore, they interpret the statement "And if in her husband's house she vowed," which is said after "And a vow of a widow," that if the widow marries a second husband, to teach that the husband cannot annul the vows of a widow, for the vows in his house he will annul, not the vows that she vowed in the time of her widowhood. And Rabbi Aaron, may he rest in peace, decided between the two opinions that if the intention of the verse is because she left the authority of the father to the authority of the husband, the husband will annul, that is the law since she left her own authority to the authority of the husband, the husband will annul. And it seems that this argument is suitable according to the opinion of Rabbi Yefet, may his memory be blessed, because Rabbi Sahl says "and her vows are upon her" refers to vows that were neither established nor annulled, but his words do not seem correct. And with the completion according to his opinion, what has the Scripture come to teach, that if vows that her father established he does not annul, also what she established during the time of her widowhood and married, the husband will not annul them, and how would it enter the mind that perhaps the vows of the widow are like the vows of the unmarried woman that were neither established nor annulled, since she is dependent on the authority of the father, therefore the Scripture came to teach that this would not enter the mind, and what did the Scripture come to distinguish? And the sage Rabbi Aaron, may his memory be blessed, said that in the correct interpretation it is not proper to say that the statement "And if in her husband's house she vowed" means that the widow marries a second husband, and he explained that the intention of it in saying "And if in her husband's house she vowed" is that the man should not say at the time of his death to his wife, "Any vow that you vow while you are keeping my bed shall be annulled," but only the vows that she vowed in his house he will annul. And so also one who goes to a distant country, because it says, "on the day he hears," and it does not seem so after the plain meaning, for according to this interpretation it seems that it said this statement to teach about something else, and this is not appropriate. However, the intention is because it says, "And a vow of a widow or a divorced woman, all that she has bound upon her soul shall stand," and it would seem that if she vowed while she was married to a husband and the vow fell in the time of her widowhood, the verse teaches that that vow that she vowed in her husband's house will be according to the authority of her husband, whether he established or annulled it, even though the vow falls in the time of her widowhood, and therefore it was careful to say, "And if in her husband's house she vowed," and this is the correct interpretation after the plain meaning. And women are divided into four categories: the first is unmarried, the second is orphaned, the third is married, and the fourth is widowed and divorced, and behold, the father has the power to annul but not the mother. The Scripture says, "All vows and all binding oaths to afflict the soul" (Num 30:14), that it connected this statement next to the husband's annulment, it distinguished between vows that the husband annuls, who married the widow according to their opinion, and between vows that the father annuls, for the husband will not annul except everything that depends on the affliction of the soul, such as fasting and the like. And the truth is that this statement includes, learning from its end, and for all of them one law, for everything that has affliction of the soul, he has authority to annul. And the Rabbanites said in saying, "These are the statutes that the Lord commanded Moses" (Num 30:17), they all were compared together. If she vowed and the father or husband heard and annulled, and she did not know that they had annulled, and she transgressed her vow or her oath, she is liable because she intended to permit the forbidden. If she vowed and transgressed before her husband or father annulled for her, even though he annulled on that day, she is liable. If the father or husband heard her vow and did not know that they were annulling, or did not know that that vow needed annulment, and when they recognized it, they have the right to annul. And the husband or father needs to say to her, "Your vow is annulled, your oath is voided," not that he voids them in his heart alone; even if he does not say anything except that she vowed not to eat meat and he gave her meat to eat, her vow is void. The husband or father has no authority to say, "Any vow that you vow and any oath that you swear shall be void," for the Scripture says, "on the day he hears," and before he hears, how will he annul? And even if a long time has passed from the time of the vow, he annuls at the time he hears, and the annulment will be whether by himself or by a letter or by a messenger. If she vowed a vow and he annulled part of it and established part of it, what he annulled is annulled and what he established is established, and the Scripture says, "And if her husband indeed keeps silent to her from day to day" etc. (Num 30:15), the verse teaches that if the father or husband stood and did not annul on that day, her vows will be established. And it says, "And if he indeed annulled them after he heard" (Num 30:16), the meaning is after the day he heard, and it says, "he shall bear her iniquity," the meaning is her punishment. And it says, "These are the statutes that the Lord commanded Moses" etc., because the matter of the vow is a proper and appropriate matter before the coming of the Torah, as we found from the matter of Jacob our father, peace be upon him, and Abraham our father, peace be upon him, but they were not according to these conditions, and therefore the term "vow" is a term of the Torah, even though its root is from the language, because of the conditions that were added to it from the law of the Torah. And the Torah approved the matter of the vow in many places, as it said, "to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering" (Num 15:3). And it says, "As a freewill offering you may prepare it, but for a vow it will not be accepted" (Lev 22:23). And it says, "These you shall prepare for the Lord in your appointed feasts, besides your vows and your freewill offerings" (Num 29:39), and because the Torah came and added conditions that reason would not agree with, therefore it says, "These are the statutes that the Lord commanded Moses, between a man and his wife" (Num 30:17), from what he completed, he began "between a father and his daughter," and it says, "in her youth in her father's house" (Num 30:17).

content.hebrew: צריך האדם להזהר בענין הנדרים כאשר נאמר "אַל-תִּתֵּן אֶת-פִּיךָ, לַחֲטִיא אֶת-בְּשָׂרֶךָ" (קהלת ה, ה) ונאמר "טוֹב, אֲשֶׁר לֹא-תִדֹּר--מִשֶּׁתִּדּוֹר, וְלֹא תְשַׁלֵּם" (קהלת ה, ד) ונאמר "כִּי-תִדֹּר נֶדֶר לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, לֹא תְאַחֵר לְשַׁלְּמוֹ" וגו' (דברים כג, כב) ונאמר "מוֹצָא שְׂפָתֶיךָ, תִּשְׁמֹר" וכו' (דברים כג, כד) ונאמר "לְךָ דֻמִיָּה תְהִלָּה אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן; וּלְךָ, יְשֻׁלַּם-נֶדֶר" (תהילים סה, ב):
content.english: A person needs to be careful in the matter of vows, as it says, "Do not allow your mouth to cause your flesh to sin" (Eccl 5:5), and it says, "It is better that you should not vow than that you should vow and not pay" (Eccl 5:4), and it says, "When you make a vow to the Lord your God, do not delay to pay it" etc. (Deut 23:22), and it says, "That which has gone out of your lips you shall keep" etc. (Deut 23:24), and it says, "Praise awaits You, O God, in Zion, and to You shall vows be performed" (Ps 65:2).

content.hebrew: נשלם ענין הנדרים      בשם משפיל ומרים
content.english: The matter of vows is completed, in the name of the One who humbles and raises up.

content.hebrew: דין הנזיר
content.english: The Law of the Nazirite.

content.hebrew: אזהרת השבועה מצאנוה בכתוב בשני מקומות באמרו בעשרת הדברים "לֹא תִשָּׂא אֶת-שֵׁם-ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ, לַשָּׁוְא" (שמות כ, ז) ונשנית בפסוק "וְלֹא-תִשָּׁבְעוּ בִשְׁמִי, לַשָּׁקֶר" (ויקרא יט, יב). ואין שבועה שחייבים עליה אלא כשתהיה אזכרת השם שהוא שם ה' ושאר כל שמותיו מפסוק "וְלֹא-תִשָּׁבְעוּ בִשְׁמִי, לַשָּׁקֶר". היתה שבועה שאין בה אזכרת ה' משמותיו שחייב לקיים כגון השבועה במקדש בתורה או בנביא אין חייבין בבית דין. אחד שבועת בטוי ואחד שבועת אלה אלו שני המינים מצאנום בכתוב לשני מינים. האחד כגון "חַי-ה'; שִׁכְבִי, עַד-הַבֹּקֶר" (רות ג, יג). והשני "ה'{{fn:175}} אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי-אֶחְקֹר אֶת-אָבִי" (שמואל א כ, יב) וזה יקרא חסר השבועה. ואולם האלה גם כן תחלק המין האחד כגון שיאמר "אָרוּר הָאִישׁ לִפְנֵי ה', אֲשֶׁר יָקוּם וּבָנָה אֶת-הָעִיר הַזֹּאת אֶת-יְרִיחוֹ{{fn:176}}" (יהושע ו, כו) והשני כגון "כֹּה-יַעֲשֶׂה-לִּי אֱלֹהִים וְכֹה יוֹסִף" (מלכים א ב, כג) וגם זה יקרא חסר השבועה. והנה התורה כמו שמנעה מן השבועה כן הכשירה השבועה כאמור "וּבִשְׁמוֹ, תִּשָּׁבֵעַ" (דברים ו, יג). וצריך להעיר הדברים להורות על איזה מין נמנע מן השבועה ועל איזה מין תכשר השבועה. ויש לדעת שהדברים נחלקים לשלשה חלקים. מחוייב נמנע אפשר. ומצאנו גם כן שיחס על השבועה שוא ושקר. ומדין לשוננו יש הבדל בין כזב ובין שוא שהכזב מבטיח ואינו עושה כגון אל תכזב בשפחתך (מלכים ב ד, טז) אשר לא יכזבו מימיו (ישעיהו נח, יא) אם כן הוא מורה על דבר שאפשר להיות. והשוא במה שאי אפשר להיות ועל כן אמר "שָׁוְא וּדְבַר-כָּזָב, הַרְחֵק מִמֶּנִּי" (משלי ל, ח) ואם כן השבועה באלה שני החלקים אסרם הכתוב. ואולם הנשבע על המוכרח במציאותו במה שאין בו חלוף הוא מחלק השוא כגון הנשבע שהמשולש שלשת זויותיו שוות לשתים נצבות. וגם הנשבע על הנמנע במה שאין בו חלוף הוא מחלק השוא כגון הנשבע שקוטר המרובע שוה לצלעו ועל כל כיוצא בו במה שאינו יכול כגון שלא יישן ולא יאכל ולא ישתה והנשבע על הברור במה שאין בו חלוף זהו מחלק השוא. ואולם האפשר נחלק לשלשה חלקים העובר ההוה והבא. העובר כגון הנשבע שלא יאכל והוא אבל או שכחש הפקדון אשר הפקד אתו או שגזל או עשק ועל כל כיוצא בהם. וכן בהוה הנשבע על ראובן שהוא יושב בבית שהוא עומד זהו הנקרא שבועת שקר. אך על העתיד מה שהוא מחויב מן התורה כגון שבת ומילה אם נשבע לבטלם הוא מחלק השוא וכן הנשבע לבטל מה שנשבע לקיימו גם זו שבועת שוא. והנשבע להרע במה שמנעה התורה והדעת הוא שבועת שוא אכן יכשר להשבע לקיים המצוה כגון שאמר "נִשְׁבַּעְתִּי וָאֲקַיֵּמָה" (תהילים קיט, קו). והנשבע חוץ ממה שסדרנו הנשבע צריך לקים אותה והתורה הכשירה זה על דרך החזוק כגון השבועה בזווג האשה כגון שקדם לנו הבאור. והשבועה על הפקדון שנגנב להחזיק טענתו באמור "שְׁבֻעַת ה', תִּהְיֶה בֵּין שְׁנֵיהֶם" (שמות כב, י). ויש שבועת חובה כגון האשה בזנות אשר לא תנקה אלא בשבועת האלה ואלו שבועות חובות. ויש שבועה ראויה כגון הנשבע לעשות חסד עם אדם או ישבע לאסור אסר על נפשו כגון שיצום או יתפלל וכיוצא בהם. ויש שבועה עוברת כגון שישבע שלא ישב בעיר או במדינה פלונית או לדחות הזק או להביא הועלה שיאמנו דבריו לזולתו. ויש שבועה נוהגת לראשי האמה ומנהיגיה לחזוק הדת והדין על ידי שבועה כגון שבועת אסא והאבות בבית שני. ויש אשר אינה לחזוק הדת והדין כי אם על צד ההסכמה כגון שנאמר "וַיֹּאֶל שָׁאוּל אֶת-הָעָם" (שמואל א יד, כד). כבר בארנו כי השבועה אשר חייבה התורה עליה עונש היא אשר יש בה אזכרת השם. אכן תקיעת כף הנזכרה והחמירו בה הדורות יותר משבועה עד שבארו חכמים שבזה מרמיז באמרו "וְהִנֵּה נָתַן יָדוֹ וְכָל-אֵלֶּה עָשָׂה, לֹא יִמָּלֵט" (יחזקאל יז, יח) שהוא תקיעת כף אמרו בעלי הקבלה שלא נהגו הדורות להחמיר בה יותר משבועה אלא להקל להמנע מעונש השבועה. והמרבה בשבועות מחלל שם שמים והנשבע על דברים בטלים מחלל שם שמים. כבר נתבאר כי הנשבע שלא יאכל בשר אם עבר ואכל אין זה נשבע על שקר כי בעת שנשבע באמת נשבע על מה שהיה לבו עם פיו שוים אלא הוא עובר משום לא יחל דברו. אסור לו לאדם להרגיל לשונו בשבועה ואפילו בדבר אמת שנאמר "הַנִּשְׁבָּע, כַּאֲשֶׁר שְׁבוּעָה יָרֵא" (קהלת ט, ב) והכתוב איים על הנשבע לשקר שנאמר "וְקָרַבְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶם, לַמִּשְׁפָּט, וְהָיִיתִי עֵד מְמַהֵר בַּמְכַשְּׁפִים וּבַמְנָאֲפִים, וּבַנִּשְׁבָּעִים לַשָּׁקֶר" (מלאכי ג, ה) שהשבועה באמונה תובעת לקיום מציאותו ית' ונאמר "הוֹצֵאתִיהָ, נְאֻם ה' צְבָאוֹת{{fn:177}}, וּבָאָה אֶל-בֵּית הַגַּנָּב" (זכריה ה, ד). ובעבור שמתפתה האדם ביותר בעון השבועה שהוא בטואי שפה על כן איימה התורה "כִּי לֹא יְנַקֶּה ה', אֵת אֲשֶׁר-יִשָּׂא אֶת-שְׁמוֹ לַשָּׁוְא" (שמות כ, ז). ונתבאר בספרי החכמים כי מי שנשבע על דבר על פי צורה ידועה ואחר כך נשתנה הדבר מאותה הצורה או נוסף בו ענין או נגרע ממנו ענין אם חוזר משבועתו אינו מבטל השבועה כי השבועה מתקיימת על פי אותה הצורה. נהיה באותו הדבר שום שנוי חוזר משבועתו ואינו נלכד על ידי חטא ועון אלא מפני שראו כזה בדברי הנביאים כמו זה המנהג ולא גנהו הכתוב באמור דוד המלך ע"ה "חַי-ה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲשֶׁר מְנָעַנִי, מֵהָרַע אֹתָךְ: כִּי לוּלֵי מִהַרְתְּ, וַתָּבֹאת לִקְרָאתִי--כִּי{{fn:178}} אִם-נוֹתַר לְנָבָל עַד-אוֹר הַבֹּקֶר, מַשְׁתִּין בְּקִיר" (שמואל א כה, לד) ולא נשבע אלא על דעת שלא סבר בדעתו כי אביגיל הולכת אצלו למנעו מבלתי בוא בדמים ובאה היא ומנעה אותו מן השבועה לבלתי געת בו ועל זה התירו לאדם שאם ישבע בדבר ולאחר זאת נודע לו הדבר באיכותו וכמותו ויש לו שנוי על מה שסבר בדעתו ונשבע עליו חוזר על מה שהיה בתחלה ואין עליו חטא ועון:
content.english: We find the warning about oaths in the Scripture in two places, saying in the Ten Commandments, "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain" (Exod 20:7), and it is repeated in the verse, "And you shall not swear by My name falsely" (Lev 19:12). And there is no oath for which one is liable except when there is mention of the Name, which is the name of the Lord and all His other names, from the verse, "And you shall not swear by My name falsely." If there was an oath in which there is no mention of the Lord from His names that one is obligated to fulfill, such as an oath by the Temple, by the Torah, or by a prophet, one is not liable in court. Both an oath of utterance and an oath of imprecation, these two types we found in the Scripture as two types. The first, such as "As the Lord lives, lie down until morning" (Ruth 3:13). And the second, "The Lord God of Israel, for I will search out my father" (1Sam 20:12), and this is called lacking the oath. However, the imprecation is also divided; the first type is such as one who says, "Cursed is the man before the Lord who rises up and builds this city, Jericho" (Josh 6:26), and the second, such as "God do so to me and more also" (1Kgs 2:23), and this is also called lacking the oath. And behold, the Torah, just as it prohibited oaths, so it approved oaths, as it says, "And by His name you shall swear" (Deut 6:13). And it is necessary to clarify the matters to teach about which type we are prohibited from swearing and about which type the oath is approved. And it should be known that matters are divided into three categories: obligatory, prohibited, and possible. And we also found that it attributed to oaths "vain" and "false." And according to our language, there is a difference between a lie and vanity, that a lie is promising and not doing, such as "do not lie to your maidservant" (2Kgs 4:16), "which will not lie" (Isa 58:11), so it indicates something that is possible to be. And vanity is what is impossible to be, and therefore it says, "Remove falsehood and lying far from me" (Prov 30:8), and if so, the oath in these two categories is forbidden by the Scripture. However, one who swears about what is necessary in its existence, in what has no alternative, is of the category of vanity, such as one who swears that the sum of the angles of a triangle equals two right angles. And also one who swears about what is impossible, in what has no alternative, is of the category of vanity, such as one who swears that the diagonal of a square equals its side, and about everything similar to it in what is not possible, such as that he will not sleep and will not eat and will not drink, and one who swears about what is clear, in what has no alternative, this is of the category of vanity. However, the possible is divided into three categories: the past, the present, and the future. The past, such as one who swears that he did not eat when he did eat, or that he denied the deposit that was deposited with him, or that he stole or oppressed, and about all similar to these. And so in the present, one who swears about Reuben that he is sitting in the house when he is standing, this is called a false oath. But about the future, what is obligatory from the Torah, such as the Sabbath and circumcision, if he swears to nullify them, it is of the category of vanity, and so one who swears to nullify what he swore to fulfill, this too is an oath of vanity. And one who swears to do harm in what the Torah and reason forbid is an oath of vanity, but it is proper to swear to fulfill the commandment, such as saying, "I have sworn and I will perform it" (Ps 119:106). And one who swears apart from what we have arranged who swears needs to fulfill it, and the Torah approved this by way of strengthening, such as the oath in the marriage of a woman, such as the explanation that preceded us. And the oath on a deposit that was stolen to strengthen his claim, as it says, "An oath of the Lord shall be between them both" (Exod 22:10). And there is an obligatory oath, such as a woman in adultery who will not be cleared except by the oath of imprecation, and these are obligatory oaths. And there is a proper oath, such as one who swears to do kindness with a person, or swears to bind himself, such as to fast or pray and the like. And there is a transient oath, such as swearing not to sit in a certain city or country, or to push away harm or to bring benefit so that his words will be believed by others. And there is an oath practiced by the heads of the nation and its leaders to strengthen religion and law through an oath, such as the oath of Asa and the fathers in the Second Temple. And there is that which is not to strengthen religion and law, but by way of agreement, such as it says, "And Saul had adjured the people" (1Sam 14:24). We have already explained that the oath for which the Torah obligated punishment is that in which there is mention of the Name. However, the handshake that is mentioned, and the generations were stricter about it more than an oath, until the sages explained that this is hinted at in saying, "Behold, he has given his hand and has done all these things, he shall not escape" (Ezek 17:18), which is a handshake, the Rabbanites said that the generations did not practice being stricter about it more than an oath except to be lenient to avoid the punishment of the oath. And one who multiplies oaths profanes the name of Heaven, and one who swears about vain matters profanes the name of Heaven. It has already been explained that one who swears not to eat meat, if he transgressed and ate, this is not swearing falsely, for at the time he swore, he swore truthfully about what his heart and his mouth were in agreement, but he transgresses "he shall not break his word." It is forbidden for a person to accustom his tongue to oaths, even in a matter of truth, as it says, "He who swears as he who fears an oath" (Eccl 9:2), and the Scripture threatened one who swears falsely, as it says, "I will come near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, against the adulterers, and against those who swear falsely" (Mal 3:5), for the oath in faith demands the fulfillment of His existence, blessed be He, and it says, "I have brought it forth, says the Lord of hosts, and it shall enter the house of the thief" (Zech 5:4). And because a person is more easily seduced in the sin of oaths, which is in the utterance of the lips, therefore the Torah threatened, "For the Lord will not hold him guiltless who takes His name in vain" (Exod 20:7). And it has been explained in the books of the sages that one who swears about a matter in a certain form, and afterward the matter changed from that form, or something was added to it or subtracted from it, if he retracts from his oath, he is not nullifying the oath, for the oath is fulfilled according to that form. If there is any change in that matter, he retracts from his oath and is not caught by sin and iniquity, but because they saw something like this in the words of the prophets with this custom, and the Scripture did not condemn it, as King David, peace be upon him, said, "As the Lord God of Israel lives, who has kept me back from hurting you, for unless you had hastened and come to meet me, surely by morning light no male would have been left to Nabal" (1Sam 25:34), and he only swore on the understanding that he did not think in his mind that Abigail was going to him to prevent him from coming with bloodshed, and she came and prevented him from the oath not to touch him, and on this they permitted a person that if he swears in a matter and afterward the matter becomes known to him in its quality and quantity, and it has a change from what he thought in his mind and swore about it, he returns to what was at first, and there is no sin and iniquity upon him. For example, if he saw people eating his fruits and thought they were strangers and swore to punish them, and it was found to be his son or his brother, his oath is permitted because his intention was only on the condition that they were strangers. Or if he saw them eating his fruits, and among the strangers was also his son, and he swore to punish them, and when he saw that his son was there and he did not want to punish him had he known it was him, he is permitted, and the rest are forbidden.
content.comments: 175 ה' — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "as the Lord, the God of Israel, lives — for I will inquire of my father," whereas the verse as cited (1Sam 20:12) reads: "the Lord God of Israel — when I have inquired of my father." 176 אֶת-יְרִיחוֹ — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "cursed be the man before the Lord who rises and builds Jericho," whereas the verse as cited (1Kgs 16:34) reads: "cursed be the man before the Lord who rises and builds this city — Jericho." (The reference is to 1Kgs 16:34, not 2Kgs 6:31 as printed.) 177 צְבָאוֹת — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "I have brought it forth, declares the Lord, and it shall enter the house of the thief," whereas the verse as cited (Zech 5:4) reads: "I have brought it forth, declares the Lord of hosts, and it shall enter the house of the thief." 178 לִקְרָאתִי--כִּי — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "as the Lord lives — if I leave to Nabal until morning light a single one that pisses against the wall," whereas the verse as cited (1Sam 25:34) reads: "as the Lord the God of Israel lives, who has restrained me from doing evil to you — for had you not hastened to come toward me…"

content.hebrew: נשלם ענין דין השבועה    בשם ה' אשר לו הישועה
content.english: The matter of the law of oaths is completed, in the name of the Lord, to whom is salvation.

content.hebrew: דין הנזיר
content.english: The Law of the Nazirite.

content.hebrew: אחרי שתורתנו הקדושה ישרת ההנהגה בלי תוספת וחסרון כאשר נאמר "תּוֹרַת ה' תְּמִימָה, מְשִׁיבַת נָפֶשׁ" (תהילים יט, ח) שהיא מרקחת תועיל לכל חליי הנפש הבאים מצד החומר במה שיסבול הגוף למצוא לה מנוח להשיג לתכליתה. על כן כשירצה האדם לחייב אסורים יותר ממה שאסרה התורה הוא על דרך פלא על כן החלה התורה פרשת הנזיר בלשון הפלאה באמור "אִישׁ אוֹ-אִשָּׁה{{fn:179}}, כִּי יַפְלִא לִנְדֹּר נֶדֶר נָזִיר" (במדבר ו, ב). אכן מפני היות מלת פלא שם משותף שימצא לשון הפרשה כגון "אֲשֶׁר יַפְלֶה ה', בֵּין מִצְרַיִם" (שמות יא, ז). וימצא ענין סתר כגון "נִפְלָאוֹת מִמֶּנִּי, וְלֹא אֵדָע" (איוב מב, ג) על כן פירשו המפרשים בו פירושים. מהם פירשוהו ענין סתירה והטעם ידור שיאמר עלי נדר ויסתיר איזה ענין נדר והוא יהיה נדר נזיר. ומהם פירשוהו לשון הפרשה והטעם בו מפני שמלת נדר כוללת סתם נדרי ערכים ונדר נזיר על כן כשיאמר עלי נדר יפריש לנדר נזירות והאמת הוא מה שפירשנו. ושם נזיר הוא שם של תורה כי כן נאמר "נֶדֶר נָזִיר--לְהַזִּיר, לַה'" (במדבר ו, ב) ויש לו חלק מן הלשון והחלק ההוא הוא לשון הפרשה מלשון "וְיִנָּזְרוּ מִקָּדְשֵׁי בְנֵי-יִשְׂרָאֵל" (ויקרא כב, ב) שהוא נבדל מתאות העולם. או שהרצון מלשון נזר הטעם יען שנפרש מתאות העולם כאלו כתר ונזר יש על ראשו כמו המלך שהוא נבדל מן ההמון בכתר אשר על ראשו כן הנזיר נבדל משאר העם ואפשר שהוא מלשון "גָּזִּי נִזְרֵךְ וְהַשְׁלִיכִי" (ירמיהו ז, כט) הטעם מה שנאמר "גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע, שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ" (במדבר ו, ה). וכל מקום שיזכיר שם נזיר אחרי שהוא שם של תורה רוצה על פי התנאים האלה הנזכרים בנזיר בזה הפרק שהם שלשה תנאים. האחד תגלחת השער והשני הטמאה במת והשלישי להנזר משתות היין. ועל כן באר החכם ר' יוסף נ"ע כי אלו התנאים אינם בשמשון אבל נקרא נזיר על צורה אחרת והוא תקון אחר תוריי כי מה שנתקיים בו איננו בנזיר מה שנזהרה אמו משתות היין ושלא תאכל טומאה רומז מה שיוצא מגפן היין ואשר נזכרים בנזיר אינם בו מפני כי מה שנאמר בו הוא התגלחת לעולם ודבר זה לא למדנו אותו מפרשה זו אלא הוא ענין בפני עצמו. ובעלי הקבלה אמרו ששני נזירים הם נזיר לזמן קצוב ונזיר לעולם ואולם הנזיר לעולם הוא ידוע מן הקבלה ויש הבדל בין נזיר לזמן קצוב ובין נזיר לעולם. והנזיר הנזכר הנה הוא נזיר לזמן קצוב מפני שאמר "וְהַיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים יפלו" (במדבר ו, יב). ועוד שאמר "וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת, הַנָּזִיר: בְּיוֹם, מְלֹאת יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ" (במדבר ו, יג) המחייב תכלית ימי הנדר אבל מה שאינו נזכר הנה הוא נזיר לעולם. ואמרו בעלי הקבלה יש הבדל בין נזיר לעולם ובין נזיר לזמן קצוב שהנזיר לזמן קצוב אסור לגלח כל ימי נזרו שנאמר "תַּעַר לֹא-יַעֲבֹר עַל-רֹאשׁוֹ" (במדבר ו, ה) אבל נזיר לעולם אם הכביד ראשו משערו מקל בתער מי"ב חדש לי"ב חדש ומביא קרבנותיו שלשה בהמות ונאמר באבשלום ויהי "מִקֵּץ יָמִים" (שמואל ב יד, כו) לימים ואבשלום נזיר עולם ונזיר עולם אם הוא נטמא הרי זה מביא קרבן טמאה ומגלח תגלחת טמאה כמו נזיר לזמן קצוב. אלא נזיר לעולם מותר ליטמא למתים ונזירות שמשון נזיר עולם היה והיה נזיר מן היין ומן התגלחת אלא לא היה מגלח לשנים עשר חדש כשאר נזירי עולם ולא היה נזהר ליטמא במתים. אע"פ כן יש מחכמינו ע"ה שאמרו כי נזיר עולם נזכר בפרשה זאת לאשר אמר "מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר" (במדבר ו, ג) ולא הורה שיש עד זמן קצוב. אכן החכם ר' יוסף נ"ע אמר כי באמרו "וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת, הַנָּזִיר" (במדבר ו, יג) רמיזה אל הנזכר בתחלה ואמר גם כן בתחלה עד מלאת ימי נזרו והנודר בנדרו להיות נזרו לעולם נדר בטל. אבל נזירות שמשון היתה מצוה לעתה והיה מותר ליטמא ולא לגלח שערו. אכן למדנו כי אין ראוי לנדור נדר נזירות זמן מועט מאשר אמר "גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע, שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ" (במדבר ו, ה) וזה לא יהיה לזמן מועט. ובעלי הקבלה אמרו אין פחות משלשים יום כמנין קדוש יהי"ה והלא גדול השער לא יהיה בחדש אחד וראוי להיות לפחות שנה ויש רמז מענין אבשלום. והנשים כשרות בזה הנדר באשר אמר "אִישׁ אוֹ-אִשָּׁה, כִּי יַפְלִא" וזאת היא שספרה בכשרות הנדר היא האלמנה והגרושה והיתומה ואשר שמע אביה ואישה החריש לה. ונדר נזירות אין ראוי לנדור בזמן הגלות מפני שיש עליו תנאים שצריכים אל המקדש מהקרבת הקרבן ונתינת השער תחת האש שמבשלים השלמים. ואחר שאמר הכתוב "וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת, הַנָּזִיר" אין הנזיר נזיר אלא עם תורתו. ושואלים החכמים אם נדר נדר נזירות עד זמן  ובתוך הזמן חרב המקדש ואין לו להקריב קרבן איך יהיה הדבר הישלים נדרו והלא התנאי בטל אם יבטל נדרו. ומשיב החכם בזה שעקר הנדר היה בכשרות ואם באה מניעה בבטול הקרבן נדרו אין בטל אכן אנשי הגלות עקר נדרם אינו בכשרות. ובעלי הקבלה אמרו נזירות נוהג בפני הבית ולאחר הבית ואם נדר בנזירות בזמן הזה הרי זה נזיר עולם שאין לנו בית המקדש להקריב קרבנותיו במלאת ימי נזרו ואין נזירות נוהגת בארץ ישראל. ומי שהיה נדר בחוצה לארץ היו כופין אותו לעלות לארץ ישראל והיה נוהג בנזירות שם עד שימות או עד שיבנה המקדש ויקריב קרבנותיו במלאת ימי נזרו ובכל זמן שהוא מחוצה לארץ אסור לשתות יין ולהטמא למתים ולגלח וכל דקדוקי נזירות עליו. והחל הכתוב לבאר תנאי הנזיר באמרו "מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר" ושם יין כולל החדש והישן אך בהתחברו עם שכר יהיה מוסגל על החדש. ויש אומרים כי מלת שכר יהיה כולל המשקה העשוי מדברים אחרים והאמת שהוא מוסגל למה שיעשה מגפן היין. ואמר "חֹמֶץ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ שֵׁכָר" (במדבר ו, ג) הנעשה משניהם ואמר "וְכָל-מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה" (במדבר ו, ג) הוא מה שיזרמו ענבים. ואחרים אמרו יין המבושל ויעשה מתוק הנקרא איפשימא. ויתכן לפרש כי רצה לאסור כל דבר השרוי ביין אך יש טענה כי למה אמר "מִשְׁרַת עֲנָבִים" ועוד שאמר "לֹא יִשְׁתֶּה". ואמר "וַעֲנָבִים לַחִים וִיבֵשִׁים לֹא יֹאכֵל" (במדבר ו, ג) ובאמרו "וִיבֵשִׁים" הטעם בו הצמוקים ואמר "מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מִגֶּפֶן הַיַּיִן" (במדבר ו, ד) בזה כולל הבוסר העלים והשבטים הלחים. ויש אומרים כי זה כולל היין החדש המבושל. ואמר "מֵחַרְצַנִּים וְעַד-זָג" (במדבר ו, ד) חרצנים הם קליפת הענבים וזג בפנים ואחרים אומרים ההפך כי החרצנים הם הפנימיים וזג מה שבחוץ דמיון מזגי הבהמה שקוראים החיצון זג והפנימי ענבל. ואסור לאכול תערובת היין. ובעלי הקבלה נתנו שעורים מה שראוי לאכילה כזית מה לשתיה כרביעית והאמת בכל שהוא. והחל תנאי שני באמור "תַּעַר לֹא-יַעֲבֹר עַל-רֹאשׁוֹ" (במדבר ו, ה) והוא הדין לכל דבר העובר בראשו ואפילו דברים שמשרין השער באסור ואמר "קָדֹשׁ יִהְיֶה--גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע, שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ" (במדבר ו, ה) לשון גדל הטעם בו לגדל השער וזה יורה שלא ידור לזמן מועט. ויש מפרשים מלשון גדילים. ואמר בו תנאי שלישי באמור "כָּל-יְמֵי הַזִּירוֹ, לַה', עַל-נֶפֶשׁ מֵת, לֹא יָבֹא" (במדבר ו, ו) ואפילו מה שהתיר לכהן משנה אסרם לנזיר אבל הוא כמו כהן גדול באמור "לְאָבִיו וּלְאִמּוֹ … לֹא-יִטַּמָּא" (במדבר ו, ז). ולא הזכיר הבן והבת מפני שהנודרים נדר נזירות הם בחורים כמו שנאמר "וָאָקִים מִבְּנֵיכֶם לִנְבִיאִים, וּמִבַּחוּרֵיכֶם לִנְזִרִים" (עמוס ב, יא) וזה מבטל מה שאמרו אין בכלל רק מה שבפרט ויהיה קדוש שלא יטמא במתים. ואמר "וְכִי-יָמוּת מֵת עָלָיו בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאֹם" (במדבר ו, ט) וזה מוסגל במת אדם לא במת זולתו ובאמרו "בְּפֶתַע פִּתְאֹם" שהוא בלתי ידיעה. ואמר "וְהַיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים יִפְּלוּ{{fn:180}}" (במדבר ו, יב) כיון שנגע במת בין בקצות המת. וטמאת הנזיר מן המת בין בנגיעה בין בנשיאה בין באהילה על כלם מגלח וסותר הראשונים ומתחייב בקרבן שלש בהמות. ואין להקיש בטמאת מת אדם שאר טמאות ודבר זה למד מן האשה שהיא אינה נצולת מן הנדות בידוע. ובעלי הקבלה אמרו הנזיר מתטמא למת מצוה ומתגלח בתגלחת מצוה אבל ביין מצוה אסור באיזה מצד כגון הנשבע לשתות יין ביום ונדר נדר נזיר חלה נזירות על השבועה וחכמינו ע"ה לא הכשירו בכל זה. חכמינו ע"ה אמרו נזיר שחלה וצריך לשתות יין או לגלח שערו כדי שירפא ואם לא ימות אמרו ימות ולא יעבור והאמת כי לא ידור הנודר אלא עם שלום גופו מן המות ואע"פ כן שלא יתנה התנאי בפיו הוא בכח הנדר שזה דבר שהדעת מסכמת בו:
content.english: After our holy Torah is right in its guidance without addition and diminution, as it says, "The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul" (Ps 19:8), which is a compound that benefits all the diseases of the soul that come from the side of matter, in what the body will endure to find rest for it to achieve its purpose. Therefore, when a person wants to obligate prohibitions more than what the Torah prohibited, it is by way of wonder, therefore the Torah began the section of the Nazirite with the language of making a special vow, saying, "When either a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the Lord" (Num 6:2). However, because the word "special" is a shared name that is found in the language of separation, such as "that the Lord will make a distinction between Egypt" (Exod 11:7), and it is found in the matter of secrecy, such as "Things too wonderful for me, which I do not know" (Job 42:3), therefore the interpreters interpreted it with interpretations. Some interpreted it as a matter of secrecy, and the meaning is he will vow, saying, "Upon me a vow," and will hide what kind of vow, and it will be a vow of a Nazirite. And some interpreted it as a language of separation, and the meaning is because the term "vow" generally includes vows of valuation and vows of a Nazirite, therefore when he says, "Upon me a vow," he separates for a vow of Naziriteship, and the truth is what we have interpreted. And the name "Nazirite" is a term of the Torah, for so it says, "the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the Lord" (Num 6:2), and it has a part from the language, and that part is the language of separation, from the language of "And they shall separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel" (Lev 22:2), that he is separated from the desires of the world. Or that the intention is from the language of crown, the meaning is since he separates from the desires of the world, it is as if a crown and diadem is on his head, like the king who is separated from the masses by the crown that is on his head, so the Nazirite is separated from the rest of the people, and it is possible that it is from the language of "Cut off your hair and cast it away" (Jer 7:29), the meaning being what is said, "He shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow" (Num 6:5). And every place where the name "Nazirite" is mentioned, after it is a term of the Torah, it refers to the conditions mentioned for the Nazirite in this chapter, which are three conditions. The first is the shaving of the hair, and the second is defilement by a corpse, and the third is to abstain from drinking wine. And therefore, the sage Rabbi Joseph, may he rest in peace, explained that these conditions were not for Samson, but he was called a Nazirite in another way, and it is another ordinance of the Torah, for what was fulfilled in him is not in a Nazirite, what his mother was careful not to drink wine and not to eat uncleanness, hinting at what comes from the vine and what is mentioned regarding a Nazirite, they are not for him, because what was said about him is shaving forever, and this thing we did not learn from this section, but it is a matter in itself. And the Rabbanites said that there are two Nazirites: a Nazirite for a fixed time and a Nazirite forever, and the Nazirite forever is known from the tradition, and there is a difference between a Nazirite for a fixed time and a Nazirite forever. And the Nazirite mentioned here is a Nazirite for a fixed time because it says, "And the days that were before shall fall away" (Num 6:12). And furthermore, it says, "And this is the law of the Nazirite: on the day when the days of his separation are fulfilled" (Num 6:13), requiring the completion of the days of the vow, but what is not mentioned here is a Nazirite forever. And the Rabbanites said there is a difference between a Nazirite forever and a Nazirite for a fixed time, that the Nazirite for a fixed time is forbidden to shave all the days of his Naziriteship, as it says, "No razor shall come upon his head" (Num 6:5), but a Nazirite forever, if his head becomes heavy from his hair, may lighten it with a razor from twelve months to twelve months and bring his three animal sacrifices, and it says regarding Absalom, "And it came to pass at the end of the days" (2Sam 14:26), to the days, and Absalom was a Nazirite forever, and a Nazirite forever, if he is defiled, brings a sacrifice of defilement and shaves the shaving of defilement like a Nazirite for a fixed time, except that a Nazirite forever is permitted to be defiled by corpses, and the Naziriteship of Samson was a Nazirite forever, and he was a Nazirite from wine and from shaving, except that he did not shave for twelve months like other Nazirites forever, and he was not careful not to be defiled by corpses. Nevertheless, there are some of our sages, may they rest in peace, who said that a Nazirite forever is mentioned in this section in saying, "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink" (Num 6:3), and it did not indicate that it is until a fixed time. However, the sage Rabbi Joseph, may he rest in peace, said that in saying, "And this is the law of the Nazirite" (Num 6:13), there is a hint to what was mentioned at the beginning, and it also said at the beginning until the completion of the days of his Naziriteship, and one who vows in his vow to have his Naziriteship forever, his vow is void. But the Naziriteship of Samson was a commandment for the occasion, and he was permitted to be defiled and not to shave his hair. However, we learn that it is not proper to vow a vow of Naziriteship for a short time from what is said, "He shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow" (Num 6:5), and this will not be for a short time. And the Rabbanites said it is not less than thirty days, like the number of "he shall be holy" (yihyeh kadosh), and indeed, the hair does not grow in one month, and it should be at least a year, and there is a hint from the matter of Absalom. And women are valid for this vow, as it says, "When either a man or a woman makes a special vow," and this is one who is recorded as valid for the vow: the widow and the divorced woman and the orphan and the one whose father and husband heard her and kept silent to her. And a vow of Naziriteship is not proper to vow in the time of exile because it has conditions that require the Temple, for the bringing of the sacrifice and the giving of the hair under the fire that cooks the peace offerings. And after the Scripture said, "And this is the law of the Nazirite," the Nazirite is not a Nazirite except with his law. And the sages ask if one vowed a vow of Naziriteship until a certain time, and within that time the Temple was destroyed, and he has no way to bring a sacrifice, what should be done? Will he complete his vow, and behold, the condition is void? If he voids his vow? And the sage answers this, that the essence of the vow was valid, and if a prevention came with the voiding of the sacrifice, his vow is not void, but the people of the exile, the essence of their vow is not valid. And the Rabbanites said Naziriteship is practiced in the presence of the Temple and after the Temple, and if one vowed in Naziriteship in this time, behold, he is a Nazirite forever because we have no Temple to bring his sacrifices at the completion of the days of his Naziriteship, and Naziriteship is not practiced in the land of Israel. And one who vowed outside the land, they would force him to go up to the land of Israel, and he would practice Naziriteship there until he dies or until the Temple is built, and he brings his sacrifices at the completion of the days of his Naziriteship, and at all times that he is outside the land, he is forbidden to drink wine and to be defiled by corpses and to shave, and all the details of Naziriteship are upon him. And the Scripture began to explain the conditions of the Nazirite, saying, "He shall abstain from wine and strong drink," and the term "wine" includes the new and the old, but when it is combined with "strong drink," it is specialized for the new. And there are those who say that the term "strong drink" would include a drink made from other things, and the truth is that it is specialized for what is made from the vine. And it says, "Vinegar of wine and vinegar of strong drink" (Num 6:3), which is made from both of them, and it says, "And any juice of grapes shall he not drink" (Num 6:3), which is what they squeeze from grapes. And others say boiled wine that is made sweet, called epsima. And it is possible to interpret that he wanted to forbid anything soaked in wine, but there is an argument, for why did it say, "juice of grapes," and furthermore, it says, "he shall not drink." And it says, "Grapes moist or dried he shall not eat" (Num 6:3), and in saying "dried," the meaning is raisins, and it says, "From all that is made from the grapevine" (Num 6:4), with this it includes the unripe grapes, the leaves, and the moist branches. And there are those who say that this includes new wine that is boiled. And it says, "From the seeds to the skin" (Num 6:4); the seeds are the peels of the grapes, and the skin is on the inside, and others say the opposite, that the seeds are the inner ones, and the skin is what is outside, similar to the uvula of the animal where they call the outer skin and the inner bell. And it is forbidden to eat a mixture of wine. And the Rabbanites gave measurements: what is proper for eating, an olive's worth; for drinking, a quarter. And the truth is in any amount. And it began the second condition, saying, "No razor shall come upon his head" (Num 6:5), and that is the law for anything that passes on his head, and even things that cause the hair to fall, is forbidden, and it says, "He shall be holy, let the hair of his head grow" (Num 6:5), the term "let grow" means to grow the hair, and this indicates that he should not vow for a short time. And there are interpreters from the language of tassels. And it said in it a third condition, saying, "All the days of his separation to the Lord, he shall not come near a dead body" (Num 6:6), and even what is permitted to a priest it forbids to a Nazirite, but he is like a high priest, saying, "For his father or his mother ... he shall not defile himself" (Num 6:7). And it did not mention the son and daughter because those who vow a vow of Naziriteship are young men, as it says, "And I raised up from your young men Nazirites" (Amos 2:11), and this nullifies what they said, "There is in the general only what is in the particular," and he will be holy in that he will not be defiled by corpses. And it says, "And if anyone dies very suddenly beside him" (Num 6:9), and this is specialized for a human corpse, not for anything else, and in saying "very suddenly," it is without knowledge. And it says, "And the days that were before shall fall away" (Num 6:12), since he touched a corpse, whether at the extremities of the corpse. And the defilement of the Nazirite by the corpse, whether by touching or by carrying or by overshadowing, for all of them he shaves and nullifies the earlier days and is obligated to bring three animals. And one cannot compare other defilements to the defilement of a human corpse, and this thing is learned from the woman, who is not saved from menstruation, as is known. And the Rabbanites said the Nazirite is defiled for a dead person as a religious duty and shaves in the shaving as a religious duty, but he is forbidden the wine as a religious duty in any way, such as one who swears to drink wine on a day and vowed a vow of Naziriteship, the Naziriteship takes effect on the oath, and our sages, may they rest in peace, did not approve of all this. Our sages, may they rest in peace, said a Nazirite who became ill and needs to drink wine or to shave his hair so that he will be healed, and if not, he will die, they said he should die and not transgress, and the truth is that one who vows does not vow except with the health of his body from death, and even though he does not stipulate the condition with his mouth, it is in the power of the vow, for this is something that reason agrees with.
content.comments: 179 אוֹ-אִשָּׁה — In *Gan Eden* it is written: "a man when he sets himself apart to make a Nazirite vow," whereas the verse as cited (Num 6:2) reads: "a man or a woman who sets himself apart to make a Nazirite vow." 180 יִפְּלוּ — In *Gan Eden* it is written, in error: "the former days shall be invalid," whereas the verse as cited (Num 6:12) reads: "and the former days shall fall away."

content.hebrew: יש שואלים שהכתוב אמר "גַּדֵּל פֶּרַע, שְׂעַר רֹאשׁוֹ" ואם יהיה קרח איך יהיה הענין אומרים שאין ראוי שידור נדר נזירות ואם מאחר שנדר יהיה חולי לו שלא יגדל שער. אומרים שאין ראוי שיפול נדר נזירות משתיית היין ומניעת הטמאה ודנו החכמים שאם צורת הנודר שיהיה על צד רפואה להמנע משתיית היין ומן גלוח השער נדר נזירות יכשר:
content.english: There are those who ask, since the Scripture said, "Let the hair of his head grow" (Num 6:5), and if he is bald, how will it be? They say it is not proper for him to vow a vow of Naziriteship, and if after he vowed, there would be an illness for him so that his hair would not grow. They say that a vow of Naziriteship should not fall regarding the drinking of wine and the prevention of defilement, and the sages judged that if the form of the one who vows would be by way of medicine to abstain from drinking wine and from shaving the hair, a vow of Naziriteship would be proper.

content.hebrew: נזיר שחלה עליו צרעת ויש לו מצוה לגלח איך יהיה הענין אמר רבינו יוסף כי חוב להקיש גלוח המצורע שהוא נזיר על טמאת מת ממה שאמר "וְהַיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים יִפְּלוּ" ויתחייב לגלח השער. ואמר שדבר זה מסופק כי יש מי שיגביר כתוב הנזיר עד שישלים נדרו ויתגלח ויש מי שיגביר כתוב המצורע ויתגלח. יש לשאול מה שיפול על דרך שגגה וטמא ראש נזרו היתחייב בקרבן הכתוב בו או יתחייב לו גם כן הקרבן הכתוב בפרשת ויקרא שהיא חטאת קבועה. והחכם ר' יוסף נ"ע חייבו גם אותו הקרבן. אבל בעלי הקבלה לא חייבו לו כי אם זה הקרבן לפי דעתם שאין מחייבים חטאת קבועה אלא לחייבי כריתות ואם הוא מזיד לוקה ומתחייב שיפלו הימים הראשונים. אך בענין הקרבן החכם רבינו יוסף נ"ע אומר מדרך סדור לחייבו מפני כי הנראה מגלוי הכתוב שלא חייב זה הקרבן אלא למי שאינו מזיד. ומי שנגע במת בימי נדרו ונעלם ממנו והשלים תנאי נדרו ואחרי כן נודע לו חייבו לו החכמים לשנות ענין הנדר והבאת הקרבן שנתחייב מפני הטמאה. ואם בא אל הקדש מתחייב בקרבן עולה ויורד והכתוב חייב לו אם יטמא במת לגלח שערו ביום טהרתו ויביא קרבן שתי תורים אחד לעולה ואחד לחטאת. אבל הכבש הנזכר פירשו החכמים יתחייב להביאו אחרי שישלים נדרו בעבור שאמר "וְהִזִּיר לַה' אֶת-יְמֵי נִזְרוֹ" (במדבר ו, יב). ולא יכשר עליו כיון שנגע במת בפתע פתאום שיגע במת במזיד ושלא ישתה יין אחר שנפסל נדרו כי זה בא לו על דרך הכרח. ואולם איך יהיה הדין אם שתה יין או גלח שערו בתוך נדרו בשגגה אם יתחייב עליו כמו שנתחייב על נגיעת המת הכתוב לא הורה בזה אך החכמים הקישו מפני שאומרים ששלשה תנאים הם שלא ישתה יין ושלא יגלח ושלא יטמא במת. וכיון שדן הכתוב על מי שנטמא במת בשוגג הוא הדין להתחייב על שתיית היין ועל גלוח השער. ואמרו "וְהַיָּמִים הָרִאשֹׁנִים יִפְּלוּ" לפחות שנים אבל אם עבר יום אחד לא יתחייב על מה שסדר הכתוב. ואם שלם זמן קרבנו ועדיין אינו מביא אסור לו באלו השלשה התנאים עד שיביא קרבנו ומצוה עליו לגלח לתת שערו באש תחת זבח השלמים שנאמר "וְגִלַּח הַנָּזִיר, פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד" (במדבר ו, יח) ולשתות גם יין ממה שאמר "וְאַחַר יִשְׁתֶּה הַנָּזִיר, יָיִן" (במדבר ו, כ). ומה שיתחייב על הנזיר אחר שישלים נדרו מפורש בפרק וזאת תורת הנזיר. ואלו היה כפי דעת בעלי הקבלה אשר אמרו כי מאמר "מֵאֲשֶׁר{{fn:181}} חָטָא עַל-הַנָּפֶשׁ" (במדבר ו, יא) על שצער נפשו מן היין לא היה ראוי לחייבו לחזור על מה שחטא. ואמנם בהשלימו נדרו מלבד אשר נזכר יש לו להתנדב  כאשר אמר "מִלְּבַד אֲשֶׁר-תַּשִּׂיג יָדוֹ; כְּפִי נִדְרוֹ, אֲשֶׁר יִדֹּר--כֵּן יַעֲשֶׂה, עַל תּוֹרַת נִזְרוֹ" (במדבר ו, כא). הדעת בו שידור להוציא נדרו בשלום שלא יארע לו שום מכשול:
content.english: If a Nazirite is afflicted with leprosy, and he has a commandment to shave, how will the matter be? Rabbi Joseph said that it is obligatory to compare the shaving of the leper who is a Nazirite to the defilement of a corpse, from what it says, "And the days that were before shall fall away" (Num 6:12), and he will be obligated to shave the hair. And he said that this matter is doubtful, for there is one who would strengthen the verse of the Nazirite until he completes his vow and shaves, and there is one who would strengthen the verse of the leper and would shave.
